chapters.title: Chapter 351: Eternal Bond [2]
paragraphs: His other special, shared ability also evolved. Previously, it was called Soul-Binding Symbiosis, and now it was called Eternal Bond. Perhaps it represented the depth of their connection now: the fact that they were no longer people bound by circumstances, but two souls that had chosen each other for eternity.
’I really like it. Both the name and its effects.’

First, its existing passive effects were strengthened, and there were a few additions. Ethea’s chronic pain would completely disappear when they were together, their mana/mental power regeneration would triple, and the same went for their cultivation speed. Their overall strength, speed, defense, and more also increased threefold. On top of that, they could now sense each other’s location and condition at all times, and transfer mana and mental power with each other at will.

Synchronicity had also changed. It no longer had to trigger by chance. They could now activate it once per day, entering a state of perfect alignment for a short period. During that time, their cultivation speed, regeneration, and learning speed all increased dramatically. Soren couldn’t help but chuckle when he read that part. They finally had a way to use the effect that had been sitting dormant for so long.

As for Symbiotic Equilibrium, it had strengthened significantly. They could now access each other’s abilities at will, without needing to transfer them back and forth. The limitation was that it only worked on lower-rank abilities for now. Fundamental and high-ranking abilities, like Soren’s constitution or Core Refinement, and Ethea’s curse and abilities, still couldn’t be shared. But everything else was fair game.
Then came the first new addition, the one that made Soren pause for a long moment.

It was a shared mental space. A private realm that existed only for the two of them, constructed from their combined consciousness. They could meet there whenever they wanted, no matter how far apart they were in the physical world. Time inside moved differently. Two days in the realm equaled just one in reality. They could talk freely, share memories, or simply spend time together without anyone else knowing.
They could also train there.

Soren’s eyes lit up at that part because they could spar, practice techniques, and learn from each other without risking physical injury or exhausting their bodies. It was a place where they could grow stronger together, away from the dangers of the real world.
’...This is amazing.’
He couldn’t wait to try it.
’And the last effect is... Eternal Vow.’
Soren fell silent as he recalled the contents and capabilities of the effect.
’...I think... It’s better not to tell Ethea about this...’
He shook his head and moved on to the next return.

Advanced Appraisal had evolved into Eyes of Truth, and this one came with a massive upgrade. He no longer had to activate it repeatedly. One use was enough. Once he appraised someone, the status window would remain open and update in real time, reflecting any changes in their condition, abilities, or mental state as they happened. The only limitation was that it lasted for a single day before expiring. Still, that was a massive improvement over what he had before.

Beyond that, as the new name suggested, he could now see the truth, though he wasn’t sure exactly how that worked yet. The information about it had been vague, mentioning something about piercing through deception and revealing hidden things. So, he would have to test it himself before reaching a conclusion.
He glanced down at Ethea, who was still asleep against his chest.
’...Should I try it on her first?’
He hesitated for a moment, then activated the ability.
Name: Ethea Everly
Status: Stable (Recovering / Critical)
[Rank: 7th Circle [Crippled / Regressed]]
[Mental Cultivation: Stellar Soul Weaver Sutra — Stage 2: Soul Tempered Core Stage]
[Current Mana Level: 0 (Sealed)]
[Current Mental Power: 86547 / 150000]
[Core condition: 70% destroyed...]
[Mana pathways: 40% functional...]
[Physical Condition:]
- Paralysis
- Chronic Pain (Level 0/10)
[Authority Status: Frost Sovereign - Sealed/Dormant]
[Affliction Detected:]
[Curse: Eclipse’s Corrosion - Grade: Eighth Circle]
[Details: ???]
[Effect: ???]
[Origin: ???]
[Estimated Survival Without Treatment: 10 months]
[Abilities: Unshackled Soul (S-Rank), Sovereign Swordsmanship (SS-Rank), ? (SSS-Rank), Absolute Zero (Sealed)]
[Affinities: Ice (Grade EX), , Darkness (?)]
[Hidden Talent / Traits: Stellar Soul, Heart of Winter, Unyielding Will, Sovereign’s Bloodline, Fated One, Perfect Recall]
[Mental State: Sleeping, Happy]
[Investment Value: MYTHIC]
[Potential: Immeasurable]
’W-Whoa!’ Soren’s eyes widened as he read through the numbers.

Just yesterday, her core condition had been at 77% destroyed and her mana pathways at 31% functional. Today, the core was at 70% and the pathways at 40%. That was a massive jump. Under normal circumstances, which included her eating medicine, magic meals, and elixirs, it would have taken about a month to see this much improvement.
He fell silent, staring at the numbers as his mind raced. The integration shouldn’t have affected her, right? So why had her condition improved so suddenly?
’...Could it be... because of Eternal Bond?’

Since it was a shared ability, it affected them both, so it would make sense if she recovered this much. Furthermore, her mental power had increased significantly as well, jumping from approximately sixty-five thousand to over eighty-five thousand, which was another big leap. The chronic pain was at level zero, as he had expected. But then something else caught his eye.
’Absolute Zero... that must be the domain ability she talked about. And... Huh? Her ice affinity is... EX grade?’
He paused, blinking a few times to check if he was seeing right. He had seen S-rank, SS-rank, even SSS-rank affinities before. But EX? He had never encountered that grade. What did it even mean?
’...I need to look into this later and tell Ethea about it...’ His thoughts trailed off as he saw her third affinity being revealed as darkness with a question mark. ’...About everything.’

’...Oh!’ His eyes lit up as he finally saw her hidden talents and traits listed at the bottom of the window. He could only see the names for now, not the descriptions, but even the names gave him an idea of what they might be. ’However...’

chapters.title: Chapter 352: Eternal Bond [3]
paragraphs: ’However, she’s incredible as I imagined her to be. No... She is even more incredible than I thought.’ Soren chuckled to himself and made a mental note to talk about these later too. She probably knew about some of them already, but maybe not all. ’...Especially the Fated One.’
With many theories already forming in his mind, he closed the window, and his thoughts drifted back to the Eyes of Truth. He had used it on Ethea, but nothing resembling ’truth’ appeared.
’...Was there no truth to reveal? Or... did I miss it? Or... used it incorrectly?’

He frowned, thinking it over. Maybe the truth only appeared when there was something to reveal. Or maybe he needed to concentrate harder. Either way, he would figure it out eventually. For now, he had more important things to focus on.
He glanced down at Ethea, who was still sleeping peacefully.
’...Let’s make this morning unforgettable as well.’

Ethea drifted through a sea of stillness, floating freely among burning constellations like a newborn star. Consciousness returned in slow waves, carrying her awareness across a luminous void that resembled a vast galaxy. The soothing warmth surrounding her felt completely foreign to her body, washing away the bitter cold that usually eroded her bones. Time lost all meaning in this expanse, leaving her content to exist within the serene flow of the cosmos.
After an unknown amount of time, a distant sound reached her from somewhere beyond the stars.
The voice kept echoing, growing clearer with every pulse.
"Ethea..."
’...Soren?’

The familiar voice and name anchored her wandering thoughts and gradually drew her back toward reality. The celestial realm faded, replaced by the physical sensation of silk sheets and a hand on top of her forehead.
"...Good morning, my love~"
"..." Ethea’s lips curled up on their own. "Good morning, my love."
Soren’s leaned down and pressed a soft kiss to her forehead. "Did you sleep well?"
"...Mm." She nodded slightly, still blinking away the last traces of the stars. "I dreamed of something. I was like a star, flying freely across the whole universe."
"That sounds amazing." Soren smiled, a hint of wistfulness in his eyes. "Unfortunately, I didn’t have any dreams. I was hoping to see us together. Hah..."
"Pfft!" Ethea giggled at his words and paused. "...Actually, I dream about us often. I even saw us... happily living in our own house with... our bonded partners."
Soren blinked, caught off guard. "You do?"
"Mm..." Ethea nodded with a bashful face, a little bit embarrassed and guilty about leaving out the rest. ’...I can’t talk about children yet or how the dream ended...’
"That’s amazing, I wish I could... Wait! I thought of something cool!" Soren’s smile widened. "Let’s watch it together later."
"Huh?" Ethea raised a brow in confusion.
"I’ll explain it to you later," Soren said with his signature mysterious smile. "We have a lot to talk about."
"Oh, ok." Ethea didn’t pry any further, realizing it might be something important and secretive.
"Anyway, let’s get you up and ready for the day."
Ethea nodded, and Soren helped her sit up, then lifted her into his arms. As he carried her toward the bathroom, she suddenly froze.
’W-Wait...’
’What is it?’
’The pain...’ She looked at him, her expression a mix of confusion and wonder. ’It’s gone. I... I don’t feel it anymore.’
Soren just smiled, saying nothing.
Ethea stared at him, puzzled. ’How did you do it?’
’...Later,’ he said softly.

She wanted to press further, but the look on his face told her to wait. So she nodded and let him carry her into the bathroom. He helped her wash up, then brought her back to the bedroom and laid her down while he picked out fresh clothes for them both. Once they were dressed, he put her in her wheelchair and wheeled it to the table where breakfast was already waiting.
They ate it together while feeding each other like yesterday. Surprisingly, Ethea told him she could use her hands freely now, and there was no need to use her mental power to aid.
Soren was relieved and told her she would be able to move her whole body soon.

They spent the rest of breakfast talking about what to do today, when to go to the academy, and so on. Afterward, Soren cleaned up the dishes and put everything away. Then he walked back to Ethea and sat down beside her.
"Ethea, I have something I want to give you."
Ethea tilted her head slightly.

"Actually, I wanted to give it to you yesterday, but we both ended up falling asleep," Soren explained as he raised his palm, revealing a small wooden box. "Ethea... I know I’m not usually good with words or expressing what I truly feel, but I hope what I’m about to say conveys everything my heart holds for you... Thinking about our past and the time we’ve spent together has made me realize one simple truth: I want every step of my future to be alongside yours. I want us to build a life together, standing side by side through every hardship and every joy, as partners for all eternity."

He pressed the side of the wooden case, and the small box popped open to reveal a pair of silver rings. Their polished surfaces caught the sunlight, each band bearing a unique pattern that fit seamlessly into the other.
"I love you, Ethea." Soren met her stunned gaze, his expression filled with an unwavering devotion. "Will you share forever with me?"
"...Yes." Ethea nodded, raising her hand. "You gave me a life I thought was lost to me. Sharing forever with you is the only promise I ever want to keep."

Soren’s smile widened, and he carefully lifted the slightly smaller band from the velvet lining. Holding her delicate fingers, he guided the silver ring onto her left hand, letting it settle perfectly into place.

He then handed the open wooden case to Ethea. She reached into the box and gently picked up the other ring. Soren extended his left hand, allowing her to slide the matching silver band onto his finger.
"Now, you are mine, and I am yours forever."

chapters.title: Chapter 353: Spirit Puppet [2]
paragraphs: Soren felt his heart swell until it filled every corner of his chest. It was like standing at the edge of a vast ocean, watching the waves roll in, knowing he could dive in and never reach the bottom. He had already given her his heart, had already let himself fall for her completely, or so he had assumed. But in this moment, holding her hand with the ring on her finger, he felt himself falling again, deeper than before, and the fall was sweeter than anything he had ever known.
They stared at each other and slowly parted their lips.
Soren chuckled softly, resting his forehead against hers. "Actually, there’s something else I wanted to give you."
He reluctantly backed away and took out something from his inventory and held it out to her. "This is for you."
Ethea raised a brow, eyeing the object. "What is this, dear?"
"It is a spirit puppet," Soren explained. "It matches its owner’s cultivation level and has a few useful abilities. It can even change its appearance based on your imagination."
Ethea’s eyes lit up as she stared at the puppet with sudden curiosity. "How do I change it?"
"Just focus on what you want it to look like. The puppet will do the rest."

Ethea nodded and closed her eyes, focusing her mind on the puppet in her hands. A moment later, when her eyelids fluttered open, the puppet had already transformed into a plush mini plushie of Soren: complete with messy brown hair, big warm brown eyes, a polite little smile, and a tiny black suit with a tie.
Soren fell silent at the sight of his own miniature self, dressed up like a little gentleman and staring back at him with those big, round eyes. He didn’t know whether to laugh or feel embarrassed.
"...That’s not... what you think of me, right?" he finally asked.
"Mm." Ethea nodded, her lips curling into a satisfied smile. "Cute, right?"
"I... I’m not sure I’d use that word for myself.
"Then what word would you use?"
Soren looked at the plushie again. Then at her. Then back at the plushie. "...I have no idea."
Ethea laughed and hugged the plushie to her chest. "I love it. Thank you, dear."
"...Well, I’m glad you liked it at least." He paused and added. "Do you wanna know what else it can do?"
Ethea nodded enthusiastically.

"First, it naturally synchronizes with its master’s cultivation, mirroring their realm without any extra effort," Soren explained, pointing to the tiny plushie in her hands. "And it constantly absorbs ambient mana from the surrounding environment on its own, so there is no need to worry about manually recharging it unless necessary. Beyond that, it possesses autonomous combat capabilities, allowing it to fight alongside its master or defend them independently in times of danger. Lastly, spells can be stored directly inside it, granting the ability to cast them remotely through the puppet whenever desired."
"It’s pretty good for a spirit puppet," Ethea muttered in surprise. "But can it reach 7th circle or higher too?"
"That... I don’t know." Soren rubbed the back of his neck awkwardly. "Though if I had to guess, it’s probably not that powerful."
"...We can find out about it once you get stronger and reach those stages," Ethea suggested a solution, and Soren nodded in agreement.

While she continued admiring the tiny plushie, he sent the remaining details directly into her mind: ’It can also create a temporary clone of itself. Though weaker, it can still fight. And if things ever turn dire, it can self-destruct to release a powerful burst of energy against surrounding foes. The puppet or its clone will be destroyed, but it can be rebuilt with time and materials. Furthermore, concentrating on the puppet allows its owner to see and hear through its senses, which makes it ideal for scouting or guarding.’
’...It’s a lot more advanced than I thought.’ Ethea looked up from the miniature figure, genuine impression warming her gaze as she smoothed her thumb over its tiny shoulder.

Soren smiled, sending one final thought through their connection. ’One last thing: it can record and store whatever information it sees and hears. The owner can review those recorded details whenever needed.’
’That’s... so cool!’ Ethea’s eyes lit up. ’It’s like a personal scout and assistant all in one.’
’...Haha, now that you said it, it really is like a miniature butler and knight rolled into one.’ Soren laughed, shaking his head.
He glanced toward the window, checking the sky’s position. "Speaking of our schedule, when is the meeting set to start?
"In about two hours," Ethea replied, cradling the tiny plushie carefully in her lap.
Soren checked his wristwatch to confirm, tapping the glass face. "That gives us a good hour and a half to spare. Let’s take a rest before we head over."
He gently nudged her shoulders, guiding her into a comfortable position. "Lean back and close your eyes. I will wake you when it is time."
"Alright, you take a rest too," Ethea replied and closed her eyes.
Soren rested his arms on the table and lowered his head, staring at her peaceful face with a soft smile before finally letting his eyelids slip shut.
’Malakor, you know what to do.’
’...Yes, master.’
’Good...’

When Soren opened his eyes again, he found himself standing in an endless grassland, a warm breeze rustling the green blades around him. He closed his eyes again, reaching out into the expanse to find a familiar presence and carefully guiding it to his side.
A few seconds later, he opened his eyes and found Ethea, standing before him on her own two feet, bathed in the soft light of the open field.
"...Dear, open your eyes."

"...?" Ethea’s eyelids fluttered open a moment later, revealing her ice-blue eyes as she blinked at the sweeping field around them. Her gaze landed on Soren first, then drifted to the endless green stretch reaching toward the horizon, confusion washing over her expression.

Before she could process the sudden change of scenery, a far sharper realization struck her. The ground felt solid beneath her soles. Weight rested firmly on her legs, balance shifting naturally with every small breath.
Her breath hitched as her gaze dropped to her feet, perfectly planted in the grass.
"Is this... a dream?"

Ethea’s eyes lit up as she stared at the puppet with sudden curiosity.
"How do I change it?"
"Just focus on what you want it to look like.
The puppet will do the rest."
Ethea nodded and closed her eyes, focusing her mind on the puppet in her hands.

A moment later, when her eyelids fluttered open, the puppet had already transformed into a plush mini plushie of Soren: complete with messy brown hair, big warm brown eyes, a polite little smile, and a tiny black suit with a tie.
Soren fell silent at the sight of his own miniature self, dressed up like a little gentleman and staring back at him with those big, round eyes.
He didn’t know whether to laugh or feel embarrassed.
"...That’s not... what you think of me, right?" he finally asked.
"Mm." Ethea nodded, her lips curling into a satisfied smile.
"Cute, right?"
I’m not sure I’d use that word for myself.
"Then what word would you use?"
Soren looked at the plushie again.
Then at her.
Then back at the plushie.
"...I have no idea."
Ethea laughed and hugged the plushie to her chest.
"I love it.
Thank you, dear."
"...Well, I’m glad you liked it at least." He paused and added.
"Do you wanna know what else it can do?"
Ethea nodded enthusiastically.
"First, it naturally synchronizes with its master’s cultivation, mirroring their realm without any extra effort," Soren explained, pointing to the tiny plushie in her hands.
"And it constantly absorbs ambient mana from the surrounding environment on its own, so there is no need to worry about manually recharging it unless necessary.
Beyond that, it possesses autonomous combat capabilities, allowing it to fight alongside its master or defend them independently in times of danger.
Lastly, spells can be stored directly inside it, granting the ability to cast them remotely through the puppet whenever desired."
"It’s pretty good for a spirit puppet," Ethea muttered in surprise.
"But can it reach 7th circle or higher too?"
"That...
I don’t know." Soren rubbed the back of his neck awkwardly.
"Though if I had to guess, it’s probably not that powerful."
"...We can find out about it once you get stronger and reach those stages," Ethea suggested a solution, and Soren nodded in agreement.
While she continued admiring the tiny plushie, he sent the remaining details directly into her mind: ’It can also create a temporary clone of itself.
Though weaker, it can still fight.
And if things ever turn dire, it can self-destruct to release a powerful burst of energy against surrounding foes.
The puppet or its clone will be destroyed, but it can be rebuilt with time and materials.
Furthermore, concentrating on the puppet allows its owner to see and hear through its senses, which makes it ideal for scouting or guarding.’
’...It’s a lot more advanced than I thought.’ Ethea looked up from the miniature figure, genuine impression warming her gaze as she smoothed her thumb over its tiny shoulder.
Soren smiled, sending one final thought through their connection. ’One last thing: it can record and store whatever information it sees and hears.
The owner can review those recorded details whenever needed.’
’That’s... so cool!’ Ethea’s eyes lit up. ’It’s like a personal scout and assistant all in one.’
’...Haha, now that you said it, it really is like a miniature butler and knight rolled into one.’ Soren laughed, shaking his head.
He glanced toward the window, checking the sky’s position.
"Speaking of our schedule, when is the meeting set to start?
"In about two hours," Ethea replied, cradling the tiny plushie carefully in her lap.
Soren checked his wristwatch to confirm, tapping the glass face.
"That gives us a good hour and a half to spare.
Let’s take a rest before we head over."
He gently nudged her shoulders, guiding her into a comfortable position.
"Lean back and close your eyes.
I will wake you when it is time."
"Alright, you take a rest too," Ethea replied and closed her eyes.
Soren rested his arms on the table and lowered his head, staring at her peaceful face with a soft smile before finally letting his eyelids slip shut.
’Malakor, you know what to do.’
’...Yes, master.’
’Good...’
When Soren opened his eyes again, he found himself standing in an endless grassland, a warm breeze rustling the green blades around him.
He closed his eyes again, reaching out into the expanse to find a familiar presence and carefully guiding it to his side.
A few seconds later, he opened his eyes and found Ethea, standing before him on her own two feet, bathed in the soft light of the open field.
"...Dear, open your eyes."
"...?" Ethea’s eyelids fluttered open a moment later, revealing her ice-blue eyes as she blinked at the sweeping field around them.
Her gaze landed on Soren first, then drifted to the endless green stretch reaching toward the horizon, confusion washing over her expression.
Before she could process the sudden change of scenery, a far sharper realization struck her.
The ground felt solid beneath her soles.
Weight rested firmly on her legs, balance shifting naturally with every small breath.
Her breath hitched as her gaze dropped to her feet, perfectly planted in the grass.
"Is this... a dream?"

chapters.title: Chapter 354: Lovers’ Discussion [1]
paragraphs: "Is this... a dream?"
Ethea looked back at Soren, her expression caught between wonder and disbelief.
"What do you think?" He smiled and spread his arms wide. "Or... do you want to check for yourself?"

"..." Ethea paused for a split second, then, throwing all hesitation aside, she sprinted across the grass and leaped straight into his arms. The grass brushed against her bare feet, each step sending a thrill through her legs that she had almost forgotten.
Thump.
Soren caught her easily, his arms wrapping around her as he spun her once before settling her against his chest. "It really feels like a dream..."
"Yeah..."
They hugged for a while, neither wanting to let go. Eventually, Ethea pulled back just enough to look at him, and standing this close, she had to tilt her head up to meet his eyes.
"...You’re really taller than me," she murmured, as if noticing it for the first time.
Soren chuckled. "You don’t like it?"
"No." She shook her head, a small smile playing on her lips. "I like it."
She paused, then added, "It makes me feel safe."
"...That’s good to know." Soren smiled and pulled her back into his arms, resting his chin on top of her head. "Then I’ll stay tall for you."
"Hehe, you promised." Ethea giggled. "But... Where exactly are we?

"Ah, right." Soren pulled back and gestured around them. "This is a shared mental space. It’s a realm created from our combined consciousness, a place that exists only for us. No one else can enter, and no one else can find it. We can meet here whenever we want, no matter how far apart we are in the real world."
Ethea looked around again, taking it in with fresh eyes. "It’s beautiful."
"Mm. And it’s useful too." He paused and explained its benefits. "As for how it was created, you know about that shared ability called Soul-Binding Symbiosis, right?"
Ethea nodded, pieces clicking into place.
"That ability evolved, and this is its new effect." Soren continued and explained the rest of the evolution. "...The reason why you didn’t feel any pain is also related to it."
"I see..." Ethea whispered. "Eternal Bond... It’s really a fitting name."
"I thought the same thing." Soren chuckled. "And... I awakened another ability."

He went on to explain Curse Resistance and its two active effects. He also mentioned that he had discovered he was cursed with a bad luck curse, and that he planned to test the new ability first before deciding whether to use Curse Reflection to send it back at whoever cast it and so on.
"...You think they might be the same person who put that curse on me?" Ethea muttered as they sat together in the grass.
Soren nodded and shared his other guesses.

"...I think you shouldn’t use the curse reflection, not until we find out who the caster is," Ethea said with a solemn expression. "If they’re who we think they are, then they might end up casting a powerful curse on you that even your ability won’t be able to defend against."
"...But why do you think they put this curse on me, then? Why not something powerful from the get-go?" Soren asked with a frown. "This makes me more uncertain about their identity and purpose."

"...I think I know the reason why," Ethea muttered, turning to Soren. "It must be because of distance and time. From what I know, casting powerful curses requires extensive preparation, complex rituals, and a massive amount of time. On top of that, the target often needs to be nearby for the curse to take hold properly. Because of those limitations, they probably had to settle for this mid-level curse instead. It might seem low-ranking to you, but executing it over a long distance is actually hard to pull off and pretty powerful in its own right.

"...If it’s really that difficult, then my guess might be more accurate than I thought." Soren narrowed his eyes. "They could cast an 8th circle curse on you after all. And... you’re right, I should keep the curse on myself, and I also think... we shouldn’t try this ability on you."

Ethea smiled, knowing well why he paused there. "Don’t worry, dear. I know you’re just worried about me... You think they might do something if I show some abnormalities again, right? Especially if I have something like that."

Soren nodded helplessly, wondering why he even bothered to hide his thoughts when she could read him this easily. "...Since we can’t do anything about it now, let’s focus on something else. I had something else I wanted to talk with you about anyway."
"Oh, what else did you want to talk about?" Ethea tilted her head curiously.
"It’s actually about you." Soren smiled. "Your hidden talents and traits, I mean."
"Huh? Can you see them now?"
"Mm. But only their names." Soren answered and listed each of them. "Did you know about all of them?"

Ethea shook her head. "I knew I had something like a photographic memory since I could recall anything I saw or read with ease. I guess Perfect Recall is that, and Stellar Soul must have appeared after I inherited and cultivated the Stellar Soul Weaver Sutra. Sovereign’s Bloodline can also be explained by the furtive encounter I told you about before, about managing to get a glimpse of an Authority."
Soren nodded as he had similar guesses. Her Authority was called Frost Sovereign after all.

"However, I didn’t know about Heart of Winter, Unyielding Will, and Fated One." Ethea continued. "Though I have a good idea of why for the first two. I haven’t noticed Unyielding Will, probably because I had the Unshackled Soul ability, and I must have confused its effects with this. The same goes for Heart of Winter. Although I don’t know exactly what it is, I probably haven’t noticed it because of my high affinity with ice."
"Hmm, that explains it... Wait, speaking of your ice affinity, I finally managed to see its grade!"
"Huh? You did?" Ethea blinked in surprise. After all, even the academy and bureau’s testing couldn’t measure it properly and graded it as grade 9. "How did it show to you? Was it grade 9 after all?"
Soren shook his head. "It’s actually called EX grade."

chapters.title: Chapter 355: Lovers’ Discussion [2]
paragraphs: "EX grade?"
"Yeah, have you heard about it?" Soren asked.

"EX grade..." Ethea trailed off for a few seconds, her expression thoughtful. "I think it’s a label for things above Grade 9. And some also treat it as the highest possible rank, reserved for things that break the conventional scale entirely. And it’s mostly used when mentioning other worlds."
"You mean... Etenia doesn’t have anything like that?"

"Not that I know of." She shook her head. "Everything in our world falls within the normal grading system. EX is for things that come from beyond, or for people and things who have transcended the limits of this world entirely."
"In that case, your ice affinity is at a transcendent level?" Soren stroked his chin thoughtfully. "And... is Transcendence what comes after Paragon rank?"
"...You know about Transcendence?" Ethea looked at him in surprise.
"Mm. I have seen someone with Transcendence potential." Soren replied. "And it’s someone you know well."
"...Ryan?" Ethea guessed after a moment’s thought.
Soren nodded. "That’s right. Although I didn’t know exactly what Transcendence is, I figured out it must be higher than Paragon after our conversation about Authorities back then."
"I see..." Ethea fell silent again, her expression unreadable. "...Was that why you were acting so close with him?"

"...That’s one of the reasons, but not exactly the true one," Soren answered. "Unfortunately, I can’t tell you about it yet. But I will talk with Ryan, and if he’s willing to share. If he agrees, I’ll tell you everything."
"Alright, thank you, dear." Ethea smiled, leaning on his shoulder.

Soren stroked her hair, letting the silence settle for a second before bringing up the other detail that had caught his attention. "Speaking of affinities, I was able to see your affinity, which was darkness. I was a bit surprised since you didn’t mention it before."
Ethea froze, tilting her head as confusion washed over her face. "I have a darkness affinity?"
Soren nodded, watching her reaction closely. "You didn’t know?"
Ethea shook her head. "This is the first time I’m hearing about it. And I haven’t sensed it before, nor did it appear in the tests."
"Then, could your darkness affinity be sealed like mine?" Soren guessed. "...I can’t think of any other reason.
"That might be the case..." Ethea trailed off, and her eyes lit up as she realized something. "Wait... could it be connected to the Fated One trait?"
"You said you don’t know Fated One, though?"
"It’s true that I don’t know about it, but I don’t have any other guesses." She paused, then looked at him. "What if... Fated One means I’m fated for... you? And you’re fated for me?"
Soren blinked, caught off guard by the suggestion. "That’s... a nice thought."
"It is, isn’t it?" Ethea smiled.

Soren returned the smile, then shook his head. "But I feel like it probably means more than that. Like you’re destined for something great. Just like in many stories. The chosen one. The protagonist."
"Me? The protagonist?" Ethea raised a brow.
"Mm. And if you’re the protagonist, then..." He paused dramatically. "Am I the male lead?"
They stared at each other for a beat and burst out laughing.
"Actually," Ethea said once the laughter faded, "I think you’re more of a protagonist than I am, dear."
"Oh, really? And what makes you say that?" Soren chuckled, looking down at her.

"Well, you’re kind, remarkably strong, and you never hesitate to help others," Ethea said, her voice soft as her eyes met his. "Plus, you always manage to save me whenever I’m in danger. If that isn’t the hero of a story, I don’t know who is."
A faint heat touched Soren’s cheeks, and he rubbed the back of his neck, caught off guard by her earnestness. "When you put it like that... it sounds a bit much.

He then cleared his throat, a light laugh breaking through his embarrassment, and pulled her back into a comfortable embrace. "I have a better way of looking at it. Instead of arguing over who gets the spotlight, let’s just say we’re both the main characters? A story doesn’t have to belong to just one person, you know. Life isn’t a single grand script written for a lone hero while everyone else fills the background. We’re all carrying our own weight, fighting our own battles, and living out our own main roles. In the end, everyone is the protagonist of their own life — it just depends on whose eyes you’re looking through."
"W-What?"
"Why are you looking at me like that?" Soren asked, suddenly self-conscious.
"I..." Ethea kept her eyes fixed on him, a subtle spark of amusement dancing in her eyes. "...I was just thinking about how lucky I am to have such a wise husband."

Soren’s lips twitched, caught between a faint scowl and a hidden grin. He knew full well she was teasing him, taking advantage of his sudden burst of eloquence to ruffle his composure. Yet despite the light mockery, the affection in her voice made his heart warm all the same.
"You’re enjoying this way too much."
"Was I not allowed to?" Ethea blinked innocently.
"Urgh... fine. Laugh all you want." He sighed dramatically, but his arms tightened around her. "Just remember, I’m the one who gets to tease you back later."
"Hehe, ok~" Ethea giggled. "But I really meant it. And in fact, I have a similar opinion to yours."
"You do?" Soren raised a brow.

"Mm... But I also think that some people are more than just protagonists in their own stories. Some people affect so many others that they become part of everyone’s story. And you’re one of those people, Soren. Whether you realize it or not."
"Well, the same can be said to you, Ethea," Soren replied. "In fact, you might be the reason my story even started and became worth telling."
"..." Ethea paused and looked up at him. "...Kiss me."

"...Ok." Soren did not need to be told twice. He cupped her cheek, his thumb brushing over her skin as he leaned down and pressed his lips against hers, taking his time before resting his forehead against hers. "...You’re so irresistible."

chapters.title: Chapter 356: One Of A Kind
paragraphs: In an unknown location, a black-robed figure knelt before a white, glowing orb, their expression respectful.
"Leader, we have executed your order. Kita City is at our mercy now."
A moment passed, and a voice replied through the glowing orb. "Good job. Now, proceed with the next phase of the plan. Make sure nothing goes wrong this time."
"Understood, Leader." The figure bowed their head. "And rest assured, we will definitely get back Young Master Lucent."
"...Don’t get overconfident. Or else, you’re gonna end up like Aeshvin."
"Y-Yes, I apologize for my arrogance." The figure lowered their head further, a visible tremor running through their shoulders. "I promise I will not fail you."
"See that you don’t. Now go. I want to see the results by this evening."
The orb dimmed, and the figure rose slowly, their expression unreadable beneath the shadow of their hood. Then they turned and disappeared into the darkness.
"We are here..."
"How does it feel to be back?" Zura asked, glancing at Ethea as she pushed the wheelchair through the academy gates.
"...Strange," Ethea admitted, looking around at the familiar buildings and courtyards. "It hasn’t changed much... But I have."
"That’s life, I suppose." Zura shrugged. "Places stay the same while people move on. It’s been, what, two years since you last visited?"
"...Yes." Ethea nodded. "And I’m sorry for not contacting you. I got caught up in work and other matters, and I forgot to keep you in the loop.

"Hey, no need to apologize." Zura waved a hand dismissively. "You’re here now, aren’t you? Besides, I could have contacted you myself, but I didn’t. Because I knew you were busy and I didn’t want to add to your plate. And honestly, I regret that decision to this day and perhaps forever."
"If I reached out to you sooner, perhaps... you wouldn’t end up like this."

"...Nura, thank you for caring about me, but you shouldn’t feel guilty. None of this was your fault, and worrying over what could have been won’t change where we are now." Ethea smiled gently at her friend. "Besides, even though I hate the condition I’m in, I’m actually happy with where my life has led me. I have a husband who loves me, friends who care about me, and a future I’m actually looking forward to. That’s more than enough for me."
"...You’re right." Zura sighed and nodded. "I’m sorry. I didn’t mean to bring down the mood."
"You didn’t. You were just being a good friend."

"Mm." Zura smiled, then her expression shifted into something more playful. "Speaking of which... a husband who loves you? Look at you, making declarations like that with a straight face. When did my stoic best friend turn into such an unrepentant romantic?"
Ethea didn’t even blink, meeting Zura’s mischievous look with remarkable composure. "It’s simply the truth."

"Is that so?" Zura leaned forward, resting her chin on her hand, her smile widening into a knowing smirk. "And what about you? Does the feeling go both ways, or is he doing all the heavy lifting here?"
Without a second of hesitation, Ethea gave a firm nod. "Of course I love him too, more than anyone else in this world."
Her tone was solemn, but the sudden flush creeping over the tips of her ears betrayed her embarrassment.

"Hahaha!" Zura burst out laughing, clapping her hands together at the sight. "Look at you! You say it so casually, yet your face is giving you away entirely." She shook her head, genuinely impressed. "Honestly though, I have to hand it to Mr. Soren. A man who can melt your heart like this deserves a medal, you know. I already respected him for looking after you, but now? I’m even more curious to see what kind of guy he really is."
Ethea’s chin tilted up slightly, an unmistakable flicker of pride crossing her features at the praise for her husband.

Seeing that subtle reaction, Zura’s lips curled into a smirk once again. "So... will you tell me about yourlovely husbandnow? I want to know everything, if possible. And hey," she skilfully adjusted her posture, smoothing a hand along her waist to showcase her striking figure with effortless confidence, "if you want, I can even help you test his loyalty. See if he really only has eyes for you.
Ethea stared at her blankly, completely unbothered by the attempt at provocation. "Try it, and you’ll just end up embarrassing yourself."
Zura tilted her head, a dangerously charming grin touching her lips. "Oh, are you really sure? You won’t cry if I end up winning him over, right?"
"Not at all," Ethea said with a serene smile, not a single trace of doubt in her eyes. "I believe in my husband and in the love we share. Nothing you do could ever shake that."
"...Tsk." Zura clicked her tongue and rolled her eyes, though a fond smile broke through her playful annoyance. "Fine, fine, I yield. There’s no need to brag so much."
"...You started it first." Ethea replied, her tone calm but with a hint of satisfaction.
"Yeah, yeah, I did." Zura shook her head, still smiling. "But seriously, I’m happy for you. You deserve this. After everything you’ve been through, you deserve someone who makes you smile like that."
Ethea’s expression softened. "...Thank you, Zura."
"Don’t mention it. But if you are really thankful, just help me find a man like him." Zura grinned again.
Ethea shook her head, her tone perfectly even. "Even if I want to, I can’t."
Zura blinked, leaning in with genuine curiosity. "Why not?"
"Because he’s one of a kind," Ethea replied flatly, without a single trace of hesitation. "There is no one else like him in this world."
Zura froze completely, turning into a statue as the shameless declaration hung in the air. For three full seconds, she didn’t move an inch.
Then, she snapped back to life, throwing her hands up in utter disbelief. "Oh, come on! So cheesy! Are you not embarrassed saying things like that with a completely straight face?!"
"..." Ethea stared back with the same expressionless face.
"Urgh!" Zura groaned, pressing a hand to her forehead. "Who are you and what have you done with my friend?"

chapters.title: Chapter 357: Academy Visit [1]
paragraphs: "Who are you, and what have you done with my friend?"
"Your friend... simply grew up and found the person she wants to spend her life with," Ethea responded calmly, unaffected by Zura’s dramatic reaction. "Is that so hard to believe?"
Zura nodded vigorously. "Yes! You’re like a whole different person! Even when you two came to the restaurant the other day, you weren’t like this. What changed between then and now?"
Ethea fell silent for a moment, considering the question. Then it hit her.
’...Right. That was before we confessed.’

Until then, there had always been a barrier she couldn’t cross, a fear that kept her from showing him how she truly felt. But now that everything was out in the open, there was no longer any reason to hold back.

Perhaps she had always wanted to show him how much she loved him, but the moment had never felt right. Now that it finally was, she found herself saying and doing things she never imagined she would, bold enough to surprise even herself.
"I think... I was just waiting for the chance to finally be more honest." She looked up at slightly confused Zura. "Fortunately, I got that chance."
"...Let me guess, it happened yesterday on your date, right?" Zura asked, a knowing grin spreading across her face.
Ethea confirmed it with a nod.
"Hehe, good. I knew it," Zura said, tapping her chin proudly. "He asked so many questions back then, so I made sure to give him the best recommendations. It must have turned out amazing."
"It was," Ethea replied, her tone soft and earnest. "Thank you for the help, Zura."

"You’re welcome," Zura grinned before her playful expression sobered, giving way to a streak of concern. She leaned in slightly and lowered her voice. "Though... is it really alright to send him in there alone? Wouldn’t it be better if you went together? You know the Vice Principal well, after all."
"It’s alright. He can handle it himself," Ethea answered. "And I don’t want to reveal my existence that openly yet."

"I see." Zura nodded in understanding, knowing they must have their own circumstances, especially considering how Soren is supposed to be seriously injured right now. "But the Vice Principal is a powerful Sovereign. She must have recognized your presence the moment you entered the academy, right?
"She probably has," Ethea agreed. "But she won’t come looking for me as long as I don’t go looking for her."
"Right... Then do you want to tour the academy while we wait? A few things have changed since you last visited."
"...Let’s wait till he comes out," Ethea answered after a pause. "I want to tour it with him."
"Ah, I almost forgot how attached you’ve become," Zura teased, letting out a soft laugh as she shook her head. "Fine, fine. I won’t force you to go without your beloved husband."

"I simply want to experience it together with him. And you will still be with us to show the way, won’t you?" Pausing briefly, she brought the playful banter to a close. "While we wait, though... can we talk about his sister?"
"...Of course. I have uncovered a few things related to her too."
With that, Zura sat down on the bench beside Ethea, and the two of them began to converse in lowered voices.

Meanwhile, in a spacious office on the top floor of the administration building, Soren lounged on a sofa that was both luxurious and comfortable, his expression calm and his posture relaxed. Across from him sat an elderly woman with silver hair pulled back into a neat bun. She wore a monocle on her left eye and a dark, high-collared dress that gave her an air of strict authority.

Soren waited patiently as she drank her tea, the silence between them stretching comfortably. She set the cup down with a soft clink and looked at him, her sharp green eyes holding a warmth that reminded him of a grandmother he never had.
"I have considered your offer," she said. "And I have decided to accept it."
Soren smiled and nodded respectfully. "Thank you, Lady Ramona. The academy won’t regret this.

"I’m sure we won’t." She nodded, a faint smile touching her lips. "The Etenia Academy is happy to cooperate with you, Mr. Everly. On behalf of the faculty and students, I thank you for your generosity."
"The pleasure is mine." Soren stood up and gave a slight bow. "I should take my leave now. I don’t want to take up more of your time."
"Of course." Ramona rose from her seat and walked him to the door. She opened it for him and stood at the threshold as he stepped out.
"Mr. Everly, don’t forget to send my regards to your wife," she said.
Soren paused mid-step. He turned back to look at her, but her expression gave nothing away. After a brief moment, he nodded.
"I will."
Vice Principal Ramona watched him leave, her expression unreadable.
’...Has what Lady Herald prophesied already begun?’ She thought as her senses landed on a familiar presence outside the building. ’...She certainly has changed a lot too.’
With a sigh, she then closed the door and returned to her desk. Her fingers tapped against the polished wood as she stared at the window.
’...The wheels of fate are turning faster than I expected.’

She then turned to the holographic monitor on her desk and tapped it twice. Two profiles appeared side by side. Nura, a special student with a sealed constitution and a tragic past. And Ryan, a lucky young man who managed to survive a Golden Gate together with Soren Everly and came out of it with a potential that rivaled the academy’s top talents.
She narrowed her eyes, studying the two images in silence. Then she let out a long, helpless sigh.
’Well... I’ll just have to wait and see what happens next,’ she muttered, closing the monitor. ’There’s no point interfering now. Lady Herald always said the path would reveal itself in time.’

chapters.title: Chapter 358: Academy Visit [2]
paragraphs: "After leaving Vice Principal Ramona’s office, Soren headed back outside the building using the teleportation circle. Once he left the building, he didn’t hurry to regroup with Ethea and Zura. He sat down on a nearby bench, closed his eyes, and focused on the floating window in his vision.
Name: Ramona Ross
Race: Human
Age: 78
Status: Healthy
Rank: 8th Circle (Peak Stage)
[Current Mana Level: 12,459,007]
[Mental Cultivation: Sage’s Path — Stage 4: Inner Sanctum]
[Current Mental Power: 848,060 / 1,000,000]
[Abilities: ? (SSS-Rank), Sage’s Sanctuary (SS-Rank), Sage’s Insight (S-Rank)]
[Affinities: Wind (Grade 9 - SSS Rank), Light (Grade 8 - SS Rank), Nature (Grade 9 - SSS Rank)]
[Hidden Talent / Traits: Sage’s Bloodline, Nature’s Chosen, Motherly Warmth]
[Mental State: Curious, Analytical]
[Investment Value: Mythic]
[Potential: Transcendence]
’...Too powerful.’
The words echoed in his mind as he stared at the window.

This was the first time he stood face to face with a true Sovereign, and it made him realize just how vast the gap between them truly was. He had known she was strong. A Sovereign-level Awakened was always someone to be respected. But seeing the numbers laid out before him was different. The gap between them wasn’t something he could close with a few months or even years of hard work.
’...And she’s not even the strongest.’

The thought lingered. If Ramona was this powerful, what about other Sovereigns? Or the beings above her? What about the enemies he would eventually have to face? Would he be able to protect Ethea when that time came? Would he even be able to put up a fight?
’...Urgh, stop being pessimistic, Soren!’

He shook his head and pushed the thoughts aside. There was no point in worrying about things he couldn’t control. All he could do was keep moving forward, keep growing stronger, and hope that it would be enough when the time came.
’Let’s use the chance to study her status more carefully.’
With that in mind, he started inspecting her status more thoroughly. The first things he noticed were her mana, mental cultivation, and mental power.

From what he remembered, Emperors typically had a mana capacity of one to three million, while Sovereigns ranged from four to ten million. That meant Ramona was at the very top of her rank, just a step away from the Paragon threshold.
’She cultivates mentally as well and is at the peak of the Inner Sanctum Stage.’

Her mental power was approaching a million, bringing her close to breaking through to the fifth stage: Immortal Zenith. At that level, the soul would be freed from physical death, able to exist independently or even reconstitute the body — a realm most people would never dream of reaching.

’...Should I help her with it?’ He pondered the idea for a moment, then shook his head. ’No, not yet. I would have to explain how I knew she cultivated mentally in the first place. That’s not something I can just bring up without raising questions.’
He made a mental note to discuss it with Ethea first. If she knew something, they could figure out a way to approach Ramona without raising suspicion.
’...Hmm. She also has an SSS-rank ability, and of course the name is hidden. But the other two give me an idea of what it might be and what kind of person she is.’
Those two contained the word ’sage,’ and even her mental cultivation technique was called Sage’s Path. So he guessed she might be some kind of sage.
’...Perhaps Sage of Nature?’ He thought as he saw her two grade 9 and one grade 8 affinities. Whatever the case, she was clearly someone deeply connected to the natural world.
He moved on to her hidden talents and traits. Each one told him something about the woman behind the title.

’Another ’sage’-related talent, but Ethea had the same thing. Does that mean they are connected somehow? Or perhaps the fortuitous encounter Ethea talked about is connected to her? And Nature’s Chosen explains her high Nature affinity. As for the Motherly Warmth trait... I guess it’s related to how she appears.’

He continued reading and saw nothing wrong with her mental state or investment value. However, he was surprised by her potential. After all, she was only the second person he’d met who had the potential for Transcendence.
’...I should really find a chance to invest in her.’

He decided, closed the window, and opened his eyes. Standing up, he headed straight toward Ethea and Zura, weaving through walkways and small groups of students. A few of them glanced at him, curious about the unfamiliar face, but none stopped him. When he finally reached the bench where the two women were sitting, he slowed his pace and offered an apologetic smile.
"Sorry. Did I make you wait long?"
"Not at all," Ethea replied, looking up at him. "How did it go?"

"It went well. She agreed to cooperate." He sat down beside her, his shoulder brushing against hers. "The contract will be finalized as soon as Ryan arrives, and his transfer exam will be scheduled for early next week."
"That’s good." Ethea nodded, relief flickering in her eyes.
"I told you there would be no problem." Zura smiled, then stood up from the bench and stretched. "So, are you two ready to tour the academy now? We’ve still got some time before lunch."
Soren and Ethea exchanged a glance and nodded.
"Please, lead the way," Soren said.
Zura gave him a thumbs-up and started walking. "Alright then. Stick close and don’t wander off. This place is bigger than it looks."
As they fell into step beside her, she glanced back at Soren with a grin. "Speaking of lunch, when are you going to treat me? You owe me for all those recommendations I gave you too, remember?"
"If you want, I will cook for you today. Lunch or dinner, at our place. Just say the word."
"Oh, are you sure?" Zura raised a brow, slightly surprised by his straightforwardness. "I don’t want to trouble you."
"It’s no trouble at all." Soren shook his head. "It’s the least I can do after everything you’ve done for us."
"Then, I want to come for dinner." Zura’s lips curved into a mischievous grin. "I’ll be bringing a very healthy appetite, so you better be prepared."
"Don’t worry," Soren said with a subtle glint in his eyes. "I’ll cook something you’ll definitely like."

He shook his head and pushed the thoughts aside.
There was no point in worrying about things he couldn’t control.
All he could do was keep moving forward, keep growing stronger, and hope that it would be enough when the time came.
’Let’s use the chance to study her status more carefully.’
With that in mind, he started inspecting her status more thoroughly.
The first things he noticed were her mana, mental cultivation, and mental power.
From what he remembered, Emperors typically had a mana capacity of one to three million, while Sovereigns ranged from four to ten million.
That meant Ramona was at the very top of her rank, just a step away from the Paragon threshold.
’She cultivates mentally as well and is at the peak of the Inner Sanctum Stage.’
Her mental power was approaching a million, bringing her close to breaking through to the fifth stage: Immortal Zenith.
At that level, the soul would be freed from physical death, able to exist independently or even reconstitute the body — a realm most people would never dream of reaching.
’...Should I help her with it?’ He pondered the idea for a moment, then shook his head. ’No, not yet.
I would have to explain how I knew she cultivated mentally in the first place.
That’s not something I can just bring up without raising questions.’
He made a mental note to discuss it with Ethea first.
If she knew something, they could figure out a way to approach Ramona without raising suspicion.
She also has an SSS-rank ability, and of course the name is hidden.
But the other two give me an idea of what it might be and what kind of person she is.’
Those two contained the word ’sage,’ and even her mental cultivation technique was called Sage’s Path.
So he guessed she might be some kind of sage.
’...Perhaps Sage of Nature?’ He thought as he saw her two grade 9 and one grade 8 affinities.
Whatever the case, she was clearly someone deeply connected to the natural world.
He moved on to her hidden talents and traits.
Each one told him something about the woman behind the title.
’Another ’sage’-related talent, but Ethea had the same thing.
Does that mean they are connected somehow?
Or perhaps the fortuitous encounter Ethea talked about is connected to her?
And Nature’s Chosen explains her high Nature affinity.
As for the Motherly Warmth trait...
I guess it’s related to how she appears.’
He continued reading and saw nothing wrong with her mental state or investment value.
However, he was surprised by her potential.
After all, she was only the second person he’d met who had the potential for Transcendence.
’...I should really find a chance to invest in her.’
He decided, closed the window, and opened his eyes.
Standing up, he headed straight toward Ethea and Zura, weaving through walkways and small groups of students.
A few of them glanced at him, curious about the unfamiliar face, but none stopped him.
When he finally reached the bench where the two women were sitting, he slowed his pace and offered an apologetic smile.
"Sorry.
Did I make you wait long?"
"Not at all," Ethea replied, looking up at him.
"How did it go?"
"It went well.
She agreed to cooperate." He sat down beside her, his shoulder brushing against hers.
"The contract will be finalized as soon as Ryan arrives, and his transfer exam will be scheduled for early next week."
"That’s good." Ethea nodded, relief flickering in her eyes.
"I told you there would be no problem." Zura smiled, then stood up from the bench and stretched.
"So, are you two ready to tour the academy now?
We’ve still got some time before lunch."
Soren and Ethea exchanged a glance and nodded.
"Please, lead the way," Soren said.
Zura gave him a thumbs-up and started walking.
"Alright then.
Stick close and don’t wander off.
This place is bigger than it looks."
As they fell into step beside her, she glanced back at Soren with a grin.
"Speaking of lunch, when are you going to treat me?
You owe me for all those recommendations I gave you too, remember?"
"If you want, I will cook for you today.
Lunch or dinner, at our place.
Just say the word."
"Oh, are you sure?" Zura raised a brow, slightly surprised by his straightforwardness.
"I don’t want to trouble you."
"It’s no trouble at all." Soren shook his head.
"It’s the least I can do after everything you’ve done for us."
"Then, I want to come for dinner." Zura’s lips curved into a mischievous grin.
"I’ll be bringing a very healthy appetite, so you better be prepared."
"Don’t worry," Soren said with a subtle glint in his eyes.
"I’ll cook something you’ll definitely like."

chapters.title: Chapter 359: Academy Visit [3]
paragraphs: Zura led them away from the administrative spire, gesturing toward the wide path ahead. "You have already seen this place, but let me still refresh your memory. This is the Welcome Plaza. It’s usually packed with students, but since it’s summer vacation, it’s pretty empty right now."
She gestured around at the sparse crowd. A few students sat on benches near the fountains, and a couple of stalls were still open, but most of the plaza was quiet.

"During the semester, you can’t even walk through here without bumping into someone. Club recruitments, food stalls, study groups, and impromptu ’sparring matches’ that end up getting broken up by faculty." Zura added, shaking her head fondly. "Anyway, let’s keep going."

She led them past the plaza and toward a large building with wide glass doors. "This is the main cafeteria: three floors, each one serving different styles of food. The first floor serves everyday meals, the second offers more formal dining and magical meals, and the third is reserved for special events and VIPs. The food is actually decent, and the head chef is a Master Magic Chef."

They continued down a tree-lined path, passing several smaller buildings along the way. "Those are the general study halls. First and second years have most of their classes there. Nothing too impressive, but they get the job done."

Further ahead, a small stone building came into view. It was old, with weathered walls and a single wooden door that looked like it hadn’t been replaced in centuries. Compared to the modern-style buildings they had passed, it looked almost out of place.
"What is this place?" Soren asked curiously.
"It’s the library," Zura replied with a mysterious smile.
"The library?" Soren raised a brow in confusion.
Zura grinned. "You’re thinking it’s too small for the best academy on the continent, right?"
Soren nodded honestly.

"That’s because you’re only looking at the shell," Zura explained proudly, gesturing toward the ancient structure. "The building itself is centuries old, preserved from the academy’s founding, but the interior was expanded using high-tier spatial magic. What looks like a tiny stone cottage on the outside is actually an endless labyrinth inside."

She began walking again as they took in the lingering spatial mana drifting near the entrance. "It holds miles of bookshelves, ancient archives, and private study rooms folded into localized dimensions. You could spend a lifetime in there and still not read everything."
"That’s indeed amazing," Soren muttered in awe.
"Mm, mm," Zura nodded enthusiastically. "Ethea and I used to come here all the time. Especially before exams, we would basically move into one of the private dimensional study rooms for days on end.
"And you usually fell asleep after thirty minutes of reading," Ethea added quietly, a subtle upturn at the corner of her lips.
Zura let out a light laugh, not even trying to deny it. "Hey, those spatial pockets are dangerously cozy! Can’t blame me for taking advantage of the atmosphere."
Soren chuckled, imagining the scene in his head.

They continued walking, passing more buildings along the way. A few training halls, potion workshops, and dormitories for first-year students. Zura pointed them out one by one without slowing down, her commentary brief but informative.

Eventually, they reached the end of the open grounds, where the pathway terminated before an imposing set of colossal stone walls embedded with glowing runic arrays. In the center stood a massive iron gate, guarded by two armed sentinels and flanked by a tall crystal pillar.

Zura stopped in her tracks and turned around, gesturing toward the structure. "Unfortunately, we will have to stop here. Because beyond these gates lies the inner campus. You can’t enter without special permission, and unfortunately, I don’t have the authority to bring guests inside yet."
"No, it’s alright," Soren reassured her. "I had a great time seeing everything. The outer campus feels massive and interesting on its own."
Zura grinned, nodding in agreement. "Actually, we only covered about a quarter of it. There’s plenty more to explore, so let’s keep moving!"
They spent the next hour walking through the remaining districts, taking in the rest of the sights before finally circling back to where they started at the welcome plaza.
Zura let out a satisfied exhale and turned to Soren. "So, what did you think?"
"It was fun," Soren said honestly. "Thank you for taking the time to show us around. I know how busy you are."
"Don’t mention it. It’s been a while since I got to play tour guide." Zura waved a hand dismissively, then glanced at Ethea. "And what about you?"
"It felt a little nostalgic," Ethea admitted. "Thank you, Zura.
"Anytime, Lea." Zura smiled, then gestured toward the main gate. "Come on, I’ll walk you both out."
They made their way back through the plaza and toward the academy entrance. As they approached the gate, Soren slowed his pace and turned to the two women.
"I’ll head out first and bring the car around," he said. "You two take your time."
Zura nodded. "We’ll be right behind you."

Soren nodded and quickly took his leave. The reason they were moving separately was simple. The academy’s exit was likely under surveillance by the Valmere family, and he couldn’t risk being seen with Ethea, who was in a wheelchair. That was why Zura had brought her in earlier, and it was safer if Zura brought her out too.

The only unfortunate thing was that they failed to encounter his little sister during the tour. He had hoped to catch a glimpse of her, even from a distance. But the academy was vast, and she was likely in the inner district or somewhere else on the grounds.
’There will be other chances,’ he told himself. ’Now that we have a connection to the academy, it’s only a matter of time.’

He reached the car, got in, started the engine, and pulled around to the pickup spot. A few minutes later, Zura emerged with Ethea, pushing her wheelchair at a casual pace. After helping her into the car, they said goodbye.
"Take care, you two," Zura said. "And don’t forget about dinner."
"We won’t," Soren replied. "See you later."
They watched until Zura’s figure disappeared into the campus. Soren pulled away from the curb and merged onto the road. They had only been driving for a minute when his phone buzzed.
"...It’s a message from Ryan."

chapters.title: Chapter 360: Ryan’s Arrival
paragraphs: "Father, Mother." Ryan turned around with a bright smile. "Brother Soren just messaged me. He’s coming to pick us up."
His parents exchanged a glance and nodded.
"There’s a cafe right over there," Ryan then suggested, pointing toward a small storefront down the street. "We can sit inside and grab a drink while we wait."
"Mommy!" His little sister exclaimed. "I want an ice cream!"
"You heard her."

Left with no choice, they walked over to the cafe and found a table near the front. Twenty minutes later, Ryan’s phone buzzed with a new notification. He checked the screen, then looked toward his parents. "He’s here."
They paid for their orders and stepped outside onto the sidewalk. Just down the curb, Soren was leaning against his car, waving toward them with a friendly smile.
"Let’s go!"

Ryan’s family walked over, and they exchanged warm greetings. Soren shook hands with Ryan’s father, gave a polite nod to his mother, and ruffled Ryan and his little sister’s hair like an older brother would.
"I hope you didn’t have to wait too long."
"No, not at all," Ryan’s father said, shaking his head. "Thank you for coming to get us."
"Of course. Let’s get in." Soren opened the rear door and gestured for Ryan and his little sister to climb in first.
The little girl spotted Ethea in the front as soon as she sat down.
"Pretty sister!" she chirped, waving enthusiastically.
Ethea waved at her through the mirror. "How have you been, little one?"
"Good! I missed you!"
"I missed you too.
Ryan slid in beside his sister and gave Ethea a respectful nod. "Sister-in-law. It’s good to see you again."
Ethea returned the nod, then turned to greet Ryan’s parents as they settled into the middle row. Once everyone was seated, Soren pulled away from the curb and merged into traffic.
"By the way, how was the journey?" Soren initiated a conversation, glancing at them through the rearview mirror.
"It was long," Ryan’s father admitted. "But we took our time and made plenty of stops. The children enjoyed seeing new places."
"That’s good to hear."

"Speaking of the journey," Ryan’s mother spoke up, "we actually came across some interesting news a few days ago. It was about a cooking competition called the Golden Ladle Championship and an attack that happened during it."
Soren blinked, feigning surprise. "You saw that?"
"Of course we did. It was all over the news." She smiled warmly. "And congratulations, Mr. Soren. We were so happy when we saw it, and Ryan wouldn’t stop talking about it either."
"Thank you, Auntie," Soren replied modestly, watching them in the mirror. "I was just lucky to have everything come together at the right moment."

"Nonsense, talent isn’t luck," she said, though her tone softened as worry crept into her voice. "Though... the reports afterward had us sick with worry. They mentioned you were severely injured during that attack. Ryan told us not to worry, but we couldn’t help it. Are you really fine? We aren’t troubling you by visiting while you need rest, are we?"
"Not at all," Soren assured her. "I’ve been recovering well, and honestly, having you here is a nice change of pace. It gets boring staying cooped up all day."
Ryan’s mother let out a small laugh. "Then we’ll try not to be too much of a handful."
"You could never be." Soren smiled warmly.

They continued chatting as he drove through the city. He told them about Ryan’s transfer process and mentioned that he had also found a place for them to stay during their visit. Ryan’s parents thanked him repeatedly, and Ryan himself kept asking questions about the academy, eager to know what awaited him.

Soon, they arrived in a modern residential complex. Soren parked the car and led them up to a spacious apartment he had arranged for their stay. While Ethea played with Ryan’s little sister in the living room, he helped Ryan and his parents settle in. Then, they shared lunch together before Soren and Ethea took their leave.

They spent the rest of the afternoon cultivating and training together in their new mental realm. However, Soren had to leave early as he had promised to cook for Zura. Fortunately, he had bought many good things during their shopping spree at the harvest festival, so he had everything he needed for a proper meal.
He got to work in the kitchen, preparing a spread that would impress even a fellow senior magic chef.
"Let’s put my improved skills to the test, shall we?"

He mumbled to himself and began cooking. Two hours passed in a flash. By the time he finished, the table was set with a full-course meal, and Ethea had already woken from her cultivation and joined him. Just as Soren placed the last platter on the table, a knock came at the door.
"She’s here."
Soren wiped his hands on a towel and walked to the door. He opened it to find Zura standing there with a small box in her hand.
"You didn’t have to have to bring anything," Soren said.
"It’s just a cake. Ethea’s favorite, in fact." She held it out to him. "Now are you going to let me in, or do I have to stand out here all evening?"
Soren stepped aside with a small laugh. "Come in."
Zura grinned and strode in, pausing as her nose twitched. "I smell something delicious."

She glanced around, spotted Ethea, and her face lit up. Without another word, she crossed the room and pulled her into a tight hug. When she pulled back, her gaze drifted past Ethea to the dining area. A low "Whoa..." escaped her lips as her eyes widened at the table, overflowing with a colorful array of freshly made dishes and sweets.
"..." She stared at it for a long moment, her eyes moving from dish to dish. Then she turned to Soren. "You prepared all of this?"
Soren nodded and pulled out a chair for her. "Please, sit."
Zura didn’t move right away, her mind still catching up with what her eyes were seeing.

She had heard the stories, of course. Ethea had told her plenty, and the rumors from the championship had spread far and wide. She knew he was good. But knowing and seeing were two very different things. The presentation, the aroma, the careful arrangement of every plate. This wasn’t just skill, this was artistry.
"...This is going to ruin me for every other meal, isn’t it?"

chapters.title: Chapter 361: Speak of the stars...
paragraphs: "...Gulp." Zura swallowed her soup while already reaching for a piece of honeybread before the bowl even hit the wooden surface. She took a massive bite, her cheeks puffing out as she chewed, her hands and utensils practically moving in a blur as she went from one dish to the next.
"Hey, slow down a little," Ethea laughed, shaking her head. "They are all yours. Nobody is gonna take them away."
"Yu shay dat bat I kent stoup," Zura mumbled, her mouth far too full to speak clearly.
Ethea sighed in defeat, a fond smile tugging at her lips as she let her continue her feast.

"By the way, what are all these dishes called?" Zura asked Soren after finally clearing her mouth with a gulp of water. She pointed her fork toward the table. "I only know this one since you cooked it in the finals."

"The soup you just finished is called Crimson Ember Broth," Soren explained, gesturing to the empty bowl before moving across the table. "It helps soothe your pathways and speeds up mana recovery. The skewers next to it are Fire-Glazed Tenderloin, which boosts physical strength and stamina, and the salad uses Dawnbloom Leaves to clear mental fatigue."
He went through each platter, detailing their names, ingredients, and effects. "...How are they? Do they live up to expectations?"

Zura nodded vigorously, her eyes sparkling. "I don’t think I’ll be able to enjoy normal food ever again at this rate!" She paused, turning her gaze toward Ethea with a mischievous grin. "And I think I finally understand how you seduced her. There is no way anyone could resist a spread like this."
Ethea’s cheeks flushed a light pink, though she simply rolled her eyes. "Keep eating, Zura, before you start talking total nonsense."

"Hey, I’m really serious!" Zura declared, taking another bite of the roast with pure bliss written across her face. "If I had someone cooking like this for me every single day, I’d fall in love on the spot too."
Soren chuckled, shaking his head as he poured them all glasses of chilled fruit juice. "I’m glad you approve. Just make sure you save some space, because there’s still dessert."
Zura’s head snapped up, her eyes wide. "There’s dessert?"
Soren nodded with a smile. "Mm. I made a few things earlier. They’re resting in the cooler right now."

Zura stared at him for a moment, then glanced down at the table. The dishes were already half-empty, and she had eaten more than her fair share. Any ordinary cultivator would have been full by now, maybe even struggling to finish their first dish and drink. Fortunately, she was a 6th circle cultivator. Her metabolism and digestion were far beyond those of ordinary and low-ranked cultivators. However, she didn’t know whether she would be able to finish everything, especially with dessert still waiting.

Still, looking at the remaining dishes and realizing how much effort Soren must have poured into each one, she clenched her fists under the table, her eyes burning with determination. Zura turned to her, completely serious. "Thisisa battle, Ethea. A confrontation between my stomach’s limits and culinary perfection. And I refuse to yield!"
"...Pfft!" Ethea laughed out, unable to hold back, and Zura couldn’t keep her stoic face for long before joining in.

’I wonder if she’s doing well...’

"Mm?"

Zura lowered her head in shame, burying her face in her hands with a soft groan as she cursed herself for acting so shamelessly. Zura’s head snapped up, a glare fixing on Ethea the moment she caught the spark of amusement in her eyes. "Urgh, you’re doing this on purpose, aren’t you?!"
"Hehe~" Ethea giggled. "Wasn’t it just you who got worked up on your own? I was just giving you an honest answer."
"..." Zura continued glaring at her, then turned away with a scoff, though her lips twitched as if threatening to betray her with a smile.
"...You’ve gone bad," She muttered a moment later, still facing away. "Marriage has corrupted you."
"Maybe a little," Ethea admitted without a hint of remorse.
"A little? You used to be the serious one. Now you’re teasing me every chance you get."
"I learned from the best."
"...I hate you!"
"Haha~"

Zura grumbled under her breath, reaching for her glass of juice to hide the smile she couldn’t quite suppress. But before she could take a sip, her phone buzzed on the table. She glanced at the screen and picked it up, still muttering complaints at Ethea.
"Yeah, yeah, laugh it up. I’ll get you back for this, just you wait."
She unlocked the phone and read the message. Her hand froze mid-air.
"...Zura?"
Ethea’s laughter faded. She watched as Zura’s expression shifted, her eyes widening as she read through whatever was on the screen. The playful mood vanished in an instant.
"It’s... bad," Zura muttered. She looked up at Ethea, then glanced toward the television. She stood, quickly found the remote, turned it on, and switched to a news channel.
The screen flickered to life, showing a reporter standing in front of a city map. Her expression was grim, and her voice sounded fearful.

"...Kita City has been completely overrun by a criminal organization known as the Outcasts. The group has taken control of the city’s main gates, communication and teleportation towers, and administrative buildings..."

A few moments later, the screen switched to footage of the city. Smoke rose from several districts, and the streets were empty. Several black-robed figures could be seen walking around with their bonded beasts.

"...The Outcasts have publicly issued their demands," the reporter continued while the screen showed a video message from the internet, posted by the Outcasts. "They want the Empire to release all captured members of their organization, including the son of their leader. Additionally, they demand compensation for their deceased comrade and the handover of the one responsible for their death. If their demands are not met within twenty-four hours, they have threatened to destroy the entire city and everyone in it..."
The room fell silent. Zura stared at the screen, her expression cold. Ethea’s hands tightened on the armrests of her wheelchair.
’The one responsible for their deaths...’ Ethea thought. ’They mean Soren.’
The reporter kept talking, but neither of them was listening anymore.

"Damn these bastards," Zura hissed, her knuckles turning white as she gripped the edge of the table. "Why hasn’t the Empire wiped them out by now?! They’re openly threatening innocent lives and acting like they own the entire city!"
