chapters.title: Chapter 362: A Silent Vow
paragraphs: Meanwhile, in the Grand Kingdom of Oros, Kalmira City.

The clouds above the city parted slowly, revealing a sky that had been hidden for days. In one particular building near the city center, frost spread across the walls and windows, creeping outward in delicate patterns that shimmered under the sudden light. Inside, the hall had been transformed: a thin layer of ice coated the pillars, floor, and chandeliers, reflecting the pale glow of the figure seated at its center.

Her white hair cascaded down her back like a waterfall of snow, and when her eyes snapped open, a brilliant silver light passed through them, illuminating the frozen hall for a single heartbeat before fading. The pressure that followed pressed down on everything in the vicinity, and the guards stationed outside the hall dropped to their knees, unable to stand against the force bearing down on them.
Then, as quickly as it had come, the pressure vanished. The ice began to recede, melting away into nothing.

The woman rose from her seat, and her feet left the ground. She floated upward, stopping a few feet above the floor. She looked down at her hands, flexing her fingers as if testing them for the first time.
"...Finally," she whispered, her lips curled upward. "The 6th circle."
She hovered in the air for a moment longer before drifting gently back down, her bare feet meeting the frost-covered floor without making a sound.

Looking down at her arms, she noticed the faint layer of dark impurities lingering on her skin, a natural byproduct of purging her body’s limits during the breakthrough. With a slight twitch of her brow, she turned and headed straight toward the adjacent bath chambers.
Twenty minutes later, she emerged wearing a beautiful silver dress that complemented her pale skin and snow-white hair, which tumbled loosely over her shoulders in damp waves.
She glided toward the pavilion’s main doors, pushing them open to reveal the courtyard outside.
"Congratulations on reaching the 6th circle, Zoe."
Zoe’s eyes lit up at the sound of a familiar voice. She turned around with a smile. "Thank you, Uncl-!"
Her words stopped mid-sentence as her eyes fell onto a figure standing beside her uncle, a faint smile playing on their lips.
"M-Master!"

Zoe called out, her voice trembling with sudden excitement. Ignoring her uncle entirely, she quickly adjusted her dress and bowed with deep reverence, her earlier composure completely replaced by eager delight.
Her uncle let out a short laugh, shaking his head at her immediate shift in focus. "See? I told you she’d forget I was even standing here the moment she saw you."
"Congratulations on your breakthrough, little Zoe." The figure stepped forward, a mild smile on his face as he gestured for her to rise. "Reaching the 6th Circle at your age is no small achievement."
"Thank you, Master!" Zoe raised her head, her bright eyes shining as she looked at him. "I couldn’t have managed it without your guidance."
"...Tsk, now you’re both ignoring me," her uncle grumbled, though the smile on his face betrayed his lack of real annoyance.
Zoe ignored him again and hurried over to her master’s side, her eyes bright with excitement.
"Master, when did you get here? Was your seclusion successful? How long are you staying? There’s so much I want to talk about with you!"
Her master let out a warm laugh. "Slow down, little Zoe. I’m not going anywhere."
"Indeed," her uncle chimed in, walking over to join them. "Let’s continue this somewhere comfortable... We have a few things to tell you too.
"..." Zoe paused and finally turned to look at her uncle, her brow furrowing slightly. "What’s the matter? Did something happen?"
Her uncle nodded. "Let’s go. I’ll explain it soon."

Without another word, the three of them rose into the air and flew toward the neighboring villa. The journey took only a few minutes, and soon they landed on a wide balcony overlooking a garden. A table had been prepared with drinks and snacks, and magic lanterns had been lit around them.

They all sat down and started talking while enjoying the refreshments. Zoe learned about her master’s small breakthrough, the reason he came here, and how long he was going to stay. She then told him about her life and progress over the past few years. She also talked about meeting some people who might surprise him, glancing at her uncle, wondering if he hadn’t spilled the beans yet.
"...Tsk, stop glaring at me." Her uncle, Craig, set his cup down with a sigh. "The old man already knows, both the boy and her."
Zoe’s shoulders dropped. She turned to her master with a look of mild disappointment. "Did you meet them already, Master?"
The old man nodded, a faint smile on his lips. "The boy was indeed as good as you said. Perhaps even better." He paused, then glanced at Craig. "But..."

Craig let out another sigh, already knowing what was coming. "Of course, the explaining is left to me. Fine." He turned to Zoe. "You might want to sit back. This is a long story. And if you interrupt, I won’t tell you anything else."
"Ok, ok, I promise." Zoe nodded half-heartedly, already fidgeting in her seat. "Hurry up!"
Craig gave her a look, then began. He told her everything, starting from meeting with Soren till the incident and the aftermath. He left out a few details he couldn’t reveal to her and soon finished.
Zoe had managed to keep her promise, though her expression had changed a dozen times throughout the story. Shock, worry, relief, anger, and everything in between had crossed her face in waves.
"So much happened," she muttered, her head lowered. "And I wasn’t there for any of it."
Craig and her master, Hector, exchanged a glance but chose to stay silent.
A moment later, Zoe raised her head. "How much time has passed since I went into seclusion?"
"...Almost two months," Craig replied.
"...Then, do you know where they went?"
Craig didn’t answer. He just looked at her, his expression unreadable. Hector watched the exchange in silence, sipping his tea.
"Why do you want to know?" Craig finally asked.
Zoe blinked. "What do you mean, why? It’s because I want to see them... I want to help. After everything you just told me, how could I just sit here and do nothing?"

"...Is your relationship with them that close?" Craig asked, his tone flat. "You were with them for barely a month. Yes, the boy helped you, and yes, you owe him for that. But he’s already been compensated more than he deserves. So stop worrying about them and focus on stabilizing your cultivation. You just broke through, so that should be your priority right now."
"..." Zoe stared at him, her expression unreadable. Then her eyes narrowed. "You’re hiding something, aren’t you?"
Craig’s expression didn’t change. "What makes you say that?"
"Because you’re never this cold about people I care about. You’re always the first one to support me when I want to help someone. So why now?" She leaned forward. "Whataren’t you telling me?"

"...I’m only doing this for your own good, Zoe," Craig replied after a moment. "It is dangerous to get involved with them anymore. If you really want to pay them back yourself, just text them or send them some money; it will be more than enough. There’s no need to go looking for them in person."
Zoe stared at her uncle for a long moment, then let out a slow breath and leaned back in her chair. Her expression softened, though her eyes still held a hint of stubbornness.
"...I understand what you’re saying," she admitted. "You’re right. I only knew them for a month. It’s not like we’re lifelong friends or anything."
Craig nodded, relieved she was seeing reason.
"But," she continued, "that month was enough for me to know what kind of people they are. And I don’t think I’m wrong about them."
Craig sighed. "I never said you were wrong. I just said it’s dangerous."
"Then let me ask you this," Zoe said, turning to face him fully. "Is it dangerous because of who they are, or... because of who’s after them?"

"...You’re too perceptive for your own good," Craig muttered after a moment. "But since you know about it now, you should realize why I’m so worried. The people targeting them are more powerful and sinister than you can imagine. The gate incident is proof of that. I..." He paused, his voice dropping. "You’re the only family I have left, Zoe. Your parents entrusted you to me before they passed. I don’t want to lose you too, especially over a fight that isn’t even yours."
"Uncle..."
"So, please forget about them." He stood up from his chair, his expression hardening. "If you refuse, then forget about having an uncle and do whatever you want."
"Uncle!" Zoe called out, rising from her chair.
But he didn’t look back. He stepped off the balcony and disappeared into the night sky, leaving her standing there, hand half-raised.
"Uncle..."
She stood frozen for a long moment, unsure what to do.
"He’s right, little Zoe."
"Master?" She turned to Hector, her eyes pleading for a different answer, but Hector only shook his head.

"I don’t want to see you throw your life away either." He muttered, his expression unreadable. "The reality is that even I can’t offer them much help against forces like these. I think the best thing you can do right now is get stronger and focus on your own path."
"I’m certain they wouldn’t want you putting yourself in unnecessary danger for their sake, too."
"...I understand." Zoe lowered her head, her voice subdued. "I’ll focus on my cultivation, and I hope you’ll help me with it, Master."
Hector nodded, satisfied with her answer. "Good. Then let’s get started tomorrow. We have a lot of work to do."
"Mm." Zoe nodded, but her gaze drifted toward the night sky where her uncle had disappeared. She didn’t say anything else, but deep down, she made a silent promise.

’...I’ll get stronger. Strong enough that they won’t have to worry about me. Strong enough to make my own choices. And strong enough to make sure no one can ever hurt the people I care about again...’

He left out a few details he couldn’t reveal to her and soon finished.
Zoe had managed to keep her promise, though her expression had changed a dozen times throughout the story.
Shock, worry, relief, anger, and everything in between had crossed her face in waves.
"So much happened," she muttered, her head lowered.
"And I wasn’t there for any of it."
Craig and her master, Hector, exchanged a glance but chose to stay silent.
A moment later, Zoe raised her head.
"How much time has passed since I went into seclusion?"
"...Almost two months," Craig replied.
"...Then, do you know where they went?"
Craig didn’t answer.
He just looked at her, his expression unreadable.
Hector watched the exchange in silence, sipping his tea.
"Why do you want to know?" Craig finally asked.
Zoe blinked.
"What do you mean, why?
It’s because I want to see them...
I want to help.
After everything you just told me, how could I just sit here and do nothing?"
"...Is your relationship with them that close?" Craig asked, his tone flat.
"You were with them for barely a month.
Yes, the boy helped you, and yes, you owe him for that.
But he’s already been compensated more than he deserves.
So stop worrying about them and focus on stabilizing your cultivation.
You just broke through, so that should be your priority right now."
"..." Zoe stared at him, her expression unreadable.
Then her eyes narrowed.
"You’re hiding something, aren’t you?"
Craig’s expression didn’t change.
"What makes you say that?"
"Because you’re never this cold about people I care about.
You’re always the first one to support me when I want to help someone.
So why now?" She leaned forward.
"Whataren’t you telling me?"
"...I’m only doing this for your own good, Zoe," Craig replied after a moment.
"It is dangerous to get involved with them anymore.
If you really want to pay them back yourself, just text them or send them some money; it will be more than enough.
There’s no need to go looking for them in person."
Zoe stared at her uncle for a long moment, then let out a slow breath and leaned back in her chair.
Her expression softened, though her eyes still held a hint of stubbornness.
"...I understand what you’re saying," she admitted.
"You’re right.
I only knew them for a month.
It’s not like we’re lifelong friends or anything."
Craig nodded, relieved she was seeing reason.
"But," she continued, "that month was enough for me to know what kind of people they are.
And I don’t think I’m wrong about them."
Craig sighed.
"I never said you were wrong.
I just said it’s dangerous."
"Then let me ask you this," Zoe said, turning to face him fully.
"Is it dangerous because of who they are, or... because of who’s after them?"
"...You’re too perceptive for your own good," Craig muttered after a moment.
"But since you know about it now, you should realize why I’m so worried.
The people targeting them are more powerful and sinister than you can imagine.
The gate incident is proof of that.
I..." He paused, his voice dropping.
"You’re the only family I have left, Zoe.
Your parents entrusted you to me before they passed.
I don’t want to lose you too, especially over a fight that isn’t even yours."
"Uncle..."
"So, please forget about them." He stood up from his chair, his expression hardening.
"If you refuse, then forget about having an uncle and do whatever you want."
"Uncle!" Zoe called out, rising from her chair.
But he didn’t look back.
He stepped off the balcony and disappeared into the night sky, leaving her standing there, hand half-raised.
"Uncle..."
She stood frozen for a long moment, unsure what to do.
"He’s right, little Zoe."
"Master?" She turned to Hector, her eyes pleading for a different answer, but Hector only shook his head.
"I don’t want to see you throw your life away either." He muttered, his expression unreadable.
"The reality is that even I can’t offer them much help against forces like these.
I think the best thing you can do right now is get stronger and focus on your own path."
"I’m certain they wouldn’t want you putting yourself in unnecessary danger for their sake, too."
"...I understand." Zoe lowered her head, her voice subdued.
"I’ll focus on my cultivation, and I hope you’ll help me with it, Master."
Hector nodded, satisfied with her answer.
"Good.
Then let’s get started tomorrow.
We have a lot of work to do."
"Mm." Zoe nodded, but her gaze drifted toward the night sky where her uncle had disappeared.
She didn’t say anything else, but deep down, she made a silent promise.
’...I’ll get stronger.
Strong enough that they won’t have to worry about me.
Strong enough to make my own choices.
And strong enough to make sure no one can ever hurt the people I care about again...’

[Target: Zoe Marron]
[Analyzing Investment...]
[Investment: You helped the target reach a breakthrough state by preparing specifically tailored food that stabilized her condition and provided the necessary foundation for advancement.]
[Analyzing target response...]

[Evaluating investment significance...]
[Evaluation complete.]
[Investment Grade: SUPREME]
[Calculating returns...]
[Calculation complete.]
[Applying Authority Modifier: Amplification (Passive) — Baseline bonus applied. Reward tier scaling upgraded.]
[Returns granted:]
[1. Mana/Mana Capacity +100,000]
[2. Cooking Mastery +1]
[3. Ice Serpent Spear Arts]
[Integration initiated...]
[Integration Complete!]
"Huff..."
Soren took a deep breath and opened his eyes. With a mental command, the messages disappeared from his vision.
’...Thank goodness she broke through successfully.’
He thought as he slowly stood and stretched.

With so much time since her retreat began, a knot of worry had been forming in the back of his mind. She was talented, but breakthroughs were never guaranteed, especially in higher circles, where too many things could go wrong. Knowing she’d made it past that threshold lifted a huge weight off his mind.
’But the returns were greater than I expected.’
Perhaps it was because it was really a big investment from him at that time.

Neverthless, he was more than satisfied. The one hundred thousand mana and mana capacity boost was substantial. No, in fact, it might be the biggest mana-related return he had gotten so far. And his guess was the same as earlier: that the scale of the returns depended on the significance and time of the investment.
’Or I could be overthinking again.’ He shook his head and moved on.
Since cooking was involved, the cooking mastery increase was expected. But the last return truly exceeded his expectations. ’Ice Serpent Spear Arts, huh...’

It was precisely what he needed right now. His Glacial Edge technique was only C-Rank, and he had been feeling its limits for a while now. This new spear style was an A-Rank technique, carrying enough depth and raw power to carry him comfortably all the way until the 6th or even the 7th Circle.
’I will ask Ethea to train with me in the Mental Realm later.’ He smiled and nodded to himself. Then, he opened the bedroom door and made his way back to the living room.
However, just as he entered, he noticed the tense atmosphere. Ethea and Zura were both glued to the TV, their expressions rigid.
"What’s wrong?" he asked as he walked toward them.
The two women finally noticed him, and their expressions shifted.
"Dear!"
"Mr. Soren!"
"It’s the Outcasts," Ethea said, her voice tight.
Soren raised a brow as a bad feeling rose in his chest. He walked over and sat down beside her, his eyes fixed on the screen. "Can you explain more clearly?"
The two women nodded and took turns filling him in.
"...I see," Soren muttered, glancing at the still-running live news program. "Although I expected them to try to rescue their young master and other members, I didn’t expect them to go this far."

Ethea and Zura nodded, sharing the same view. They were more familiar with the Outcasts than he was and knew they wouldn’t dare go overboard like this. There must be a reason for it, a pretty obvious one, in fact.

"It’s because of their young master, isn’t it?" Soren spoke out loud their thoughts. "He must be more important than I thought... But then again, considering how respectful those guys were to him and how spoiled he acted, it somewhat makes sense too. Perhaps he is the only child or something."
"Yeah, I thought so too," Zura spoke up first, her fists clenched. "But I still can’t believe it. They’re practically begging for an all-out war."
"...No," Ethea spoke up next. "The Empire won’t go to war unless absolutely necessary. And I think there is a hidden reason why they haven’t been hunted down yet."
"You mean..." Soren trailed off, guessing what she meant. "They have backing? Someone powerful enough to shield them from the Empire’s full attention."

Ethea nodded. "It’s the only explanation that makes sense. The Outcasts have been operating for years without being wiped out. That doesn’t happen unless someone with influence is protecting them. Besides, do you remember the news after the incident in Bagdad? The Empire responded appropriately, but they didn’t say anything concrete about searching for and punishing the rest of the Outcasts."

"...Now that you said it, it does indeed sound strange." Zura frowned, her expression souring. "Politics is so complicated and... distasteful. I wish the current Emperor was as ruthless as Emperor Temur."
"Zura," Ethea called out, shaking her head. "Be careful with your words."

"I know, I know." Zura sighed. "But it’s true, isn’t it? If we had someone like Emperor Temur on the throne, the Outcasts would have been wiped out years ago. No, in fact, they wouldn’t have been able to grow this large in the first place."

"Perhaps." Ethea didn’t argue the point. "But there’s another reason, too. You know the Outcasts’ leader is a powerful Sovereign. If he goes all out, he can cause tremendous damage to the Empire. Unless a Paragon intervenes directly, taking him down isn’t easy. That’s likely one of the reasons they’ve survived this long." She paused. "...And I think the Imperial Family will act this time. The Outcasts are blatantly threatening them now, after all. If they value their honor and reputation, they definitely won’t ignore it."
"Hmm, I hope they do, or else the academy will have to intervene again..."

Soren listened to Ethea’s words and nodded in agreement. But he had his own thoughts. He guessed the Imperial Family, namely the current Emperor, might have just contacted Paragon of Order, Lord Temur, and asked him to take care of them, but probably didn’t because they didn’t want to look incompetent or appear weak in front of other people.
’Or perhaps Paragon of Order is extremely busy, and they don’t want to disturb him... Yeah, sounds convenient...’
Soren leaned back against the chair, his mind racing.

After thinking more deeply, he felt Lord Temur was already fully aware of what was unfolding. A Paragon’s reach was vast, and a man of his caliber undoubtedly possessed extensive intelligence networks and loyal subordinates who reported directly to him on every major or even minor threat within the realm.
Yet, he hadn’t taken action.
’...Is he waiting for the right moment?’ He wondered. ’Or... is this all part of another larger board game?’

chapters.title: Chapter 364: Trouble
paragraphs: ’...I really hope they won’t hand over the captives.’ Ethea talked to Soren via their bond. ’If such a thing happens, you will end up being targeted by them and...’
She trailed off, but Soren understood what she was trying to say.

He was the one who killed Sevihan, the Puppeteer, and captured their young master, Lucent, along with the other two, Leech and Nullifier. Worse yet, those two might know about Ethea’s existence since they worked with Sevihan. If the Empire surrendered the captives to satisfy the Outcasts, both Soren and Ethea would immediately have massive targets on their backs.
And while the chance was slim, he couldn’t completely rule out the possibility that the Empire might also hand him over to ’keep the peace’. When politics were involved, nothing was ever guaranteed.

Then again, Princess Roya, Commander Ervin, and Lord Asad promised to keep the matter a secret, and probably weren’t the type to betray. Only the other people present at the scene, the elves, the other knights, and the princess’s personal guards were the ones he couldn’t completely vouch for.

’...No.’ He shook his head, reminding himself not to be naive. The Princess and Lord Asad had their integrity and big reasons not to betray them, but the rest were loyal to the Empire above all else. If an order came down from the higher-ups to sacrifice an outsider for the greater good, they wouldn’t hesitate to obey.
Just then, Zura spoke up, breaking the heavy silence. "Why did you two quiet down all of a sudden?"
Soren looked up and shook his head lightly. "I was just thinking about how the Empire will handle this situation, and... the possibility that I might get involved."

"You?" Zura raised a brow. A moment later, a flash of realization passed through her eyes. "Yeah, I doubted you just sat on the sidelines during that incident, as the news suggested. I guess you played a big role then?"
"He’s the one who subdued almost all of the outcasts," Ethea spoke up before Soren could answer.

Soren turned toward her and nodded. Ethea then briefly explained the true events of the incident, leaving Zura stunned as the full scope of what Soren had accomplished finally sank in. She turned to Soren, her gaze filled with shock and a sliver of doubt.
"You... defeated the Hollow Pair? The Leech and the Nullifier? O-On your own?"

"It wasn’t easy," Soren answered. "I had help from Commander Ervin and others who held off the Leech and the possessed long enough for me to take out the Nullifier first. But yes, that’s what happened."
"..." Zura fell silent, her mouth slightly open.

Truthfully, she had written him off until now, viewing his strength through the lens of a typical 4th Circle cultivator and treating him primarily as a skilled magic chef. She had even privately categorized him as weak compared to the people she usually dealt with in her line of work.

Nobody could really blame her for thinking that way, either. Being at the 4th Circle at his age was completely ordinary, the literal definition of average. In fact, most of her students were at the same Circle as him, with some even surpassing him.

On top of that, he never carried himself like a warrior. He gave off no sharp or threatening aura and lacked the keen edge of seasoned combatants. He just looked like an ordinary guy who’d been exceptionally lucky enough to marry Ethea.

Yet the Hollow Pair were absolute nightmarish entities. They were the kind of threat that made seasoned, high-ranking veterans break into a cold sweat, fighters who could strip away your advantages and grind you down before you even realized what hit you.
For a 4th Circle chef like him to not only survive an encounter with them, but to actively dismantle them and walk away victorious, was nothing short of absurd.
’...Could it be he’s not a 4th Circle cultivator but higher?’

The thought struck her like a sudden bolt. Right, perhaps he was hiding his true strength using some high-grade concealment artifact. It was the only logical explanation for how anyone could pull off a feat like that.

"!" She was about to voice the theory, but the words caught in her throat as she recalled what Soren himself had told her. While talking about his sister, he had explicitly mentioned that he’d been unawakened for most of his life, exiled by his family, and only recently awakened.
If he had barely started cultivating a few months ago, then how was any of this possible?
"Just who are you...?"
The words slipped out before she could stop herself.
"Me?" Soren pointed at himself and chuckled. "I’m just an ordinary guy who was lucky to achieve where I am today. Nothing more, nothing less."
"What exactly does that mean?" Zura frowned, but as she picked up on the subtle shift in their emotions, she realized she was prying into matters far too personal.
"Ah... sorry," she mumbled, backing off quickly. "F-Forget I asked. That was out of line."
"It’s fine, it’s natural to be curious," Soren dismissed her apology with a small gesture. "Truth is, I just happen to have a unique physique. That’s the main reason I managed to handle those two."
"I... I see," Zura said, letting out a breath as the explanation somewhat settled the absurdity of it all.

An awkward silence fell over the room as Zura cursed herself internally for making things so uncomfortable. She had let her shock get the better of her, blurting out questions that clearly touched on sensitive ground.
"So," Soren was the first to break the ice, "what should we do then? Should we prepare for a worst-case scenario just in case?"
Ethea nodded after a moment’s thought. "I think we should."

"I-If it comes to that, you don’t have to face it alone," Zura chimed in, seizing the chance to pivot away from her earlier blunder. "The Academy can protect you if anything goes wrong. We have five Sovereigns, and every single one of them is an absolute powerhouse. Not even the Outcasts would be foolish enough to mess with us on our home ground. We can even summon Principal’s Avatar if things get out of hand."
"...Thank you," Soren said with a slight smile. "That’s a great safety net, and it’s reassuring to know we have that option."
He paused, glancing over at Ethea before meeting Zura’s gaze again.

"Still, staying locked up here forever isn’t realistic," he continued. "We can’t just hide behind the Academy’s walls indefinitely. Besides, if the Outcasts decide to come after us anyway, staying put just puts every innocent student on campus right in the crosshairs."
"...I’ll reach out to Princess Roya," Ethea added.
"Right!" At the sound of that name, Zura’s eyes lit up instantly. "That’s actually a great idea. I almost forgot you were close with her. "

"Mm." Ethea nodded and took her phone from Soren’s hand. She tapped rapidly on the screen, typed a concise message, and sent it off. She locked the device and rested it on her lap. "Now, we can only wait."
"In that case, let me bring the desserts," Soren said, standing up. "No point letting good food go to waste while we wait."
"Ah, no..." Zura wanted to stop him, but he had already left before she could finish.

She slumped back in her seat, finding it hard to muster an appetite when the situation hung so heavily over them. Yet, as she stared at the empty doorway, logic slowly won out. There was nothing more they could do right now anyway. Spiraling into anxiety would only wear them down for whatever might come next. Besides, for all they knew, they were just overthinking the whole thing and stressing over shadows.
"...Yeah, I really hope we are overthinking it." She muttered, exchanging a glance with Ethea. "I’m sorry for bringing the mood down. This was supposed to be a nice dinner."

Ethea shook her head. "You didn’t do anything. But you’re right, this was supposed to be a nice dinner. A nice dinner for you. So please, stop feeling guilty and finish your food." She paused, then added with a teasing smile. "Or... are you going to admit defeat?"
Zura blinked, then burst out laughing. "Haha~. You’ve really changed, haha~."
"For the better, right?"
"Mm, I liked the past you, but I like the current you even more."
Just then, Soren returned with a tray of desserts in his hands. He set them down on the table and looked between the two women.
"Did I miss something?" he asked, pretending he hadn’t heard anything. "Can I join in, or is this a private club?"
"It’s women’s talk," Zura said with a smirk, playing right along with his act. "So, unfortunately, you can’t join."

"Ah, what a shame," Soren sighed in fake disappointment, though his lips twitched with amusement. He quickly cheered himself up, pulling out a chair and gesturing toward the sweet treats on the table. "Guess I’ll just have to win you over with these instead."
"Hehe, I’ll be the judge of that then~."

"Ah... sorry," she mumbled, backing off quickly.
"F-Forget I asked.
That was out of line."
"It’s fine, it’s natural to be curious," Soren dismissed her apology with a small gesture.
"Truth is, I just happen to have a unique physique.
That’s the main reason I managed to handle those two."
I see," Zura said, letting out a breath as the explanation somewhat settled the absurdity of it all.
An awkward silence fell over the room as Zura cursed herself internally for making things so uncomfortable.
She had let her shock get the better of her, blurting out questions that clearly touched on sensitive ground.
"So," Soren was the first to break the ice, "what should we do then?
Should we prepare for a worst-case scenario just in case?"
Ethea nodded after a moment’s thought.
"I think we should."
"I-If it comes to that, you don’t have to face it alone," Zura chimed in, seizing the chance to pivot away from her earlier blunder.
"The Academy can protect you if anything goes wrong.
We have five Sovereigns, and every single one of them is an absolute powerhouse.
Not even the Outcasts would be foolish enough to mess with us on our home ground.
We can even summon Principal’s Avatar if things get out of hand."
"...Thank you," Soren said with a slight smile.
"That’s a great safety net, and it’s reassuring to know we have that option."
He paused, glancing over at Ethea before meeting Zura’s gaze again.
"Still, staying locked up here forever isn’t realistic," he continued.
"We can’t just hide behind the Academy’s walls indefinitely.
Besides, if the Outcasts decide to come after us anyway, staying put just puts every innocent student on campus right in the crosshairs."
"...I’ll reach out to Princess Roya," Ethea added.
"Right!" At the sound of that name, Zura’s eyes lit up instantly.
"That’s actually a great idea.
I almost forgot you were close with her.
"Mm." Ethea nodded and took her phone from Soren’s hand.
She tapped rapidly on the screen, typed a concise message, and sent it off.
She locked the device and rested it on her lap.
"Now, we can only wait."
"In that case, let me bring the desserts," Soren said, standing up.
"No point letting good food go to waste while we wait."
"Ah, no..." Zura wanted to stop him, but he had already left before she could finish.
She slumped back in her seat, finding it hard to muster an appetite when the situation hung so heavily over them.
Yet, as she stared at the empty doorway, logic slowly won out.
There was nothing more they could do right now anyway.
Spiraling into anxiety would only wear them down for whatever might come next.
Besides, for all they knew, they were just overthinking the whole thing and stressing over shadows.
"...Yeah, I really hope we are overthinking it." She muttered, exchanging a glance with Ethea.
"I’m sorry for bringing the mood down.
This was supposed to be a nice dinner."
Ethea shook her head.
"You didn’t do anything.
But you’re right, this was supposed to be a nice dinner.
A nice dinner for you.
So please, stop feeling guilty and finish your food." She paused, then added with a teasing smile.
"Or... are you going to admit defeat?"
Zura blinked, then burst out laughing.
"Haha~.
You’ve really changed, haha~."
"For the better, right?"
"Mm, I liked the past you, but I like the current you even more."
Just then, Soren returned with a tray of desserts in his hands.
He set them down on the table and looked between the two women.
"Did I miss something?" he asked, pretending he hadn’t heard anything.
"Can I join in, or is this a private club?"
"It’s women’s talk," Zura said with a smirk, playing right along with his act.
"So, unfortunately, you can’t join."
"Ah, what a shame," Soren sighed in fake disappointment, though his lips twitched with amusement.
He quickly cheered himself up, pulling out a chair and gesturing toward the sweet treats on the table.
"Guess I’ll just have to win you over with these instead."
"Hehe, I’ll be the judge of that then~."

chapters.title: Chapter 365: The Empire’s Response [1]
paragraphs: They ate desserts while talking about other topics. Soren used the chance to tell her about Ryan’s arrival and what time it would be ok to take him to the academy, and so on.

Eventually, the dinner came to an end; however, there was no reply from the princess. Since it was already past nine, Zura decided to take her leave. She stood up, smoothing down her clothes before turning to face Soren and Ethea.

"Contact me right away if anything happens," she instructed, her voice laced with genuine concern. "Although we are going to meet up tomorrow at the appointed time, don’t hesitate to reach out if something comes up before then."
"We will," Ethea nodded. "Get home safely."
"Have a good night." Soren waved with his free hand.
"Mm, you two have a good night," Zura replied with a small wave, stepping out into the hallway as the door gently closed behind her.

Soren and Ethea turned back toward the living room. Soren made quick work of clearing away the empty plates and cleaning up the kitchen while Ethea helped him as much as she could with her significantly improved mental power. Once everything was settled, they went through their usual routine before heading off to bed as the long day drew to a close.
Soren told Ethea to go to sleep and that he would wake her up if Princess replied or anything happened. Ethea reluctantly agreed and went to ’sleep’.

Soren then asked Malakor to keep an eye on their surroundings and alert him if he sensed anything, good or bad, and began cultivating himself. However, he couldn’t bring himself to fully relax. Every ten minutes, he paused to check Ethea’s phone and scroll through the latest news feeds, staying alert for any development.

Just like that, five hours slipped by in constant vigilance. At around 2:30 AM, a notification finally lit up the screen. It was a reply from the Princess. Soren immediately set his phone aside and went over to wake Ethea, gently shaking her shoulder. She opened her eyes right away, and together, they read the message.
[Greetings, Ethea,]it read.[First, I must apologize for replying at such a late hour. I was tied up handling urgent matters regarding Kita City and the Outcasts."]
The text went on to reassure them.

[The overall situation is a bit complicated at the moment, but rest assured, under no circumstances will we hand over the captives to them. We will not comply with whatever demands they make. Furthermore, your involvement is being kept completely confidential on our end to ensure your protection... I will contact you again soon with more details. Stay safe.]
As soon as they finished reading, they looked at each other, their lips curling up.
"I knew we could trust the princess." Soren sighed in relief.
"Mmm." Ethea nodded and asked. "Is there any news about Kita City?

Soren nodded, his expression turning grave as he recalled the late-night feeds. "Empire forces have completely surrounded the area, but the Outcasts dropped a pitch-black barrier over the whole sector. They’re threatening to tear the entire city apart the moment our troops make a single wrong move."
"I see..." Ethea muttered and fell silent. "...Since the problem seems to be solved, we should take a rest and prepare for tommo-I mean, the day ahead."
Soren chuckled and gave her a light kiss. ’Don’t forget to sleep, dear. Although your mind might be fine, your body still needs rest.’
’...Understood.’ Ethea smiled as their lips parted. ’Then I will go back to sleep now.’
’Mm. I will wake you up myself.’

Soren smiled, and only after confirming she had drifted off to real sleep did he sit back up. He then reached into his spatial storage and pulled out a fresh batch of mana stones, surrounding himself with their vibrant energy.

With threats closing in on every side, breaking through to the 5th Circle as fast as possible was no longer just a goal - it was essential for survival. He closed his eyes and began drawing the energy into his core. Thanks to the triple cultivation speed boost from their Eternal Bond, he absorbed the surrounding mana at a pace far beyond anything he had managed before. At the same time, his Core Refinement technique worked continuously, compressing and liquefying the rapid influx of power into pure, dense reserves.
’At this rate,’ Soren thought, feeling the immense volume of power surging through his channels, ’if I hit the Gates with Ryan this week, reaching the 5th Circle shouldn’t be an issue.’
With that in mind, he closed his eyes and plunged into deep cultivation.

Meanwhile, in the capital city of the Temur Empire, Samarend, the highest-ranking individuals in the empire were gathered around a large round table. Generals in decorated uniforms, officials in formal robes, and a few holographic figures who were attending remotely from distant posts. The atmosphere was thick with tension.

"What are we even waiting for, and why are we wasting so much time?" A deep voice rumbled from the far end of the table, rough with age and agitation. "While they’re all in one place, we should crush them. I’ll lead the charge myself if I have to. Just give me enough barrier masters and spatial mages to protect the civilians from the fallout."

"And what fallout would that be?" Another voice cut in, each word placed carefully. "The one where the whole city burns? The one where they slaughter every hostage the moment we attack? You’re so eager to swing your sword that you’ve forgotten what’s at stake. We don’t even know how they took over the city and have the guts to act like they can kill everyone there easily."
"Then what do you suggest?" The first voice retorted.

"I think we should play along with their demands," the second voice replied. "We will negotiate, exchange the captives, and secure the safety of the city first. Once the barrier is down and the citizens are safe, we strike with everything we have and round up every last one of them."

"I think you meant we will let them slip right through our fingers." A third voice joined, mocking. "If we show them even a shred of compliance, they will take those captives and vanish into thin air. All the blood and effort we spent dragging those criminals into chains will be completely wasted. In fact, we hold the real leverage here. We should pull out their leader’s son and threaten to execute him on the spot unless they tear down that barrier and release the city."

"N-No!" The second voice snapped, dropping all its previous composure. "Are you out of your mind? Do you have any idea how insane those lunatics are? You try to threaten them with a hostage, especially their young master; they will not only surrender but also massacre every single person in that city, just to make a point."

"I agree with him," one of the holographic figures chimed in. "The Outcasts do whatever they want, and they don’t care about consequences that much. Threatening the boy will only accelerate the destruction of the city."

"So what then? We just sit on our hands while they dictate terms to the entire Empire?" The first voice’s owner, an old general, slammed his heavy palm down on the round table, making the tactical projections jitter. "Every minute we waste bickering in this room gives them more time to fortify their position. If we give them back their people, we lose all our leverage for good!"

The argument went back and forth with no sign of resolution. Voices rose, fists struck the table, and the holographic figures flickered as their owners argued. Only a few people kept silent throughout the discussion, their eyes fixed on the head of the table where a figure sat with an unreadable expression.

It was a middle-aged man wearing robes of deep gold with intricate embroidery running along the collar and sleeves. He sat perfectly still, back straight, hands resting on the armrests of his throne-like chair. His face was angular, with a strong jaw and a nose that looked like it had been broken once and set well. His pale golden eyes, like molten glass, were fixed on the argument unfolding before him, without a hint of what he was thinking.
On his head rested a crown that caught the eye the moment you looked at him, its design evoking the image of a rising sun without directly depicting it.
He narrowed his eyes, tracking the escalating noise across the room, and tapped his index finger once against the surface of the table.

In an instant, the room fell silent, as though every voice had been swallowed whole. The generals, who had been shouting moments earlier, froze mid-sentence, mouths still open and forming words, but no sound emerged.
Realizing what had happened, a few swallowed hard while the others straightened in their chairs, suddenly aware of how out of line they had been.
All eyes locked onto him.

chapters.title: Chapter 366: The Empire’s Response [2]
paragraphs: "...We are the Temur Empire. The strongest power on this continent." The figure spoke, his voice flat and deceptively soft, yet carrying to every corner of the silent room. "Yet, looking at the ’leaders’ of our high command bickering like street thugs over a handful of terrorists, one would think we are on the brink of collapse."

His pale golden eyes swept across the room, tracking every individual present. Under his gaze, those who had been shouting moments earlier lowered their heads. Their faces paled, sweat beading on their brows, and no one dared meet his eyes.

"Hah..." The figure let out a disappointed sigh and tapped a finger on the table again. The next moment, sound returned to the room. The faint shuffle of feet, the rustle of fabric, the sound of someone swallowing a bit too loudly. A few let out breaths they had been holding.
"Dayyan," the figure called out, "I will leave this to you."

All eyes fell on the figure standing behind the emperor. A young man who bore a striking resemblance to him. He had the same black hair and sharp features, though his eyes were a different color entirely, a deep crimson that stood out against his pale skin.
Dayyan stepped forward and inclined his head. "As you command, My Liege."

He turned to face the table, his gaze sweeping over the gathered generals and officials. "I want to inform everyone that the rescue operation is already underway, led by the Shadow Emperor Zayn himself. The shadow unit and specialized rescue team were deployed to Kita City an hour ago, and they should be executing their orders as we speak."

The reactions were immediate. Some of the generals’ eyes widened in shock. Others exchanged glances, clearly caught off guard by how quickly things had moved. A few remained unmoved, their expressions neutral, as if they had already known or expected nothing less.

Dayyan continued without pause. "Furthermore, in case the Outcasts plan on retaliating after we rescue the hostages, defense barriers have been activated in every major city across the Empire. As for the captives, we are transferring them to a secure location. The trial will proceed as scheduled, and no amount of outside pressure will change that."
He let the words settle, then added one final piece.
"That is all I had to say. If you have any questions or concerns, I am ready to hear them."
Silence stretched across the council chamber. Nobody wanted to risk breaking the fragile order, especially with the Emperor sitting right behind Dayyan.

After a few quiet seconds, one of the older officials carefully raised his hand and spoke up. "Your Highness, securing the cities and rescuing the hostages solves the immediate crisis, but what about the long-term threat? We cannot keep our cities under defense barriers forever. What is our plan regarding the Outcasts themselves? Especially their leader?
Dayyan met his gaze with a calm, unwavering expression. "The barrier deployment is merely a temporary precaution. Once the hostages are clear, our next steps will be made known."
He kept his tone neutral, intentionally hiding the fact that the secret annihilation operation was already in motion. Revealing that would only tip off the traitor seated among them.
"And to the esteemed sovereigns present, we may need your assistance soon. I hope you will stand by and remain available."

His gaze moved across the room, pausing briefly on each of the figures he addressed. When his eyes reached the holographic figure of a woman at the far end of the table, he let his gaze linger for a moment longer than the others before stepping back and returning to his position.
The entire hall remained silent, no one daring to raise a question or utter another word.
The crowned figure looked over the silent room one last time before resting his hand back on the armrest.
"The council is adjourned. You may all leave."

One by one, the figures in the room rose, bowed their heads, and filed out. The holographic displays flickered off. The doors closed behind the last person, leaving only the crowned figure and Dayyan alone.
...Tap.
The crowned figure tapped his finger on the table and turned to Dayyan. "...Did you find out anything?"
Dayyan lowered his head. "No, Father. I apologize for my incompetence. The mole is still among us, and I have yet to identify them."
"...My expectations are high for you," the crowned figure muttered a moment later. "I hope you won’t disappoint me.
Dayyan bowed his head even lower, his gaze fixed on the floor. "Understood, My Liege."

The Emperor began to rise from his throne, but before he could stand fully, the heavy doors at the back of the chamber swung open. A figure stepped into the hall, her hurried footsteps breaking the room’s stillness.
Dayyan raised a brow, his red eyes narrowing in surprise as he recognized her. "Roya? Why are you here?"
Roya stopped a few paces away and bowed respectfully to both figures. "Forgive the sudden intrusion, Father, Brother. But I have just uncovered critical information regarding the captives."
She looked directly at her father and spoke in a solemn tone. "The captive Lucent’s true family name is Starlight."

"...Starlight?" Dayyan’s brow furrowed as his crimson eyes locked onto her. "Are you trying to say he is connected to the Starlight family? Before that, where did you even get this information, and can you prove it is accurate?"
Roya met her brother’s gaze calmly. "I learned it from a trusted source. I cannot disclose who, but I can assure you the information is highly accurate."
Dayyan wasn’t satisfied. "Let’s say it’s true. But what does it prove? You should know that the Starlight family fell decades ago."

"I know, and that’s why I researched it before coming here," Roya explained. "And I managed to discover an interesting clue. The current head of the Assen family had a younger sister. She was married off to the Starlight family a few years before they fell."
Dayyan raised a brow and gestured for her to continue.

"Her whereabouts after the Starlight house fell are unknown. And..." Roya paused. "I am not entirely sure, but I believe the captive Lucent must be her child. And if that is true, then the Assen family head almost certainly knows it too."
"You mean the Assen family head is the traitor?" Dayyan asked, then fell silent, turning to the crowned figure whose lips curled faintly. ’...I see.’

Dayyan wasn’t satisfied.
"Let’s say it’s true.
But what does it prove?
You should know that the Starlight family fell decades ago."
"I know, and that’s why I researched it before coming here," Roya explained.
"And I managed to discover an interesting clue.
The current head of the Assen family had a younger sister.
She was married off to the Starlight family a few years before they fell."
Dayyan raised a brow and gestured for her to continue.
"Her whereabouts after the Starlight house fell are unknown.
And..." Roya paused.
"I am not entirely sure, but I believe the captive Lucent must be her child.
And if that is true, then the Assen family head almost certainly knows it too."
"You mean the Assen family head is the traitor?" Dayyan asked, then fell silent, turning to the crowned figure whose lips curled faintly. ’...I see.’

chapters.title: Chapter 367: The Empire’s Response [3]
paragraphs: ’...I see.’ Dayyan muttered inwardly, realizing his little sister’s information was more than just a clue.

His mind raced as he recalled everything he knew about the Assen family. The head of the family, Jerome Assen, was the Vice Minister of Internal Affairs. On paper, he answered to the Minister, a figurehead appointed by the Emperor to oversee domestic security. However, Dayyan knew that in practice, Jerome ran the ministry. After all, every report, investigation, and deployment of internal security forces passed through his hands before reaching anyone else.

As his master, the Minister probably trusted him implicitly, leaving the operational details entirely in his care. That single gap in oversight must have let Jerome manipulate intelligence from within. If an investigation into the Outcasts grew too thorough, the reports were quietly altered. If an imperial raid threatened a major cell, troop deployments were delayed under the pretense of administrative protocol. Every mysterious leak, every stalled purge, and every strangely lenient response from the state after major incidents suddenly had a clear, singular origin.

Dayyan slowly turned his head toward the throne. "I will immediately begin a discreet investigation into Jerome Assen and his activities. If he is the mole, I will find proof before he realizes we’re onto him."
The crowned figure gave a subtle nod.

Dayyan then turned to his sister. For once, the usual coldness in his expression softened, and a faint smile crossed his lips. "Thank you, Roya. You have provided the answer we have been searching for."

Roya’s eyes widened slightly, clearly not used to receiving praise from her older brother. Then she smiled back, a genuine warmth in her expression. "I am glad I could help, Brother. Then I will take my leave and leave it in your capable hands."
She bowed once more, first to Dayyan, then to their father. The Emperor waved a hand, dismissing her. Roya turned and left the chamber.
As she walked through the empty corridor, she let out a slow breath she hadn’t realized she was holding. Her mind drifted back to the message she had received from Ethea.
’Thank you, Ethea,’ she thought, a small smile playing on her lips. ’Thanks to you, we finally have a lead. And now... you and Soren don’t have to worry about anything...’
’...The Empire will handle the rest.’
"Damn it! How long do we have to wait?" A harsh voice growled, throwing a dagger at the figure sitting opposite him.
"We have no choice but to wait, so be patient," the figure replied as they easily caught the dagger, making it disintegrate into black particles.
"Be patient? The Empire could be planning something right now while we sit here doing nothing."
"Then what do you suggest? That we attack first? Use your head. If we provoke them, they’ll retaliate. The young master’s life is at stake."
"He’s right." A female voice chimed in. "And if you don’t want to leave the group, you’d better pray the Empire gives back the Young Master. Otherwise, you are done for. No, we will all be done for."
A tense silence followed. Then another voice spoke up, quieter than the rest.
"Did we really have to ask for those things? Those three’s release? Aeshvin’s killer? The Empire will never agree to that. We’re just giving them more reasons to refuse."
"...Kukuku..."
The others snapped their heads toward the sound, their expressions souring. "Why are you laughing, you creepy bastard?" one of them asked, his voice dripping with irritation.

"...Kukuku..." The figure stepped forward slightly, the shadows clinging to the folds of his dark cloak as he let out another raspy laugh. "Kukuku... You fools haven’t realized it until now? Those extra demands are just fluff. Whether the Empire gives them up or not changes nothing. The entire point of this whole circus is simply getting the Young Master back."

The others fell silent, realizing his words indeed had some truth to them. Their young master was the most important person to the leader. More important than any of them. In fact, they knew deep down that if it came down to it, the leader would sacrifice every single one of them to save his only kin. But what could they do? Their lives were already in his hands anyway.

Just then, the door opened, and a young-looking girl stepped inside. She had a lollipop in her mouth, her eyes glued to the phone in her hand, her expression casual, as if she had just strolled in from a walk.
"What’s the matter?" one of them asked.
The girl paused and pulled the lollipop from her mouth. She licked it a few times, her gaze shifting up from the screen toward the gathered group.
"...We have a guest."

The room fell silent for a beat. A few men frowned, their hands immediately drifting toward their weapons, while others gave eager chuckles, their eyes gleaming at the prospect of violence — as if they’d been waiting for something to break the monotony.
Just then, shadows beside the girl swirled and condensed into a towering shape. A figure stepped out of the darkness and stood calmly beside her, their face hidden behind a black mask.
"I am an envoy sent by the Empire," the figure said, his voice muffled behind the mask. "And I have come to negotiate."
Those who had been eager for a fight clicked their tongues in disappointment. One of the larger men stood up, his heavy boots thudding against the floor as he walked straight toward the envoy.
He stopped a few paces away and looked down with a sneer. "We won’t negotiate with you. Our demands won’t change. Just fulfill them, and we will free the city and disappear from here."
The envoy sighed, the breath rushing against the inside of his mask.
"I said I came here to negotiate," he said, raising his gaze to meet the man’s eyes. "But I didn’t say it would be with you."

Before the man could react, a sudden surge of pressure slammed down on the room, forcing him to his knees as the floor cracked beneath his boots. The envoy looked past him, his masked gaze locking onto the others.
"Bring out someone who actually makes the decisions."

chapters.title: Chapter 368: The Empire’s Response [4]
paragraphs: [Thank you, Ethea! Thanks to your help, we managed to find out who the traitor is...]
Soren read the reply from the princess and fell into deep thought. ’So it was really a family connected to the Starlight family...’

Actually, he had been racking his mind for a way to lend a helping hand, something he could do from a distance while the Empire handled the situation in Kita City. During yesterday’s dinner with Ethea and Zura, they had discussed the Outcasts and the possibility of someone powerful backing them. That conversation had stuck with him throughout the night.

So during his occasional breaks, he had looked into everything related to the Outcasts, especially Lucent, and any families that might connect to them. That was when he found it. A fallen noble family called the Starlight family, which matched Lucent’s family name.

Soren knew it could easily be a coincidence, since several noble and ordinary families across the world shared the Starlight name. Even so, he decided to pass the clue along to the princess anyway. If it proved wrong, no harm was done, but if it turned out to be true, it would give the imperial court the missing piece they needed to pull the traitor out of the dark. And now, looking at the princess’s reply, it seemed his hunch had paid off.
’Now, we only have to wait and see...’

However, he didn’t have to wait too long. Within an hour, social media exploded with news regarding the liberation of Kita City and the fierce clash between the Outcasts and the Empire’s elite Shadow Unit, led directly by the Shadow Emperor.

Soren scrolled through the endless flood of headlines and live updates, a subtle smile curling at his lips. Although casualties were reported on both sides, the worst-case scenario, a total massacre of the city’s populace or a prolonged siege, had been successfully avoided. Half of the Outcast forces were eliminated in the strike, while the rest were taken into custody.

However, he soon furrowed his brows as he read through the list of wanted escapees. Three key figures had managed to slip through during the chaos. A young girl with a lollipop in her mouth, a bald man with a creepy smile, and a beautiful woman whose eyes were completely white, as if she were blind.
’...No, sheisblind.’ Soren thought as he recalled what he learned about the outcasts. ’If I’m not mistaken, she was an assassin too.’
...A blind assassin. It really sounded strange, but the Outcasts weren’t exactly a normal group either.
’There must be a story behind it.’ Soren guessed. ’And the bald man...’

He was a spatial mage and a scientist. The reports called him a madman who had caused a massacre in one of the Empire’s research facilities years ago. He had opened a portal during an experiment, and it had connected to a gate instead of the intended destination. The monsters poured through, and everyone in the facility died. Everyone except him. He had escaped through his own portal before the authorities arrived and had been on the run ever since.
’He must have been the one who helped them teleport during the Bagdad incident.’ Soren narrowed his eyes, and his gaze shifted to the girl with a lollipop. ’...Is she a new member?’

There was no information about her online, and Ethea had never mentioned her before. So, either his guess was correct, or she had never appeared in public or taken part in any known operations until now. Either way, she was a variable they couldn’t afford to ignore.

’I hope they will be caught soon...’ He closed his phone and set it aside. He knew that although the Empire had won this battle, it wasn’t over yet. Outcasts would surely retaliate, and there was still their leader, a Sovereign, to take care of. ’...It is going to be a brutal battle.’

He sighed deeply, his hands clenching into tight fists in his lap. A bitter weight settled in his chest. As much as he wanted to step onto the battlefield and make a real difference, he knew the harsh truth: in his current state, he was still too weak to intervene in a clash among Sovereigns, outcasts, and imperial elites.
Suppressing his frustration, he closed his eyes and resumed cultivating. Soon after, Malakor’s voice echoed in his mind.
’Master, we have guests.’
’...’ Soren paused his cultivation and opened his eyes. ’How many?’
’...Five.’ Malakor replied. ’There is one Emperor as well.’
’I see.’ Soren’s eyes narrowed. ’Do they know our location?’
’...I think so. They must have someone with tracking abilities.’
’...They must know about your existence if they sent an Emperor,’ Soren theorized, and, recalling something, added, ’Can you describe their appearances?’
’From what I can sense,’ Malakor began, ’there are three men and two women. The Emperor is an older man with silver hair and a scar across his left cheek. The others are—’
A strange sensation washed over Soren, cutting Malakor’s voice off mid-sentence. The room around him dissolved into pitch black.

He felt the connection to Malakor and the outside world vanish completely. Yet, thanks to Eternal Bond, he could still faintly feel Ethea’s presence at the edge of his awareness, though the sensation felt muted, warped, and unnaturally distant.
’Am I... trapped in a domain or another dimension?’
Soren thought to himself and calmly activated Eyes of Truth.
[Void Arena]
Classification: Pocket Dimension
Origin: ’Void Arena’ Ability

Description: A sealed battlefield created by the ability user. The target is trapped within an isolated dimension with no connection to the outside world. The environment is shaped by the caster’s will.
Atmospheric Mana: Suppressive
Effects:
- Sensory Dampening: Sound and light are muted, making it difficult to track enemies.
- Mana Drain: The trapped target’s mana is slowly drained over time.
- Caster’s Domain: The ability user can sense everything within the arena and manipulate the terrain to an unlimited extent.
Exit Condition: Only the ability user can release the target from this space. Killing the ability user will also cause the dimension to collapse.
’So I was righ-!’

chapters.title: Chapter 369: Trapped [1]
paragraphs: ’So I was righ—!’
Soren activated Phantom Step and his body blurred to the side just as a blade sliced through the space where his neck had been. He reappeared a few meters away, his feet skidding against the ground.

Another strike came from behind. He twisted, dodged, and moved again. The darkness made it hard to track the attackers, but his high perception and Eyes of Truth gave him just enough clarity to see their outlines.
’...There are three of them.’

He tried to keep his gaze locked on the glowing text floating before him, but the relentless barrage forced him into a constant sequence of dodges and evasive steps. The sharp whistle of condensed spatial blades tore through the void around him, shaving off his margin for error.

While his body blurred across the pitch-black field, his mind raced through the tactical situation. Five hostiles had arrived at their location. If three were trapped in this domain with him, that left two unaccounted for outside.
The Emperor was likely engaging Malakor. The remaining member was almost certainly going after Ethea.

Though the bond signaled that she was safe for now, the mere possibility of her being targeted made his blood run cold. His eyes narrowed, burning with a sharp, murderous intensity. If the Emperor had trapped Malakor in a similar spatial isolation, Ethea would be completely defenseless against an enemy.
He couldn’t afford to waste a single second in here.

Without holding back, Soren unleashed Overlord’s Aura. A crushing wave of dominant, suffocating pressure exploded outward from his body, heavy enough to momentarily distort the dark space around him and halt the attackers. Simultaneously, he activated his amplification, boosting his strength, speed, and reaction time. He closed his left eye for a moment and opened it again, activating Nature’s Eyes on it.

’...One attacking, one hiding, and one in the sky.’ Although using two different abilities in two different eyes felt a bit weird, he managed to spot their positions easily and used the brief delay to skim the rest of the floating window before dismissing it.

’So I just have to kill the ability user to get out?’ he thought, his gaze sweeping across the three outlines as he traced their mana flows and life forces. The one floating in the air was feeding a continuous current into the surrounding void. ’Found him.’
Although he couldn’t exactly see them, he could tell they were staring back at him.
Swoo-!

Just as Soren was about to launch himself upward, the space around his legs violently warped, twisting his ankles in opposite directions. He braced his core, gritting his teeth against the shearing torque, and barely dodged sideways as a spatial rift snapped shut where his lower body had been.
[Stop.]

An alluring voice echoed directly inside his head, imposing a sudden weight on his body. He froze for a split second, the command sinking into his muscles before Indomitable Soul flared, shattering the control.
CLANG!

Two thick, dark iron chains shattered the pitch-black space right where he had stood a moment ago. Missing their mark by a fraction of an inch, they recoiled instantly and shot straight up into the void after him.
Soren didn’t react at all; instead, he just flicked his fingers.

A flash of rime erupted from his hand, tracing the air like pale blue lightning. The frost rapidly expanded upon contact, creeping down the links of the dark iron chains and snapping their momentum mid-flight. Heavy, brittle blocks of ice encased the metal, dragging them down into the floorless dark. Around him, even the thin atmospheric vapor froze into suspended, razor-sharp crystals, momentarily locking the air in place.
Perhaps recognizing that raw physical strikes were useless against him, the attackers soon changed their style.

Fluctuations in the void signaled the deployment of elemental energy. Yet, within the pocket dimension, these constructs remained completely invisible until they breached his immediate reaction radius.
So he kept moving, twisting his body through the featureless air.

Space kept warping around him with a sickening pop while spatial blades carved through his flank, severing his amplified frost armor as if it were parchment and leaving a bloody gash across his body. Before the wounds could even bleed properly, follow-up waves of acid washed over, sizzled against his skin, and cracked the remnants of his ice casing. Chains tore through his skin and bit off his flesh each time.
He ignored the burning agony completely, his expression cold, his eyes indifferent.
With a mental command, he summoned his beloved Nightfrost, inverted his momentum mid-air, and drove himself straight down, slamming the butt of the weapon into the void.

An overwhelming shockwave of glacial energy exploded outward in every direction. Massive, jagged spires of blue-white ice erupted from empty air, expanding like a frozen forest to pin down the immediate terrain and forcing the two grounded attackers onto the defensive.
Without wasting a single breath, Soren planted his boots on the freshly forged ice pillars, executing a series of rapid treading steps to launch himself back into the sky toward the domain caster.

Mid-ascent, the ambient gravity suddenly inverted and multiplied tenfold. A suffocating pressure slammed into his chest and shoulders like a falling mountain, threatening to shatter his momentum and drag him into the abyss below.
Soren’s face never lost its stone-cold composure.
’...Frozen Moment.’

In an instant, the world shuddered into a complete standstill. The crushing gravitational pull froze, the drifting frost locked in place, and in the fraction of a millisecond stolen from time itself, Soren bridged the remaining distance.
He materialized directly before the spatialist, his spear already coiled to strike.
Whoosh-!

The weapon thrust forward, a streak of blue piercing through the dark space. The spear tip drove cleanly through the target’s sternum, exiting their back. In the very next heartbeat, frost exploded outward from the blade, turning the target into a motionless block of ice.
"Tch."

Soren clicked his tongue as he realized he had hit the wrong target. Because at the last second, he ’saw’ it. The spatial user had reached out through the void and swapped places with the one with the blade.
Swoosh-!
The gravity increased another tenfold, and another command echoed in his mind at the same time.
’Fall!’
’Damn it.’

’...One attacking, one hiding, and one in the sky.’ Although using two different abilities in two different eyes felt a bit weird, he managed to spot their positions easily and used the brief delay to skim the rest of the floating window before dismissing it.
’So I just have to kill the ability user to get out?’ he thought, his gaze sweeping across the three outlines as he traced their mana flows and life forces.
The one floating in the air was feeding a continuous current into the surrounding void. ’Found him.’
Although he couldn’t exactly see them, he could tell they were staring back at him.
Swoo-!
Just as Soren was about to launch himself upward, the space around his legs violently warped, twisting his ankles in opposite directions.
He braced his core, gritting his teeth against the shearing torque, and barely dodged sideways as a spatial rift snapped shut where his lower body had been.
[Stop.]
An alluring voice echoed directly inside his head, imposing a sudden weight on his body.
He froze for a split second, the command sinking into his muscles before Indomitable Soul flared, shattering the control.
CLANG!
Two thick, dark iron chains shattered the pitch-black space right where he had stood a moment ago.
Missing their mark by a fraction of an inch, they recoiled instantly and shot straight up into the void after him.
Soren didn’t react at all; instead, he just flicked his fingers.
A flash of rime erupted from his hand, tracing the air like pale blue lightning.
The frost rapidly expanded upon contact, creeping down the links of the dark iron chains and snapping their momentum mid-flight.
Heavy, brittle blocks of ice encased the metal, dragging them down into the floorless dark.
Around him, even the thin atmospheric vapor froze into suspended, razor-sharp crystals, momentarily locking the air in place.
Perhaps recognizing that raw physical strikes were useless against him, the attackers soon changed their style.
Fluctuations in the void signaled the deployment of elemental energy.
Yet, within the pocket dimension, these constructs remained completely invisible until they breached his immediate reaction radius.
So he kept moving, twisting his body through the featureless air.
Space kept warping around him with a sickening pop while spatial blades carved through his flank, severing his amplified frost armor as if it were parchment and leaving a bloody gash across his body.
Before the wounds could even bleed properly, follow-up waves of acid washed over, sizzled against his skin, and cracked the remnants of his ice casing.
Chains tore through his skin and bit off his flesh each time.
He ignored the burning agony completely, his expression cold, his eyes indifferent.
With a mental command, he summoned his beloved Nightfrost, inverted his momentum mid-air, and drove himself straight down, slamming the butt of the weapon into the void.
An overwhelming shockwave of glacial energy exploded outward in every direction.
Massive, jagged spires of blue-white ice erupted from empty air, expanding like a frozen forest to pin down the immediate terrain and forcing the two grounded attackers onto the defensive.
Without wasting a single breath, Soren planted his boots on the freshly forged ice pillars, executing a series of rapid treading steps to launch himself back into the sky toward the domain caster.
Mid-ascent, the ambient gravity suddenly inverted and multiplied tenfold.
A suffocating pressure slammed into his chest and shoulders like a falling mountain, threatening to shatter his momentum and drag him into the abyss below.
Soren’s face never lost its stone-cold composure.
’...Frozen Moment.’
In an instant, the world shuddered into a complete standstill.
The crushing gravitational pull froze, the drifting frost locked in place, and in the fraction of a millisecond stolen from time itself, Soren bridged the remaining distance.
He materialized directly before the spatialist, his spear already coiled to strike.
Whoosh-!
The weapon thrust forward, a streak of blue piercing through the dark space.
The spear tip drove cleanly through the target’s sternum, exiting their back.
In the very next heartbeat, frost exploded outward from the blade, turning the target into a motionless block of ice.
"Tch."
Soren clicked his tongue as he realized he had hit the wrong target.
Because at the last second, he ’saw’ it.
The spatial user had reached out through the void and swapped places with the one with the blade.
Swoosh-!
The gravity increased another tenfold, and another command echoed in his mind at the same time.
’Fall!’
’Damn it.’

chapters.title: Chapter 370: Trapped [2]
paragraphs: ’Damn it.’
Soren cursed inwardly as his body plummeted like a meteor, dragged down by the staggering pull of gravity.
Waiting for him in the dark below were the iron chains, shooting upward to tear him apart. He instantly manifested Winter’s Barrier, a thick wall of dense ice forming beneath him.
BOOM!

The chains shattered right through the ice barrier and tore through his re-formed frost armor. Soren managed to twist his torso away at the last millisecond to avoid a fatal blow, but the jagged iron still sliced deep into his thigh and left arm. The wounds stung viciously, his flesh burning as if doused in molten acid.

He also felt a foreign substance instantly invading his body, probably poison, but ignored it as Core Refinement activated simultaneously. Besides, he didn’t have time to worry about it as the space directly beneath him twisted, and four spatial arrows tore through his back, bursting cleanly out of his chest, spraying his blood into the void.
’...Urgh.’

Soren spat out a mouthful of blood. The crushing gravity paired with the continuous mental compulsion made every movement feel like dragging heavy lead, forcing him to fight his own body with every breath.
Then, the floor vanished entirely.

Soren fell even again, even faster this time, dropping helplessly into the endless abyss while the chains struck again. One wrapped tightly around his neck, while the other shot straight for his heart.

Gritting his teeth against the suffocating grip on his throat, Soren twisted his body mid-fall. He clamped his left hand around the chain aiming for his heart, while his right hand grabbed the chain strangling his neck.

With a brutal surge of amplified strength, he yanked both chains down, pulling the hidden attacker straight toward him. The figure on the other end of the chains surged through the pitch-black void, dragged by his sheer force. Soren braced himself, ready to finish them the moment they were in range.
But as they approached, the figure exhaled. A cloud of strange, greenish gas erupted from their mouth and shot straight into his face.
Soren recognized the poisonous nature of the gas immediately and acted without hesitation, covering his face and head in a solid helmet of frost armor while shooting ice arrows at the target.

The arrows pierced through the space where the figure had been, but they had already vanished, snatched away by the spatial user before the ice could reach them. The greenish gas lingered for a moment, then ignited with a sudden burst of flame that slammed into him, cracking the frost helmet and sending him spinning through the void.
Thud-!

Soren slammed hard into a massive, jagged boulder that materialized out of nowhere in the darkness. The impact shattered the stone into fragmenting debris, sending him tumbling as the pocket dimension’s geography warped and twisted around him.
The void was no longer an empty abyss. Rocky crags, suspended cliffside ledges, and sheer stone faces shifted into existence around him, shifting coordinates in real time.
As he fell, the assault never stopped.

The dark iron chains whipped out from the newly formed terrain, coiling around his limbs and slamming him against the rock faces. Spatial blades carved through the stone cliffs, slicing cleanly through his frost armor and leaving deep, bleeding gashes across his chest and legs. Gravity shifted violently every few seconds, one moment dragging him down like a meteor, the next hurling him sideways into jagged outcroppings.
THUD! THUD!

Soren bounced off stone ledges and tumbled through collapsing terrain, his body taking the full force of the shifting domain while spatial attacks and chemical explosions repeatedly detonated around him in the dark.
"Gah!"

Soren grunted in agony as a spatial blade cleaved straight through his thigh. Seconds later, a heavy iron chain whipped from the shadows, shattering against his ribs and sending an agonizing scream tearing from his throat. He hit another jagged rock face, coughing up a mixture of dark blood and pulverized frost.

His face twisted in desperation. His eyes widened in panic, his movements growing frantic, sloppy, and weak. He flailed against the shifting gravity, taking hit after hit. Then, after a particularly violent blow from a stone spire, his head snapped back. His eyes rolled back in his head and closed, his limbs going completely limp.

The attackers didn’t stop immediately. A few more spatial blades sliced across his torso, and an iron chain slammed into his back, but Soren’s body absorbed the impacts like a ragdoll, his breathing thinning to near nothing.
Seeing no further signs of life, the barrage gradually ceased.
CLANG! CLANG!
The chains wrapped tightly around his arms, torso, and legs, binding his blood-soaked, motionless body in place in just a few seconds. Soren hung there suspended in the dark, entirely unresponsive.
A few moments passed in silence.

Then, silently and cautiously, a figure approached. They nudged his body with their foot, testing for any reaction. When none came, they moved closer and started to sit, only to vanish into thin air mid-motion.

Then the surrounding darkness gradually warped. The pitch-black void thinned as the isolated coordinate re-anchored itself. Light trickled back in, color and sound returning to the world as the surroundings transformed into a simple, small arena.
...Thud.
The spatial caster hit the stone floor, exhaling raggedly as he wiped a thick sheen of sweat from his brow. "Huff... Huff..."
Across from him, the other figure, a woman with slit eyes and short red hair, moved toward Soren, sat down beside him, and reached out to check his pulse and vitals.
"Huff... How is he?" the spatial user asked between breaths.
The woman tilted her head, her fingers lingering on Soren’s neck. Then she smiled, a cheerful expression crossing her face. "He’s fainted, hehe."
"F*ck, finally." The spatial user slumped back against the stone floor. "I am out of mana again."
The woman chuckled, her slit eyes trailing over Soren’s bloodied face with something close to fascination. She traced a finger along his jaw, tilting his head slightly to get a better look.
"Hehe~ He was indeed as strong as they said." Her lips curled into a playful smile. "Alas, he offended the young master and enraged the leader. Or else... I would have made him my new toy~"
