chapters.title: Chapter 371: Trapped [3]
paragraphs: "You can make him your toy later." The spatial user said, still recovering. "We need to find out the situation outside first and then act accordingly. We wasted more than enough time as it is."
"Then, let me out first," the woman said, smiling as she stood, her body slowly turning invisible. "Be ready to pull me back if anything goes wrong."
"Just don’t take too long. I can’t hold this place open forever."
"Relax." Her voice echoed from the air where she had been standing. "I’ll be quick."

The woman vanished. The spatial user watched the empty space where she had been for a moment, then let out another heavy breath and reached into his storage ring. He pulled out a small vial and downed it in one go.
’Another one.’

He had lost count of how many he had consumed during the fight. More than ten, at least. His ability was indeed powerful, but its consumption rate was equally brutal. Maintaining the Void Arena for that long had drained him to the edge of his reserves. If the fight had gone on any longer, he would have collapsed from mana exhaustion before the target did.
After wiping his mouth, his eyes drifted over to the frozen corpse lying on the stone floor a short distance away, and a cold sweat broke out across his back.
’...If I had been a second late, that would have been me.’
A raspy, manic chuckle escaped his throat. "...Keke~"
Then, his gaze shifted to the bloodied target lying not far away.
’To think a mere 4th Circle could push us into such a mess...’

It felt unreal. But the guy was the one who beat the Hollow Pair, so it fit. Heck, even with a coordinated ambush and a pocket dimension at their disposal, they had still lost one of their own just to bring him down. Not that he gave a damn about the dead guy anyway. The idiot was just a weak newcomer who failed to finish off the target in time, so it was his own fault. At least his death took out the target’s surprise attack and trump card.
He sighed and teleported beside the bound body.
Leaning in close, he narrowed his eyes at jagged lacerations slowly stitching themselves back together, the bleeding slowing with each passing second.

"His regeneration is indeed fucking amazing..." he muttered, leaning in to inspect the flesh even more closely. "If only I could get him as my test subject. The things I could learn from a body like this..."
He reached out and grabbed Soren’s chin, tilting his head from side to side to get a better look at the healing wounds.
However, his expression darkened as he sensed the woman calling for him from outside. He sighed again and closed his eyes, connecting with the external coordinate and pulling her back in.
A moment passed, and the woman began to materialize beside them. At that exact second, a bloodied hand shot out from the chains and locked onto the spatial user’s hand and then-
BOOOOM-!
"Fuc—!"

The curse died in his throat as the explosion consumed him. Kinetic force and frost erupted in every direction, tearing through his body before he could even register the pain. His grip on the space snapped instantly, and the domain broke apart, the surrounding arena crumbling into nothing as his vision cut to total black.

Soren groaned and forced himself upright. His head pounded, a sharp ache throbbing behind his eyes, and his senses were in disarray. The explosion had hit him harder than he’d expected. His ears rang, his vision blurred, and every nerve in his body screamed in protest. However, his gamble had paid off. His enemies were dead, and he had survived.
"Huff..."

Exhaling deeply, he reached into his inventory and pulled out a couple of potions, downing them one after another. The healing energy spread through his body, dulling the pain and slowly clearing the fog in his mind. With his own regeneration and abilities, he didn’t have to wait long to start thinking clearly again.
"Huff..."

With another exhale, he blinked away the blur in his vision and surveyed the scene. He was back on the paved street right outside their hotel. The ground was littered with fragments of frost and remnants of chaotic mana, traces of the collapsed void arena and the explosion that had ended it.
Just then, a familiar voice echoed in his head.
’Master! You’re back!’
’Yes...’ Soren replied. ’How is the situation?’
’I’m fighting with the emperor in our domains,’ Malakor quickly explained. ’I have left my clones to protect the lady but-’
’It’s ok, I will take it from here.’ Soren replied, forcing himself to stand up. ’Just he-’
’Master, don’t worry about her,’ Malakor added immediately. ’She was rescued earlier. Reinforcements from the empire had already arrived before the intruder could get inside.’

Soren fell silent. Sitting back, he closed his eyes and extended his perception outward to sweep the nearby hotel. Ethea was still inside the bedroom, safe and sound. Right outside the building, however, several powerful figures stood guard, their mana flares locking down the perimeter.
’...’ Soren’s brows furrowed as he considered using the Guardian’s Mark to teleport directly to Ethea’s side, but he stopped himself after a moment’s thought.

Besides, he’d kept part of his focus on Ethea’s condition throughout the ordeal, so he knew she wasn’t in immediate danger. He had held off using it inside the Void Arena for the same reason. Well, even if he used it, the spatial user would likely have pulled him right back in, wasting his single escape card. Keeping it in reserve was the smarter move in case things went south again.
"...Mr. Everly?"
"..." Soren opened his eyes and saw a familiar figure walking toward him. It was Princess Roya’s personal guard, the same woman who had thanked him after the Bagdad incident. ’So it was her...’
"Greetings, Knight Aya." He tried to get back to his feet, but his body wouldn’t cooperate. His legs gave way, and he nearly fell back to the ground.

Aya moved quickly, vanishing for a split second before appearing right beside him. She caught his shoulder and helped him stay upright, her gaze scanning the deep gashes across his skin and the blood coating his clothes. "Mr. Everly, let me take you to a healer."

chapters.title: Chapter 372: A Moment of Peace
paragraphs: "N-No..." Soren replied, his gaze landing on the hotel. "There’s no need..."
But then he paused. His legs were still shaking, his body barely holding together. If he went to Ethea like this, she would worry and feel guilty again.
"...Actually," he corrected himself, "maybe a little help wouldn’t hurt."

Aya nodded and stepped closer, letting him lean on her shoulder for support. With his free hand, Soren reached into his inventory and pulled out a small artifact, activating it. The next moment, his face shifted into his usual disguise.
Aya noticed it but didn’t say anything. However, as they started walking toward the hotel, she finally broke the silence.
"I must apologize to you, Mr. Everly. Our negligence put both you and Mrs. Everly in grave danger."
Soren kept his pace slow, letting her support most of his weight as she continued.

"We managed to capture the traitor inside our ranks, but it was already too late," she explained, her voice tinged with regret and guilt. "He had passed your location to the Outcasts after learning it from the Hollow Pair. As soon as Her Highness learned of it, she sent us here to guard you. Yet... we still arrived too late and put you in such a desperate situation. I am truly sorry."
"...It’s ok," Soren replied after a moment. "You came in time to save my wife at least."
He then paused and looked at the pitch-black sky. "...How’s the situation?"

"Commander Ervin is currently aiding your summoned beast in their fight against the enemy’s Emperor," Aya began explaining. "We also intercepted the individual attempting to abduct Mrs. Everly. They were relatively weak in direct combat, though her abilities made her somewhat troublesome to secure."
"I see..."

"Furthermore, a full-scale purge is underway across the empire," Aya continued. "Many Sovereigns and high-ranking powerhouses are actively participating in the hunt for the Outcasts’ leader and any remaining members. By morning, the entire operation should be brought to an end.
"That’s reassuring," Soren murmured, focusing his remaining energy on keeping his stride even.

They walked the rest of the way in silence. As they approached the hotel entrance, the armored figures posted around the perimeter came into view. They snapped to attention and saluted Aya without a word.
Aya nodded, ordered them to keep their guard up, led him into a makeshift tent not far away, and immediately motioned to a high-tier healer stationed inside.
The healer didn’t hesitate, stepping forward and gathering bright green mana into his hands before laying them over Soren’s torn back.

As the healing magic washed through his flesh, sealing the outer gashes, Soren took advantage of the proximity. He subtly opened the status windows of the healer and every knight in his line of sight. He checked each profile methodically, ensuring none were hidden threats.
A few minutes passed, and Soren finished receiving treatment. With a gesture from Aya, the healer took their leave and left them alone.
"If it’s not too much trouble, can you tell me what happened and how you ended up in such a state?" Aya asked in a polite tone. "How many of them did you fight with?"
’...Did they not ask the captive, or did the captive refuse to answer?’ Soren thought as he lay on the patient bed. ’Or is she trying to verify it through my story?’
Regardless of her motive, lying offered no advantage. He gave a straightforward account of the encounter, describing the enemy’s count and abilities till how he ended up in this state.
Aya listened quietly, and by the end, her expression darkened with a mixture of guilt and grim respect. Gulping dryly, she opened her mouth. "So... are they all dead?"

"The spatial user and the other are dead, but I can’t guarantee the woman’s fate," Soren replied. "She got out of the pocket dimension for more than a minute earlier; didn’t you sense her? And although I timed my attack the moment she was entering the pocket dimension, she might have slipped away before the explosion reached her."
Aya nodded, her eyes narrowing. "Thank you for sharing such valuable info, Mr. Everly. Since you need time to regain your strength, I will leave you to rest for a moment."
With a polite gesture, she excused herself and left the tent. Then she immediately ordered her subordinates to conduct a grid search of the city for enemies.
Soren sighed, closed his eyes, and focused on his bonds.
’Dear...’
’Can you hear me?’
His lips curled up, and his expression became serene at the sound of a familiar voice.
’Mmm. I can, dear. Sorry for making you worry.’
’T-Thank goodness!’ Ethea’s voice trembled in his mind. ’Are you okay? Where are you? When I woke up and found you gone, I could barely sense your presence at all. I thought... I thought you were...’
’It’s alright now,’ Soren interjected softly. ’I’ll explain everything soon.’
’Dear... I felt that you were in grave danger just a moment ago,’ she insisted, her emotions tangled in fear, worry, and restlessness. ’What exactly happened? How are you holding up now?’

Her words filled his heart with affection and guilt. Just imagining how terrified she must have been upon waking up to find him missing and his presence dangerously faint, as if dying, made his chest tighten.

He took a slow breath and briefly explained the situation, keeping the worst of the gore to himself as he recounted the spatial ambush, the domain trap, how he had broken free, and his current situation. ’...I will come up soon, don’t worry.’ He finished and opened his eyes. Knight Aya was standing above him, as if she had been guarding him the entire time.
Naturally, Soren had sensed her arrival and was monitoring the situation while talking with Ethea, so he didn’t look surprised. He sat up slowly and asked, "How’s it going?"
"They’re still searching," she replied, also knowing he must have heard her earlier. "But there’s good news, too: the fight above is about to end."
"That’s indeed good news."

chapters.title: Chapter 373: Time To Rest
paragraphs: "It’s indeed good news." Soren smiled, glancing out of the tent entrance at the sky. He couldn’t see anything but a vast expanse of pitch-black darkness stretching across the heavens, devoid of stars or moon, a stark reminder of the massive forces clashing above.
’...Let’s wait till the end.’

He hadn’t contacted Malakor again because he feared that if his bond was engaged in serious combat, a sudden mental communication might break his concentration at a critical moment and put him in danger.

Still, he couldn’t suppress the small sigh that escaped him. Part of him was disappointed to have missed the battle between Emperors. Their fight must have been on an entirely different level from his own.
’...I’ll ask him about it later.’ He decided.

As a mental-type magic beast, Malakor was fully capable of using illusions to project his memories, which meant he could share the entire battle directly into Soren’s mind later on. Observing how Emperors usually fought through such a vivid playback would offer invaluable insight into high-level combat tactics.
With that thought comforting him, Soren settled in to wait patiently alongside Aya until Malakor’s voice finally resonated in his mind.
’Master, it is over now.’
’Good job, but are you ok? Did you get any injuries?’
’Unfortunately, yes, but nothing too severe.’
’Then come down here; I will give you an elixir. There’s a healer too.’
Understood...’

A few minutes later, three figures descended from the sky and landed beside the tent. Among them was the sleek form of a black panther, Malakor, his fur singed in several places, with faint smoke curling from his flanks. Beside him stood Commander Ervin, his armor scuffed and dented, carrying the unconscious body of an enemy combatant slung over one arm.
Aya snapped a salute and ordered the healer to treat them right away.
Soren stepped out of the tent as well, his eyes sweeping over the arrivals. Commander Ervin met his gaze and nodded, relief clear in his eyes. "It is a relief to see you standing, Mr. Everly.
"Likewise," Soren replied, pulling a vitality elixir from his storage and offering it to the commander. "Thank you for your assistance, and here, this should help with your injuries."

Ervin accepted the vial with a word of thanks and uncorked it immediately. Soren then turned to the black panther. Smiling softly, he reached out and patted its head, feeling the warmth radiating from its coat.
"Open up," Soren instructed gently.

Malakor parted his jaws, letting Soren tilt another elixir into his mouth. He then swallowed the liquid in a single gulp, the faint burns along his dark hide already beginning to soothe under the potion’s effect.
’Thank you, Master.’ He bowed in gratitude. ’Right. Shall I teleport you to Lady Ethea’s side now, Master?’
’Yes, but let me wrap things up here first. In the meantime, you can rest and recuperate.’

’Understood.’ The panther nodded and blended into his shadow. Soren took a deep breath, stretched his stiff shoulders, and turned back to Commander Ervin. "Commander, may I ask about something? Did you notice any other suspicious individual?"
Ervin shook his head.
"Then what about that guy?" Soren pointed at the unconscious body of the enemy emperor.

"Actually, he’s not affiliated with the Outcasts. He is a criminal hired by the traitor to help the Outcasts. His ability helps him find anybody, as long as he knows how they look and has a faint trace of their mana signature."
Soren’s eyes sharpened as the pieces clicked into place. ’So he was the one who pinpointed our location and guided them directly to us...’
As for how they got his mana signature, it must be leech’s work since he absorbed his mana back then.
"Unfortunately," Ervin added, "we could not extract any further details before he lost consciousness."
"I see. Thank you for telling me," Soren said, shifting his posture. "Is it alright if I take my leave now? I would like to check on my wife."
Ervin gave an understanding nod. "Of course. Rest and recover with peace of mind, Mr. Everly. My men and I will secure the area until the situation is fully resolved."
"I appreciate it." Soren nodded toward Commander Ervin and Knight Aya, taking his leave as he stepped back toward the main corridor.
Just as he reached the entrance, the space around him blurred, and his form vanished entirely.
An instant later, he materialized inside the bathroom of their hotel room. ’Thank you, Malakor.’
’It is my duty, Master.’
’Mm...’ Soren took his clothes off and stepped into the shower. ’Dear, I’ll take a quick bath first.’
’...Alright.’

’...Alright.’ Ethea stared in the direction of the bathroom, her heart still pounding from worry. She knew he didn’t want to show her his injuries and was trying to wash away the blood before coming out, but waiting alone here only made every second feel agonizingly long. A persistent dread lingered within her, a stubborn anxiety that refused to subside until she could wrap her arms around him and see him whole.

Fortunately, she didn’t have to wait that long, as Soren soon opened the door and entered the room. At a glance, he looked completely fine, with no visible injuries on his skin apart from a few faint pink traces. Yet her observant gaze instantly caught the subtle detail: he had deliberately put on a high-collared, long-sleeved shirt, clearly meant to hide any remaining marks from her view.
She swallowed her worry and chose not to call him out on it.
"Dear..." She called out, showing him a relieved smile. "You’re back."
"Mm." Soren offered her a gentle smile as he crossed the room and sat down on the edge of the bed. Reaching out, he carefully helped her sit up, supporting her back with steady hands.

As soon as she was upright, Ethea leaned forward and wrapped her arms around his torso, holding him gently without pressing too hard against his chest. She said nothing, resting her cheek against his shoulder as if to confirm he was truly here.
Soren returned the embrace, wrapping his arms securely around her, letting her feel his pulse and the steady rhythm of his breathing.
They stayed like that until Ethea recovered her composure. Then she pulled back slightly and looked at him.
"Dear, you should lie down and rest now."
"Mm. Let’s do it together."

chapters.title: Chapter 374: Elixir's Effects
paragraphs: ‘Hmm? What is this?’ Ervin raised a brow as he noticed something peculiar.
The injuries he sustained during the intense battle earlier, which would usually take weeks to heal even with a skilled healer’s help, had healed completely in just a few minutes.

Even more astonishing was the sensation settling deep within his bones: several hidden ailments and lingering scars from past campaigns had vanished entirely. His breath came easy and clean, his muscles felt fluid, and a vibrant surge of energy coursed through his limbs, making him feel as though he had returned to the peak of his physical prime. Even his mana pathways, which had been slightly worn from decades of use, felt smoother than they had in years.
He flexed his gloved fist, genuinely stunned by the sudden vitality restoring his body.

‘What in the world...’ He blinked, then remembered the potion Soren had handed him a while ago. He had known the moment he uncorked the vial that its potency was impressive, but now it was clear he had drastically underestimated it.
‘Could it be... an elixir?’

The thought struck him with sudden clarity. Potions of the sixth grade and below were considered standard concoctions, but those reaching and surpassing the seventh grade were elevated to the status of elixirs. And healing-type elixirs possessed miraculous effects capable of easily reversing organ failure, bringing one back from the dead, and purging deeply entrenched impurities and even high-grade toxins.

‘Come to think of it, he had given the same thing to that elf girl back then too.’ Ervin recalled the scene from the cooking competition. The elf was approaching the brink of death with low life force, and in a few minutes, she had completely recovered as if the fatal damage had never occurred. ‘Yeah, there’s no need to doubt it now. It was really an elixir.’
And that was precisely why the gesture carried so much weight.

Elixirs were extraordinarily rare treasures. They were usually sold only at high-tier auctions or kept hidden in the vaults of high-ranking noble families or Awakened. Securing even a single bottle required immense wealth and connections, making them nearly impossible to acquire through standard channels.
Yet Soren had handed one over without a single moment of hesitation.

‘To possess such treasures and give them away so freely...’ Ervin thought, glancing back toward the building. Soren probably held a high status, but even more notable was his generosity toward those standing on his side.

‘...’ A firm resolve settled in Ervin’s chest. Someone who treated his allies with such benevolence deserved proper respect and protection in return. He made a mental note to express his gratitude properly once the situation settled.
Refocusing, Ervin expanded his sensory range across the surrounding area, fully committed to guarding them with all his power until the threat vanished completely.

Soren held Ethea close, gazing affectionately at her face while gently caressing her hair. He leaned down, pressing a warm kiss to her head and then to her forehead. Ethea shifted closer into his embrace, snuggling against his chest with deep affection, content to stay wrapped in his arms.
Just then, a familiar ding rang in Soren’s mind, prompting him to close his eyes and watch messages appear in his vision.
[Investment detected.]
[Target: Commander Ervin]
[Analyzing Investment...]
[Investment: You provided the target with a high-grade elixir that healed his injuries, restored his body to peak condition, and purged old wounds and ailments he had carried for years.]
[Analyzing target response...]

[As a result of your actions, the target has fully recovered and is now in the best physical condition he has been in for decades. His gratitude toward you has deepened significantly, and he has committed himself to guarding you and your wife with everything he has.]
[Evaluating investment significance...]
[Evaluation complete.]
[Investment Grade: High]
[Calculating returns...]
[Calculation complete.]
[Applying Authority Modifier: Amplification (Passive) — Baseline bonus applied. Reward tier scaling upgraded.]
[Returns granted:]
[1. Sovereign Vitality Elixir x2]
[2. Recipe Unlocked: Scar Recovery Salve]
[3. Basic Military Knowledge]
[Integration initiated...]
[Integration Complete!]

‘...’ Soren smiled and opened his eyes. The returns were great for a high-grade investment. He used only a single Sovereign Vitality Elixir, so he didn’t expect a high-grade return like this. But then again, given how it affected the target, that made sense too. It was a powerful elixir, after all; hadn’t he already recovered himself?
He hadn’t thought much of it earlier since it didn’t affect Ethea that much, but he hadn’t accounted for her curse interfering with the elixir’s effect and weakening it significantly.
‘I think I should be more mindful about when I use them,’ he thought. ‘Though since I got two in return, it ended up being more than worth it.’
It would serve as a nice investment material for a long time, and the new recipe might come in handy someday too.
‘Though they’ll have to have scars to need the salve in the first place.’
With an internal chuckle, he moved on to the last return.
‘Basic Military Knowledge, huh.’

He had picked up bits and pieces over the years, from books, from conversations, from watching movies and such. He knew some famous tactics and basics, like pincer maneuvers, hit-and-run ambushes, and supply-line harassment. But this return elevated his understanding to a completely different level, giving him a grounded foundation in actual warfare.

It taught him all the core fundamentals, such as military ranks and chain of command, basic squad formations, battlefield logistics, terrain utilization, signaling, defensive fortifying, rapid troop positioning, and various other tactical drills.
‘It really fills in all the gaps.’

And looking back at his previous investments, he realized a pattern in how these types of returns worked. The knowledge he gained often tied directly to the target’s identity, profession, and unique specialization. Investing in an Imperial Knight Commander like Ervin gave him military knowledge, just as investing in a caretaker like Aunt Clara gave him caretaking knowledge.

‘If the type of knowledge depends on who I invest in, then I should broaden my scope,’ Soren decided. Whenever the opportunity presented itself, he would invest in people from every path and discipline, building a comprehensive web of skills and insights for himself. ‘Especially curse specialists...’

He knew some famous tactics and basics, like pincer maneuvers, hit-and-run ambushes, and supply-line harassment.
But this return elevated his understanding to a completely different level, giving him a grounded foundation in actual warfare.

It taught him all the core fundamentals, such as military ranks and chain of command, basic squad formations, battlefield logistics, terrain utilization, signaling, defensive fortifying, rapid troop positioning, and various other tactical drills.
‘It really fills in all the gaps.’
And looking back at his previous investments, he realized a pattern in how these types of returns worked.
The knowledge he gained often tied directly to the target’s identity, profession, and unique specialization.
Investing in an Imperial Knight Commander like Ervin gave him military knowledge, just as investing in a caretaker like Aunt Clara gave him caretaking knowledge.
‘If the type of knowledge depends on who I invest in, then I should broaden my scope,’ Soren decided.
Whenever the opportunity presented itself, he would invest in people from every path and discipline, building a comprehensive web of skills and insights for himself.
‘Especially curse specialists...’

chapters.title: Chapter 375: News
paragraphs: Half an hour later, Soren received another investment notification, this time for Malakor. The returns were smaller than Commander Ervin’s: just +5000 mana and an elixir, probably because Malakor had no hidden injuries. Still, it seemed that Malakor’s loyalty and respect for Soren had deepened considerably.
It improved Soren’s mood since he regarded Malakor as a real magic beast bond instead of a slave now. Though he doubted Malakor would ever change how he addressed him in the near future.
Meanwhile, Ethea exchanged a few messages with the princess again, and they continued tracking the latest updates on the outcasts.
Then, around six in the morning, a new headline exploded across the internet.
"Outcasts’ Hidden Lair Raided — Leader Escapes!"

The article revealed that a group of the empire’s sovereigns had uncovered the outcasts’ hidden lair and launched a full raid, capturing most of the remaining members. However, their leader had managed to slip away while sustaining severe injuries.

Not long after, another news bulletin broke, reporting a chaotic breakout during a prisoner transfer. The Hollow pair and several other high-risk criminals were killed in the clash. Amid the chaos, however, a mysterious individual had appeared and took Lucent away without leaving a trace.

Soren and Ethea were clearly troubled by the news. The Outcasts’ leader was still alive and on the run, despite being injured. Lucent had escaped too, and whoever had taken him was powerful enough to bypass the Empire’s security and disappear without a trace. That left them vulnerable to becoming targets once again.

They could understand the leader escaping. A Sovereign was a Sovereign. They wielded enough power to destroy nations and reshape continents. Cornering one was difficult enough, but killing or capturing one was another matter entirely. Yet letting a mortal escape right in front of their eyes? That was harder to swallow.

’...The Empire is more incompetent than I thought.’ Soren thought with a wry smile, but kept the thought to himself. Criticizing the Empire in front of its knights wouldn’t do them any favors. However, he still decided to ask Ethea’s opinion. ’What do you think, dear?’

’As long as we’re near the academy, they won’t target us anytime soon.’ Ethea answered thoughtfully. ’Besides, they said he took serious injuries; unless he has supreme elixirs, it will take years to recover from them. However, we should stay on guard and remain cautious to prevent today from repeating itself.’
’Mm, I had the same idea.’ Soren nodded. ’By the way, Ryan and I are going to start clearing the gate whenever we’re free, starting today. Will you be able to stay with his family when we’re gone?’
Ethea paused. ’I can. But... are you going to leave Malakor with me?’
’Of course. He’ll stay with you the whole time.’
She nodded, then hesitated. ’Is it really necessary, though? Wouldn’t it be better to focus on cultivating and training instead? You can gain more from meditation than from gate diving.’

Soren smiled. ’Clearing gates is training for me. It’s just as beneficial as cultivating, maybe more. So trust me on this... Actually, I’m aiming to break through to the fifth circle as quickly as possible too.’
Ethea studied him for a moment. ’...Just don’t overdo it. Cultivating more slowly and steadily is fine too. There’s no need to rush.’
’I’ll keep that in mind.’ Soren promised. ’But the same goes for you. Don’t push yourself hard.’
’Mmm.’
’Good.’ Soren smiled, planted a gentle kiss on her forehead, and let his thoughts drift to his cultivation.

Actually, he wasn’t too worried about his progress. To reach the 9th circle, one needed to comprehend an Authority, and since he already had one, it meant his potential was at least 9th circle, so he didn’t have to worry about bottlenecks or limits like many others. All he had to do was keep pushing forward. With Eternal Bond tripling his cultivation speed, constant mana returns from investments and threads, absorption from killing monsters, and Core Refinement passively liquefying his mana, reaching the 5th circle was only a matter of time.
’I’ll need your help when it comes to breakthrough, though.’ He chuckled. ’You’re more knowledgeable about it than I am, and you’ve experienced it personally, too.’
’I’ll help however I can.’ Ethea agreed readily.
’I wonder how long it will take this time, though...’

The higher a cultivator’s rank, the longer it took to break through. Talent affected the time, but the general rule still held. When he pushed into the fourth circle, the process had taken a little over a day. Ethea had been stunned by the speed, considering that her own attempt back then required five full days of uninterrupted concentration, a pace already considered the best among her peers.
’I should make preparations for it too...’ He thought, and his thoughts naturally drifted to the things he would need and the environment that would give him the best chance of success.
Just then, Malakor’s voice echoed in his mind.
’Master, Commander Ervin is approaching your room.’
Soren nodded and turned to Ethea. ’Commander Ervin is here. I’ll go welcome him.’
Ethea nodded softly in response as Soren left the room and made his way to the entrance. He opened the door just as the commander reached their room. "Commander, please, come in."
"I appreciate the offer, but I’m afraid I can’t." The commander said apologetically.
"Is something the matter?" Soren asked curiously. "Something related to the Outcasts."

"Partly, yes. But mostly it’s orders from above. My superiors have called me back. There are matters that require my attention elsewhere." He paused, then met Soren’s eyes. "I came to bid farewell before I left."
"I see," Soren said, nodding in understanding. "I wish you a safe journey, Commander. And once again, thank you for coming to our aid."
Commander smiled and shook his head. "It should be me thanking you, Mr. Everly. What you gave me helped more than you know. So, I wanted to express my gratitude in return."
He paused and presented Soren with two items. A silver metal token and a small blue magic bead.

"This token bears my personal crest," he explained. "If you ever need to reach me, show it to any Imperial Knight, and they’ll know how to contact me. And this bead is a teleportation artifact. It’s single-use, but it can take you to any place you’ve visited before. I hope it proves useful."
"This..."

chapters.title: Chapter 376: Meeting The Sister-In-Law
paragraphs: "This..." Soren stared at the two items in his hand, looking up at the commander. "You do not have to give me anything, Sir. I only-"
"Compared to what you gave me, Mr. Everly, this is nothing." Ervin cut him off decisively. "Please, take them. It puts my heart at ease."
"...Thank you, Commander. I’ll put them to good use."
Ervin nodded, then glanced toward the hallway. "I’ll leave a few of my subordinates stationed nearby, just in case." He bowed his head slightly. "Take care, Mr. Everly."
"You too, Commander."
Soren watched until Ervin’s figure disappeared down the corridor. Then he turned and went back inside.

By the time they finished getting ready, the morning sun had fully risen. Soren helped Ethea into her wheelchair, and they headed outside. They went to Ryan’s apartment since they had promised to have breakfast at their house. Ryan’s mother had insisted on treating them, saying she would cook Soren’s favorite dumplings and bake cookies for Ethea.

As Soren drove down the morning streets, he glanced in the rearview mirror. A dark sedan was maintaining a steady distance behind them, matching their every turn. He focused his senses for a moment, traced the familiar mana signatures inside, and realized they were simply the guards Commander Ervin had assigned to keep watch. Satisfied they posed no threat, he let it be and kept his focus on the road.
Breakfast went smoothly, thanks to Ryan’s mother’s lively hospitality. After they finished eating, Ryan picked up his gear and joined them, and they headed straight to the Etenia Academy.

Not long after they departed, Ryan asked Soren about what actually happened during the recent incident and whether he had actually fought with the Hollow Pair. Soren shared the story, keeping the details brief but honest. Ryan listened with wide eyes, occasionally interrupting with questions.
"...That’s how it went."
"Amazing..." Ryan muttered in awe as Soren finished. "I wish I had been there too. I could have helped, or at least seen it with my own eyes."
"Don’t worry, there will be many opportunities in the future," Soren said with a wry smile. "Besides, you should worry about the exam right now."
"Right, the exam." Ryan nodded and, recalling something, raised his head. "By the way, Brother Soren, I saw the news about the Outcasts. Nothing happened to you and Sister-in-law, right?"
"There was some trouble, but we managed to take care of it. But thanks for worrying, though.
"Mm."
"Anyway, we couldn’t talk much yesterday. How did the past month go for you?" Soren gave Ryan a meaningful smile. "I see that you have already reached the fourth circle. Congrats."
"Yeah, thank you..." Ryan rubbed the bridge of his nose and let out a sheepish laugh. "I actually broke through about a week ago."
"Congratulations, Ryan," Ethea offered with a genuine smile.
"Thank you too, Sister-in-law." Ryan beamed, clearly pleased by her praise.
"That explains why I could not get ahold of you back then," Soren added, noting how differently Ryan reacted to Ethea’s words. ’I almost forgot she is his ’hero’. Well, not that I mind.’
"Pretty much," Ryan nodded, leaning back against his headrest. "It took me four full days."
"Four days?" Soren gave him a quick thumbs-up. "That is fast."
He kept his own breakthrough timeline to himself, knowing better than to bring up the one-day record.
"Let’s test how much you have improved this afternoon, then," Soren added. "I booked a 3rd Circle Gate."
"Sounds good," Ryan nodded eagerly. "I’ve been wanting to test out my new strength."

They kept chatting about their afternoon plans until they arrived at their destination. Soren parked the car and helped Ethea out. Ryan and Ethea went in first. Soren waited about ten minutes before following them.
They reunited inside the academy and made their way to the Vice-Principal’s office. Someone was already waiting for them at the entrance to the building.
"Good morning, Lady Zura." Soren greeted her first, and Zura politely returned the greeting before hugging Ethea.
"And is this the boy I’ve heard so much about?" Zura turned to Ryan with a playful smile. "He looks cute~"
Ryan straightened his back and bowed. "G-Greetings, ma’am. It’s a pleasure to meet you."
Zura let out an amused chuckle and waved dismissively. "Relax, there is no need to be so tense around me. After all, I’m gonna be your teacher once you pass the exam."
"Y-Yes, ma’am!
"Hehe." Zura giggled before turning to Soren. "You can go on ahead. We’ll be waiting nearby."
Soren nodded in gratitude. "Ryan, let’s go."
"Oh, ok." Ryan hurriedly followed after Soren.
Zura watched them go and turned back to Ethea. "Lea, do you wanna see something interesting?"
"...Are you going to take me to see her?" Ethea guessed as Zura took the wheelchair’s handle.
"Yep. You said you want to learn more about her, right?" Zura’s eyes glinted. "Isn’t this the perfect chance? They’ll probably be in there for a while, so we’ve got enough time to kill."
"...If you say so," Ethea muttered and let Zura do whatever she wanted.
About ten minutes later, they arrived in front of a classroom, and Zura activated an invisibility artifact, steering the wheelchair inside without making a sound.

Ethea’s gaze swept across the room, taking in the fifteen or so students scattered among the desks, before falling upon a particular girl sitting in the front row near the window. Crimson hair caught the sunlight as the girl looked intently at the teacher explaining the lesson.

’...So she is my little sister-in-law.’ Ethea watched her intently, tracking the way she listened to the lecture. When the teacher paused, Nura raised her hand, asked a question, then immediately jotted down the answer in her notebook. ’She really looks cute. But...’
There was a desperate intensity in the way she moved: a girl pushing herself to her limits, eager to absorb every shred of knowledge just to prove her worth and grow stronger.
And strangely, watching her brought back memories of the past.

She... She reminded Ethea of her younger self. She too was like this back then, entirely consumed by her studies and driven by that same relentless urge to prove herself, perhaps even more obsessive about never showing a single flaw.
’...We must save her.’

chapters.title: Chapter 377: Interview
paragraphs: Knock. Knock.
Soren knocked on the door out of formality, and a gentle voice echoed from inside. "Come in."
He gestured to Ryan with his eyes, opened the door, and entered first. Ryan followed after him, and his eyes landed on the figure sitting behind the mahogany desk.

At first glance, she seemed harmless, almost unassuming as she leaned over her paperwork. Yet Ryan’s instincts immediately screamed otherwise. Every fiber of his gut told him she was like a sleeping predator, concealing her true depth beneath a calm facade.

Just then, she raised her head, and their gazes met. And in that single instant, he felt exposed, as if she were peeling back his layers and looking right through him. Before he could process the sensation, a crushing force bore down on his shoulders without a warning. The pressure hit him like an anvil, threatening to collapse his legs and force him to his knees.
Gritting his teeth, Ryan instinctively grounded his stance, channeling his mana to endure the force while forcing his facial features to remain completely calm.

He knew this was some kind of test, and she probably matched the output to his own strength, intending to measure his limits. Trusting in his foundation and the grueling weeks he’d spent training, he tightened his grip and held his ground.

Soren watched from the side, a flicker of surprise passing through his eyes at Ryan’s quick reaction, but he chose not to interfere. He was more interested in how easily she controlled the pressure and targeted Ryan.
A few moments later, the suffocating pressure vanished into thin air.

"Huff..." Ryan took a deep breath, letting the tension drain from his shoulders. With a subtle flick of fire mana, the thin beads of sweat forming on his brow evaporated into steam before they could even fall.
He leaned forward and bowed respectfully, his voice steady. "Greetings, Vice-Principal. I am Ryan."
"Welcome, Ryan." Ramona inclined her head, studied him for a moment, then gestured toward the chairs in front of her desk. "Please, both of you, take a seat."
They sat down, and Soren leaned forward slightly. "How have you been, Vice-Principal? I heard you participated in the purge. You didn’t get any injuries, right?"
Ramona nodded, a faint smile touching her lips. "I did. Thank you for asking." She paused, her green eyes meeting his. "I hope you did well too, Mr. Everly.
’Oh, she already knows.’ Soren raised a brow before replying with a smile of his own. "I was fortunate, and compared to what you and the other Sovereigns accomplished, my part was small."
Ramona’s smile widened slightly. "Modesty suits you, but false modesty doesn’t. From what I heard, you handled yourself better than most would in your position."

’...Heard, huh.’ Soren paused, then gave a small nod. "Thank you for your praise. And..." He reached into his pocket and pulled out a small ring, placing it on the desk in front of her. "This is the promised item."

Ramona picked up the ring and stared at it for a few seconds before turning back to them. "I’ve checked it and verified its contents." Her fingers lightly tapped the band before she looked up. "Rest assured, we will put it to good use."

Soren gave a brief nod. "I am sure you will." He paused, steering the conversation back to their main reason for visiting. "Then, should we talk about Ryan’s transfer now? I heard there are a few documents he needs to complete."
"There are indeed documents like enrollment forms, a medical evaluation, and a registration of his abilities. But before all that..." She turned her gaze to Ryan. "There’s also a personal interview."
"Interview? ...I guess you’re the one who will be conducting it?"

"You guessed it right." Ramona blinked before turning her attention to Ryan. "However, there’s something I have to tell you before that... If you fail to pass the interview, you won’t be accepted into Etenia Academy."
Ryan swallowed hard, the weight of her words settling over him, but he held her gaze and nodded firmly. "I understand and am prepared for the interview."
"Good."

Ramona flicked her fingers. In a fraction of a second, the office blurred and warped, space folding in on itself. The bookshelves, the wooden floor, Ramona, and Soren all vanished from sight, leaving Ryan standing alone in a vast, seamless expanse.
His body instantly went on high alert, but he forced his hands to stay at his sides, keeping his cool despite the sudden shift.
’This must be another test too...’
Ryan muttered inwardly, letting his senses expand outward. The space around him was utterly featureless, an infinite stretch of grey that gave no sense of direction or distance.
"Let’s start the interview." Vice Principal Ramona’s voice resonated directly inside his mind, coming from every direction at once. "First, tell me your name."
"R-Ryan.
"Your age?"
"Sixteen, and I’ll turn seventeen soon."
"Do you have any hobbies?"
"Yes. I like swordsmanship and reading books. I also enjoy playing games, especially role-playing ones."
"Do you love someone?"
"Eh?" Ryan blinked dumbfoundedly before quickly replying. "Y-Yes. I love my family."
"Have you ever killed someone?"

"..." Ryan fell silent, caught off guard once more by the abrupt shift in her questions. He took a moment to compose himself before answering. "No, I haven’t killed anyone. However, I have killed many monsters and... former humans who turned into monsters."
"Then... will you kill someone?"
"What do you mean, kill someone?" Ryan frowned.
"..." Silence followed, and Ryan understood she wouldn’t speak unless he answered. ’...Alright, let’s do this.’

"...I will kill, but only if there is no other choice. If someone threatens my life or the people I care about, I won’t hesitate to strike them down. However, I will never take a life without a proper reason, nor will I ever do so mindlessly."
"...Why did you apply for Etenia Academy?"

"...I want to get stronger and protect what matters to me. I need access to resources, proper guidance, and an environment that pushes me to work hard and break past my limits. Etenia is the only place capable of providing that standard of growth."
"...Do you... like black tea?"
"Eh?"

Soren knocked on the door out of formality, and a gentle voice echoed from inside.
"Come in."
He gestured to Ryan with his eyes, opened the door, and entered first.
Ryan followed after him, and his eyes landed on the figure sitting behind the mahogany desk.
At first glance, she seemed harmless, almost unassuming as she leaned over her paperwork.
Yet Ryan’s instincts immediately screamed otherwise.
Every fiber of his gut told him she was like a sleeping predator, concealing her true depth beneath a calm facade.
Just then, she raised her head, and their gazes met.
And in that single instant, he felt exposed, as if she were peeling back his layers and looking right through him.
Before he could process the sensation, a crushing force bore down on his shoulders without a warning.
The pressure hit him like an anvil, threatening to collapse his legs and force him to his knees.
Gritting his teeth, Ryan instinctively grounded his stance, channeling his mana to endure the force while forcing his facial features to remain completely calm.
He knew this was some kind of test, and she probably matched the output to his own strength, intending to measure his limits.
Trusting in his foundation and the grueling weeks he’d spent training, he tightened his grip and held his ground.
Soren watched from the side, a flicker of surprise passing through his eyes at Ryan’s quick reaction, but he chose not to interfere.
He was more interested in how easily she controlled the pressure and targeted Ryan.
A few moments later, the suffocating pressure vanished into thin air.
"Huff..." Ryan took a deep breath, letting the tension drain from his shoulders.
With a subtle flick of fire mana, the thin beads of sweat forming on his brow evaporated into steam before they could even fall.
He leaned forward and bowed respectfully, his voice steady.

You didn’t get any injuries, right?"

Everly.

chapters.title: Chapter 378: The Grand Puppet Theater [1]
paragraphs: ‘Hmm...’ Soren stared at the two floating windows in his vision and continued to track the updates in their mental states.
[Mental State: Curious, Suspicious, Analytical...]
[Mental State: Confused, Analytical, Determined...]

He was really curious what kind of questions Ramona was asking Ryan, considering how fast Ryan’s mental state was changing. One moment calm, the next baffled, then thoughtful, then confused again. It was like watching someone navigate a maze blindfolded.

However, he hoped Ryan could pass; otherwise, all their hard work would go down the drain. Still, Soren believed Ryan would pull through. Ramona had likely given him that warning to push his mental boundaries and test how he handled unexpected pressure when cornered.
A faint smile touched his lips as he waited for the interview to end.
About twenty minutes passed before Ryan and Ramona reappeared in the office.
Ryan looked a little lost, his expression dazed, as if he had just been through something he couldn’t quite process. Ramona’s expression, on the other hand, was unreadable as always.
Soren glanced between them, then asked, “How did it go, Lady Ramona? Did Ryan pass?”

Ramona gave a single nod and added, “The written exam will take place three days from now, and the practical exam will follow the day after. The exact times will be sent to you once the administrative staff processes his initial files.”
Soren nodded and turned to Ryan, clapping him on the shoulder. “Congratulations. You made it through the first step.”
“Ah, r-right!” Ryan snapped out of his daze, blinking a few times before giving a firm nod. He turned his attention back to Ramona, his expression carrying a mix of caution and lingering uncertainty.
Ramona casually flicked her hand. A small stack of documents materialized out of thin air, dropping onto the desk directly in front of Ryan.
“Please, read these carefully and fill them out,” she instructed smoothly.

“Understood.” Ryan nodded and took the papers, scanning through them carefully before starting to fill in the blanks. When he finished, Ramona called for an assistant, who led them out of the office to handle the remaining paperwork.
It took them more than half an hour to finish everything. Bidding farewell to the assistant, they made their way back to where Ethea and Zura were waiting. Zura spotted them first and waved.
“All done?” she asked.
“All done,” Soren confirmed.
“Good. Then I should get going. I still have work to do.” Zura turned to Ethea and pulled her into a quick hug. “Take care, Lea.”
“See you again.”

They said their goodbyes and left the academy the same way they came in. Soren drove straight to the weapon shop he had researched in advance. He wanted to buy new armor and boots for himself and Ryan. Their old ones were either already broken and beyond repair or didn’t meet their needs anymore.

And with the help of Eyes of Truth and Ryan’s strange luck ability, they managed to buy a few interesting and useful finds. Soren secured two sets of B-rank armor for himself, keeping a spare on hand in case the primary set took heavy damage. He also picked up a new pair of B-rank boots enchanted for mobility, featuring an automatic short-distance blink capability.

For Ryan, he bought a set of lightweight B-rank leather armor that wouldn’t restrict his agility, along with a pair of boots designed for high-speed maneuvers. He also bought another defense artifact for Ethea, adding another layer to her defenses.
After sorting out their gear, they returned to the hotel for lunch, then stopped by Ryan’s apartment to drop off Ethea before heading straight to the gate.
“By the way, can you tell me what she asked in the interview?” Soren asked as they drove to the Gate’s location. “There’s no need to force it if it’s supposed to be confidential, though.”

“No, it’s fine.” Ryan shook his head, then explained the details of the interview, from how the trivial questions about his biography and hobbies suddenly shifted into inquiries like taking lives. And then more questions about his inspirations and grades before jumping to whether he liked black tea or had eaten some kind of strange monster meat.
Soren nodded as he listened, the explanation filling in the gaps. ‘This is probably why his mental state had spiked so wildly.’
“...And she also asked about the Golden Gate. What happened, to be more exact.”
“...Did you tell her?” Soren asked after a pause.
“...No, not everything. I only told her about our fight with the drakes and the boss. But I felt like she knew or guessed what else happened.”
“She might have.” Soren agreed with Ryan’s view. After all, she was a Sage and a Sovereign. “But she didn’t say anything else about it?”

“Yes. She went quiet for a while, then moved on to the next question. She still asked a lot of weird, hard-to-answer questions, but thankfully, I managed to answer them all, and I think she was satisfied with my answers. Besides, I did my best to be as honest as possible because I had a feeling she could detect a lie the moment it left my mouth.”
“Good call.” Soren praised him. “That was a smart decision... By the way, Ryan. Do you think... I can tell Ethea what happened in the Golden Gate? But of course, I won’t tell everything in detail.”
“...” Ryan fell silent and lowered his head.
Soren didn’t have to look at his profile to tell he was conflicted.
“...Alright, I trust you. I also trust her, so,” Ryan finally said, “you can tell her.”
“Thank you.” Soren nodded. “Though if you want, you can tell her yourself. I’m sure she’d be happy to hear it from you too.”
“Huh?” Ryan’s eyes lit up. “I can?”
“Of course.”
“Then... I’ll do that. But you’ll be there too, right?”
Mm. Let’s have dinner together tonight. I’ll cook something good.”
Ryan agreed enthusiastically, and they continued talking about what to do inside the gate. Ten minutes later, they arrived at their destination.
The gate was located in the corner of the city, tucked away between two old buildings that had been converted into a checkpoint station.
A sign above the entrance read: ‘The Grand Puppet Theater — Third Circle Gate.’

They passed through the checking station, where the guards verified their identification and logged their entry. Once the formalities were complete, they stepped through the gate and found themselves in a theater.
“Whoa...” Ryan let out an exclamation at the sight.

Rows upon rows of velvet seats stretched out before them, filling the space from floor to ceiling, and every single one was occupied. Hundreds of figures sat in silence with their faces turned toward the stage, looking no different from any ordinary audience.

They breathed, blinked, and shifted slightly in their seats just like humans would. But with Eyes of Truth and Nature active, Soren could see the truth beneath the surface. They had no life force, and almost invisible threads descended from the ceiling, attaching to their limbs, their heads, and their spines, turning them into nothing more than puppets on strings.
The stage at the center was grand and imposing, framed by massive red curtains that had been drawn back. A spotlight shone down on the empty floorboards, waiting.
Then the curtains rustled.
“Welcome, honored guests.”
The voice came from everywhere and nowhere at once, echoing through the theater like a whisper and a roar combined.

“Once upon a time, there was a theater that never stopped performing. Every night, the actors took the stage, the audience watched, and the story reached its happy ending. But tonight... we have intruders.”
The voice paused, and the whole ‘audience’ turned in their direction, their eyes hollow. It looked a bit creepy, but Ryan and Soren had seen far worse, so they weren’t affected at all.
“Uninvited guests who wish to disrupt our tale. Let us show them what happens to those who interrupt a story before its final page.”

Soren and Ryan exchanged a glance. Nightfrost materialized in Soren’s hand, and Ryan summoned his beloved sword, its blade blazing with flames. At the same time, the nearest row of puppets rose from their seats and began walking toward them, while the rest turned back toward the stage.
“...Let the performance begin.”

“Alright, let the training begin,” Soren muttered at the same time and moved. He met the first puppet head-on, with Nightfrost already whirling in a strange pattern. The spear twisted through the air, and the puppet raised an arm to block, but the blade slipped past its guard at the last moment and pierced its chest.
‘Not bad, but not as I expected...’ Soren narrowed his eyes at the fallen puppet, recalling the technique’s details.

Coiling Strike was the foundation of the Ice Serpent Spear Arts. The spear moved in a serpentine pattern, weaving and twisting through the air to confuse and misdirect opponents. The key to mastering it was unpredictability. Each thrust had to flow into the next without a set rhythm or pattern, making it nearly impossible for enemies to track or parry. Speed mattered, but deception mattered more.
Soren had chosen this gate precisely because of its puppets. They were slow, predictable, and came in endless waves. Perfect for drilling the same form over and over until it became second nature.
‘I’ll learn it and raise my mastery as much as possible.’

chapters.title: Chapter 379: The Grand Puppet Theater [2]
paragraphs: Swoosh-!
Thud-!
Swoosh-!

Ryan kept cutting down the puppets, his flames flaring with each swing, but his eyes kept drifting toward Soren. The way he moved was mesmerizing to watch. He twisted the spear and coiled through the air like a living serpent, each move flowing into the next without pause.
’So that’s his new spear art,’ Ryan thought, a spark of admiration flashing through his mind. ’It looks fluid, but the underlying intent is vicious.’

Ryan knew a technique like that demanded complete mastery over one’s body and momentum. In the hands of an inexperienced fighter, those winding arcs would leave wide openings. But Soren, seasoned by countless life-or-death battles, was executing every twist, slash, and thrust with almost zero wasted motion, turning the deceptive maneuvers into a deadly net.
’...Should I try incorporating something similar into my style?’

The thought crossed Ryan’s mind for a split second before he shook his head and discarded it almost instantly. First, his weapon and affinities were fundamentally different. Second, Soren’s new technique relied on deception and continuous flow, while Ryan’s current style rested on decisive, single-strike efficiency. And finally, he knew that blindly copying someone else’s path would only hold him back from mastering his own strengths.
’Yeah, let’s focus on my own path...’
He tightened his grip on the sword’s handle and channeled his mana. The air around him grew hotter as the blade burst into a brilliant crimson blaze.

Ryan waited for five puppets to close in at once, their blades raised together. As soon as they entered his reach, he shifted his weight, pivoted sharply on his heel, and unleashed a fully powered Quick Slash.
A circular arc of flame exploded outward in one silent flash.

The blade passed through all five targets at once with zero resistance. The puppets froze mid-stride, their wooden bodies cut clean in half before the heat of his mana ignited their cores, bursting them into glowing embers that showered the carpet.
’Yeah, this is my style.’ Ryan nodded to himself.

Just like that, they kept advancing together, carving a path through the endless rows of seats. The puppets kept coming, wave after wave, but they moved in sync, covering each other’s blind spots and cutting down anything that came too close.

Most were weak, barely worth the effort, but a few stood out. One had blades for fingers that spun like saws, forcing Ryan to duck and weave before he found an opening. Another could stretch its limbs like rubber, attacking from unexpected angles until Soren froze it and shattered it into fragments of ice. Another had a porcelain face that cracked and reformed every time it was struck, making it hard to land a finishing blow until Ryan burned it to ash with a concentrated burst of flames.
But those were just the warm-up.
As they finished all the ’audience puppets’ and finally arrived at the stage, the curtains on either side drew back fully, revealing four figures standing in a line.

"You monsters!" The first one shouted, pointing a glowing sword at them. He looked like a hero straight out of a fairy tale, with signature golden hair and a righteous expression burning in his eyes. "To slaughter innocent people without mercy... In the name of justice, I will cut you down!"

The second figure stepped forward, a massive two-and-a-half-meter frame carrying a shield in one hand and a mace in the other. His voice boomed across the theater. "I will smash you both and bring justice to the fallen!"
The third figure floated high above the stage, clutching a staff. Their eyes burned with killing intent as they stared down at Soren and Ryan. "You... will pay for this."
As for the fourth figure, they had long disappeared from view. It was probably an assassin figure.

"So these are the Hero’s Party?" Ryan muttered, recalling what Soren had said on the way. They had to defeat these four to summon the boss and clear the Gate. "Should we take two each or battle together?
"...Let’s just enjoy the fight," Soren said, a smile curling at his lips. "This is a good chance to test ourselves."
"I’ll fight the hero then," Ryan said.
Without another word, Ryan kicked off the stage floor and burst toward the blond swordsman. The knight raised his glowing blade to meet him, his face locked in a righteous snarl.
"For light and glory!" the hero shouted, bringing his sword down in a brilliant arc.

Ryan didn’t activate his flames immediately. He wanted to test his pure swordsmanship against an opponent built around blade techniques. He raised his sword and deflected the heavy strike with a precise parry.
Clang!

The sharp ring of steel echoed through the grand theater. Ryan absorbed the impact through his shoulders, pivoted swiftly, and sliced at the knight’s torso. But the hero construct moved fluidly, twisted his waist, stepped inside Ryan’s guard, and delivered a rapid thrust aimed straight at Ryan’s throat.
’He’s fast,’ Ryan realized, his eyes narrowing.
Swoosh-!

He raised his sword just in time to parry again, then swept it upward, throwing the hero off balance. Exploiting the brief opening, Ryan stepped forward and launched a piercing counterattack directly at the hero.
The hero reacted instantly, stomping his lead foot onto the stage floorboards.
"Radiant Vanguard!"

A sudden burst of blinding golden light erupted from his sword, forming an ethereal barrier of compressed mana that slammed into Ryan’s blade, pushed him back three paces, and seamlessly transitioned into a thrusting follow-up attack.

As the glowing tip of the hero’s sword lunged toward his chest, a sudden prickle of cold static raced down the back of Ryan’s neck. The soundless air behind him distorted, revealing twin daggers slipping toward his neck.
Swoosh-!

Ryan dropped his weight, letting the hero’s strike pass over his head as he twisted mid-air to slip between the two opponents. The hero’s sword thrust into empty space, clashing with the assassin’s daggers in a metallic screech.
Before either opponent could recover from the collision, Ryan planted his foot, using the momentum of his mid-air spin to drive his blade straight into the hero’s flank.

The edge caught the hero right beneath his armplate, cutting deep through the outer armor and releasing a shower of bright sparks. The heavy blow forced a muffled groan from the hero, making him stumble two steps sideways.

Ryan pulled his blade back for a follow-up, but the assassin had already moved to his right, slashing viciously across his ribs. He quickly shifted his stance and snapped his blade up in a swift, sharp arc to meet the incoming daggers.
Clang!
The collision pushed the assassin back a few steps, but Ryan couldn’t follow up with a counterattack as dozens of swords of light rained down on him.
’Shadow Steps!’

Ryan’s body instantly vanished into a blurred trail of speed. He wove between the falling swords of light, every blade of energy piercing empty floorboards right behind his heels. Before the light show faded, he executed a shadow blink, vanishing from the hero’s sight and reappearing directly behind him.

He didn’t give the swordsman a second to turn. His blade flashed in a blazing arc, the strike slicing cleanly through the hero’s neck. The head and torso crashed to the stage in a burst of embers and molten metal.
Without pausing to watch the hero crumble, he slammed his heel onto the floorboards.
Whoosh-!

A wave of vivid black fire erupted outward, sweeping across the entire stage. The spreading flames outlined a faint human silhouette creeping along the left prop wall, instantly forcing the assassin out of hiding.
’Shadow Steps!’

Ryan closed the distance and sent two crescent-shaped fire slashes flying toward the assassin. It reacted instantly, its silhouette flickering into nonexistence as it attempted to blink away through the shadows.
Ryan merely smiled. Having tracked its movements throughout the fight, he had already calculated the exact maximum range and timing of its short spatial jumps.
’There!’
Ryan pivoted toward a spot three meters to his left, drawing his blade back into his waistline. The moment the assassin reappeared in the air, his daggers mid-raise, Ryan unleashed his Quick Slash.
A single line of intense black heat split the air.
The assassin’s head separated from his shoulders, the clean cut holding for just a heartbeat before the entire figure dissolved into a harmless cloud of dark fog.
However, Ryan didn’t even pause. Reversing his grip on the hilt, he deftly jabbed the blade backward through the narrow gap between his arm and chest, thrusting it into the empty space behind him.
Pfft!
The tip sank deep into the real assassin who materialized behind him.
A faint gasp escaped the assassin’s lips as black flames flared along the steel, burning it away from the inside out until nothing remained but fading cinders.
Ryan exhaled slowly and straightened up. He had wanted to test his pure swordsmanship, but in the end, he still ended up using a technique.
’Well, at least there’s still a boss.’
He then turned toward Soren, who had already brought down the mage and the tank. The mage was shattered into fragments of ice, while the tank was reduced to a headless sculpture of ice.
"Get ready," he muttered to Ryan, his gaze fixed on the ceiling. "We have company."

Thud-!
Swoosh-!
Ryan kept cutting down the puppets, his flames flaring with each swing, but his eyes kept drifting toward Soren.
The way he moved was mesmerizing to watch.
He twisted the spear and coiled through the air like a living serpent, each move flowing into the next without pause.
’So that’s his new spear art,’ Ryan thought, a spark of admiration flashing through his mind. ’It looks fluid, but the underlying intent is vicious.’
Ryan knew a technique like that demanded complete mastery over one’s body and momentum.
In the hands of an inexperienced fighter, those winding arcs would leave wide openings.
But Soren, seasoned by countless life-or-death battles, was executing every twist, slash, and thrust with almost zero wasted motion, turning the deceptive maneuvers into a deadly net.
’...Should I try incorporating something similar into my style?’
The thought crossed Ryan’s mind for a split second before he shook his head and discarded it almost instantly.
First, his weapon and affinities were fundamentally different.
Second, Soren’s new technique relied on deception and continuous flow, while Ryan’s current style rested on decisive, single-strike efficiency.
And finally, he knew that blindly copying someone else’s path would only hold him back from mastering his own strengths.
’Yeah, let’s focus on my own path...’
He tightened his grip on the sword’s handle and channeled his mana.
The air around him grew hotter as the blade burst into a brilliant crimson blaze.
Ryan waited for five puppets to close in at once, their blades raised together.
As soon as they entered his reach, he shifted his weight, pivoted sharply on his heel, and unleashed a fully powered Quick Slash.
A circular arc of flame exploded outward in one silent flash.
The blade passed through all five targets at once with zero resistance.
The puppets froze mid-stride, their wooden bodies cut clean in half before the heat of his mana ignited their cores, bursting them into glowing embers that showered the carpet.
’Yeah, this is my style.’ Ryan nodded to himself.

The puppets kept coming, wave after wave, but they moved in sync, covering each other’s blind spots and cutting down anything that came too close.
Most were weak, barely worth the effort, but a few stood out.
One had blades for fingers that spun like saws, forcing Ryan to duck and weave before he found an opening.
Another could stretch its limbs like rubber, attacking from unexpected angles until Soren froze it and shattered it into fragments of ice.
Another had a porcelain face that cracked and reformed every time it was struck, making it hard to land a finishing blow until Ryan burned it to ash with a concentrated burst of flames.
But those were just the warm-up.
As they finished all the ’audience puppets’ and finally arrived at the stage, the curtains on either side drew back fully, revealing four figures standing in a line.
"You monsters!" The first one shouted, pointing a glowing sword at them.
He looked like a hero straight out of a fairy tale, with signature golden hair and a righteous expression burning in his eyes.
"To slaughter innocent people without mercy...
In the name of justice, I will cut you down!"
The second figure stepped forward, a massive two-and-a-half-meter frame carrying a shield in one hand and a mace in the other.
His voice boomed across the theater.
"I will smash you both and bring justice to the fallen!"
The third figure floated high above the stage, clutching a staff.
Their eyes burned with killing intent as they stared down at Soren and Ryan.
"You... will pay for this."
As for the fourth figure, they had long disappeared from view.
It was probably an assassin figure.
"So these are the Hero’s Party?" Ryan muttered, recalling what Soren had said on the way.
They had to defeat these four to summon the boss and clear the Gate.
"Should we take two each or battle together?
"...Let’s just enjoy the fight," Soren said, a smile curling at his lips.
"This is a good chance to test ourselves."
"I’ll fight the hero then," Ryan said.
Without another word, Ryan kicked off the stage floor and burst toward the blond swordsman.
The knight raised his glowing blade to meet him, his face locked in a righteous snarl.
"For light and glory!" the hero shouted, bringing his sword down in a brilliant arc.
Ryan didn’t activate his flames immediately.
He wanted to test his pure swordsmanship against an opponent built around blade techniques.
He raised his sword and deflected the heavy strike with a precise parry.
Clang!
The sharp ring of steel echoed through the grand theater.
Ryan absorbed the impact through his shoulders, pivoted swiftly, and sliced at the knight’s torso.
But the hero construct moved fluidly, twisted his waist, stepped inside Ryan’s guard, and delivered a rapid thrust aimed straight at Ryan’s throat.
’He’s fast,’ Ryan realized, his eyes narrowing.
Swoosh-!
He raised his sword just in time to parry again, then swept it upward, throwing the hero off balance.
Exploiting the brief opening, Ryan stepped forward and launched a piercing counterattack directly at the hero.
The hero reacted instantly, stomping his lead foot onto the stage floorboards.
"Radiant Vanguard!"

A sudden burst of blinding golden light erupted from his sword, forming an ethereal barrier of compressed mana that slammed into Ryan’s blade, pushed him back three paces, and seamlessly transitioned into a thrusting follow-up attack.
As the glowing tip of the hero’s sword lunged toward his chest, a sudden prickle of cold static raced down the back of Ryan’s neck.
The soundless air behind him distorted, revealing twin daggers slipping toward his neck.
Swoosh-!

The hero’s sword thrust into empty space, clashing with the assassin’s daggers in a metallic screech.

chapters.title: Chapter 380: The Grand Puppet Theater [End]
paragraphs: Ryan turned toward the ceiling and saw the boss monster - the Puppeteer.

It hovered high in the rafters, a tall human-like figure draped in a pitch-black coat that swayed without wind. Its face was smooth and blurry, lacking eyes, nose, or a mouth, as if the features had been erased from existence. Dozens of glowing silver threads extended from its pale, slender fingers, stretching like a web into every corner of the grand theater.
"...You ruined such a masterpiece." It spoke, then suddenly dove straight at them. "You will have to become what you have destroyed."

Its fingers twitched at blinding speed, and the silver threads snapped taut, slashing through the air in overlapping arcs. The attack carried immense speed and condensed mana, cutting through space with the same deadly precision as Ryan’s Quick Slash; no, they were even faster and deadlier.
Swoosh-!

The threads carved through the stage, reducing the floor to splinters and sending rubble flying. The grand curtains were sliced into ribbons that drifted down, and the backdrops collapsed as the lines tore through their supports. Soren and Ryan dove in opposite directions, the threads whistling past close enough to graze their skin.
The boss pursued them, its pale fingers twisting into fluid patterns. The silver lines swept out again, producing sharp crescent waves of force that mirrored Ryan’s technique with cleaner execution.

Ryan narrowed his eyes as he dodged, observing it closely. The threads moved in perfect sync, each one following a slightly different arc to create a web of slashes that covered every possible escape route, and he twisted through the gaps as best he could, but a thread caught his shoulder, slicing through his armor and drawing blood.
’I see, so this is the infamous Perfect Replication.’

It really did replicate perfectly, and even improved the technique to suit its own style. The threads didn’t have the limitations of a physical blade, so they could attack from angles he couldn’t, change direction mid-strike, and cover more ground in less time.
’I think I can really get inspiration from this! Thank you, Brother So-!’

Before Ryan could rejoice, the boss landed on the broken stage and changed its style. The threads stopped slashing and started coiling, twisting, and weaving in unpredictable patterns before striking like snakes.
’Damn it!’

Ryan cursed and dodged strikes aimed at his vital points, but two hidden strikes still managed to hit him and send him flying. Ryan now understood how tricky Soren’s Coiling Strike was and used Shadow Steps to distance himself from the boss while watching Soren, who seemed engrossed in his own observations as he dodged masterfully.
’...Let’s just wait for my turn then.’ He muttered inwardly and swallowed a healing potion.

And just like that, they spent the next ten minutes watching the boss replicate their techniques and refining their understanding. Only after they had learned everything they could did they launch a counterattack.

Ryan set the surrounding webs ablaze with black flames, burning the lines straight back to the boss’s hands. At the same time, Soren froze the remaining threads and shattered them into snowflakes with a flick of his finger.
"You... leave me no choice..."
The boss muttered, severed the ruined strands, and let the burnt, frozen remnants drop to the floor.

Then, its tall frame distorted as six additional arms tore through its coat, fingers tipped with needle-like points. Its body expanded to over four meters as the ceiling above split open into a dark void. Hundreds of new puppets dropped from above, connected to the massive cables extending from the eight-armed boss.
"Is this the hidden phase?" Ryan muttered, turning to Soren beside him.
"Mm. Do you want to observe more?"
Ryan shook his head. "I’ve seen enough."
"Then let me take care of this." Soren took a step forward. "We’ve wasted enough time."
Ryan nodded and backed away to give him space.
Soren took a deep breath and raised his palm, staring coldly at the falling puppets.

The next moment, countless ice swords started to materialize beside him, filling the air in a dense formation. Another set formed above the horde of puppets, their tips pointed downward like a second sky of frozen blades.
Soren waited until all the puppets emerged, then lowered his hand decisively.
Swoosh-! Swoosh-!

The swords launched at once, and those beside him shot forward like a volley of arrows, tearing through the puppets’ front line and freezing whatever they touched. The ones above rained down from the ceiling, impaling the puppets and pinning them to the floor. They shattered under the onslaught, and the air filled with the sound of cracking joints and snapping strings.
Before the survivors could even react, Soren gently tapped his foot against the floor.
Whoosh-!

In an instant, a raging wave of frost surged outward from the point of contact, bursting upward into jagged ice spikes that pierced the remaining puppets from below. They were knocked off their feet and shattered into frozen fragments that rained down like snow.
"Amazing..."

Ryan gaped in awe at the sheer scale and efficiency of the execution. Turning his head toward the eight-armed boss, he couldn’t help but think that if it had a face, it would have been completely bewildered.
"You..." The boss’s voice echoed again, confused and enraged at the same time. "You-argh!"
It gave a distorted roar, thrust all eight arms forward, and lunged straight at Soren.

"..." Soren raised Nighfrost and exhaled softly, twisting his body into a fluid stance. Then the spear moved, its tip tracing a circle in the air before snapping forward, pulling back, and circling again from a different angle. The movement was hypnotic, almost serpentine, and each time the boss swung his arms at him, they struck only empty air.
With each circular motion, the air chilled rapidly, weaving an inescapable web of ice around the monster’s defenses.

Soren stepped in close, the spear flowing around the boss’s guard like water around a stone. Each attack found its mark, severing one arm after another, and as the assault peaked, the condensed frost formed a massive ice serpent that coiled around Nightfrost, opened its jaws wide, and clamped down on its torso. Soren finished the sequence with a single, clean cut that split the puppet from shoulder to hip.
"Argh-!"
The monster screamed in agony, and Soren drove his spear forward one final time, severing the puppet’s head from its body.
