chapters.title: Chapter 381: Dinner
paragraphs: Soren watched the Puppeteer fall apart, its limbs and torso collapsing inward. He stepped quickly and plucked the core before it could hit the ground. Then countless messages appeared in his vision.
[Ding!]
[Equity Stake Liquidated]
[Target: Theater Puppet]
[Stake: 100%]
[Dividend: +90 Refined Mana]
[Equity Stake Liquidated]
[Target: The Puppeteer]
[Stake: 100%]
[Dividend: +1000 Refined Mana]
’Good, with this, I absorbed about twelve thousand mana.’ His eyes glinted in satisfaction. ’A few more Gates, and then it will be done.’
With that thought, he turned toward Ryan. "Let’s gather the loot and leave the place."
"Yes!" Ryan replied enthusiastically and started picking up the mana cores the other puppets had left behind.

About ten minutes later, they finished, divided the loot, and headed out through the exit portal. They stopped by an exchange shop to sell the loot, then drove back to Ryan’s apartment to pick up Ethea. After they returned to the hotel, Soren helped Ethea change and attend to her other needs, while Ryan was left alone in the living room to prepare the snacks and set the table.
Soren wheeled Ethea into the living room and brought her up to the table.
"You two wait here," Soren said, positioning the wheelchair securely. "I’ll start dinner."

Ryan and Ethea both nodded. Soren turned and walked into the kitchen, pulled out his cooking equipment, and got ready to start. But even as he set out the ingredients, he kept his ears on the living room, listening to their conversation.
"...Sister-in-law, I heard you wanted to know about what really happened in the Golden Gate back then."
"Yes. If it’s ok, I want to learn more about it. But if you’d rather not talk about it, I understand. You don’t have to force yourself."
"No, it’s alright, but..." Ryan paused, and Soren could tell what he was about to say. "Can you promise not to tell anyone else? What I’m about to say... it’s not something I want spreading around."
"...I promise." Soren heard Ethea’s sincere voice. "Whatever you say stays between us. I won’t repeat a word of it to anyone. Well, aside from my husband."
"Haha, right, you can freely talk to Brother Soren about it. But I really appreciate your understanding." Ryan then took a deep breath. "It all started when we discovered the Golden Gate..."

Soren listened to Ryan’s tale while his hands moved automatically across the counter. He prepped the meat, trimmed the vegetables, and set the pans on the stove, their sizzle blending into the background.
Ryan kept the story general and didn’t go into too much detail.

He told her that after being thrown into the Golden Gate, he had lost consciousness and drifted through dreamlike scenarios that felt real but weren’t. He mentioned he had no idea how much time had passed before he finally opened his eyes and found Soren there.

He then described the Sunless Reliquary and spoke briefly about being chosen as a successor. He also told her about their conversation and his acceptance of his master’s inheritance. However, he didn’t tell her about who his master was or what happened during the inheritance process, nor did he mention the exact nature of the legacy he received.

Ethea also listened silently, and after some time, Ryan finally finished his story. Then they started talking about the incident, and the topic gradually shifted to his upcoming exams. He asked for her guidance, and she gave her suggestions.

Soren was glad to ’see’ them getting along so well, and found himself imagining a future moment when his little sister, Nura, could sit at the same table with them. It would bring back a piece of his life he thought he had lost for good.

Come to think of it, Ethea had mentioned seeing her earlier this morning and insisted they find a way to step in as soon as possible, pull her clear of the family’s influence, and save her before things got any worse.
’...Let’s think about this more carefully.’
His thoughts naturally turned toward the problem. By the time he finished plating the food and bringing the dishes over to the table, he had the outlines of a plan forming in his head.
"Dinner’s ready."
Ryan stood up hurriedly and took his own portion while Soren placed Ethea’s and his own.
"What were you guys talking about?" He asked as he sat down. "Can I join in?"
"Mm. We were talking about his upcoming transfer exam." Ethea answered with a smile. "I was giving my opinions about what to expect and do."

"I see." Soren nodded, understanding that he hadn’t missed out that much. Then, as if he’d remembered something, he turned to Ryan. "Speaking of which, should we hold off on the Gates until your exams are over? You might need the time to study."

"It’s alright." Ryan shook his head without missing a beat. "I’m not worried about the written exam, so we can keep going. Besides, clearing Gates helps me grow stronger and sharpen my skills, which is far more useful for the practical exam anyway."

"The practical exam might involve surviving in a Gate, so I recommended he spend more time on field experience," Ethea added. "The academy puts a lot of effort into training students in real Gates from the third year onward, so they can adapt to the real world more easily. That’s why diving into Gates will prepare him far more than reading textbooks."
"That’s right, so you shouldn’t worry about it, Brother Soren." Ryan grinned and dug into his food.
"Haha, that’s a relief." Soren chuckled as he reached for Ethea’s bowl. "It actually saves me the trouble of finding another party member while you’re busy."
"Huh?" Ryan paused mid-bite, his spoon hovering in the air. "Wait, what about the exam days then? You’ll be going alone?"
Soren raised a brow. "What do you mean? I will head to the academy with you and wait outside. Missing two days of diving won’t hurt us."
"...Thank you." Ryan smiled at him, then watched as Soren gently fed Ethea a bite before quickly looking down at his own bowl. ’...Right. Just focus on the meal.’

He prepped the meat, trimmed the vegetables, and set the pans on the stove, their sizzle blending into the background.
Ryan kept the story general and didn’t go into too much detail.
He told her that after being thrown into the Golden Gate, he had lost consciousness and drifted through dreamlike scenarios that felt real but weren’t.
He mentioned he had no idea how much time had passed before he finally opened his eyes and found Soren there.
He then described the Sunless Reliquary and spoke briefly about being chosen as a successor.
He also told her about their conversation and his acceptance of his master’s inheritance.
However, he didn’t tell her about who his master was or what happened during the inheritance process, nor did he mention the exact nature of the legacy he received.
Ethea also listened silently, and after some time, Ryan finally finished his story.
Then they started talking about the incident, and the topic gradually shifted to his upcoming exams.
He asked for her guidance, and she gave her suggestions.
Soren was glad to ’see’ them getting along so well, and found himself imagining a future moment when his little sister, Nura, could sit at the same table with them.
It would bring back a piece of his life he thought he had lost for good.

Come to think of it, Ethea had mentioned seeing her earlier this morning and insisted they find a way to step in as soon as possible, pull her clear of the family’s influence, and save her before things got any worse.
’...Let’s think about this more carefully.’
His thoughts naturally turned toward the problem.
By the time he finished plating the food and bringing the dishes over to the table, he had the outlines of a plan forming in his head.
"Dinner’s ready."
Ryan stood up hurriedly and took his own portion while Soren placed Ethea’s and his own.
"What were you guys talking about?" He asked as he sat down.
"Can I join in?"
"Mm.
We were talking about his upcoming transfer exam." Ethea answered with a smile.
"I was giving my opinions about what to expect and do."
"I see." Soren nodded, understanding that he hadn’t missed out that much.
Then, as if he’d remembered something, he turned to Ryan.
"Speaking of which, should we hold off on the Gates until your exams are over?
You might need the time to study."
"It’s alright." Ryan shook his head without missing a beat.
"I’m not worried about the written exam, so we can keep going.
Besides, clearing Gates helps me grow stronger and sharpen my skills, which is far more useful for the practical exam anyway."
"The practical exam might involve surviving in a Gate, so I recommended he spend more time on field experience," Ethea added.
"The academy puts a lot of effort into training students in real Gates from the third year onward, so they can adapt to the real world more easily.
That’s why diving into Gates will prepare him far more than reading textbooks."
"That’s right, so you shouldn’t worry about it, Brother Soren." Ryan grinned and dug into his food.
"Haha, that’s a relief." Soren chuckled as he reached for Ethea’s bowl.
"It actually saves me the trouble of finding another party member while you’re busy."
"Huh?" Ryan paused mid-bite, his spoon hovering in the air.
"Wait, what about the exam days then?
You’ll be going alone?"
Soren raised a brow.
"What do you mean?
I will head to the academy with you and wait outside.
Missing two days of diving won’t hurt us."
"...Thank you." Ryan smiled at him, then watched as Soren gently fed Ethea a bite before quickly looking down at his own bowl. ’...Right.
Just focus on the meal.’

chapters.title: Chapter 382: Cooking Together [1]
paragraphs: Three days passed in the blink of an eye. Today was the written exam day, and Ryan had already entered the examination hall. As for Ethea, Zura had taken her away for ’sightseeing’. And so, Soren was sitting alone near the exam building, waiting for them to come back. However, it was good for him too: he could finally sort through his thoughts and plan what to do next.
’Hmm... Let’s start with the gains in the past few days...’

First, the gates. Over the past four days, they’d cleared seven in total: six 3rd Circle Gates and one 4th Circle Gate. As a result, he’d gained about 105,000 mana. He also absorbed about 10,000 mana from the Threads’ daily returns.

Furthermore, he had received three more investment returns from Ethea, Ryan, and Zura. Ryan and Zura’s investment grade had been high and gave him 75,000 mana/mana capacity, +2 Cooking Mastery, a Fire Resistance ability upgrade, and basic teaching knowledge.

As for Ethea’s returns, his Frost Armor had strengthened and evolved, gaining the ability to gradually absorb ambient mana from its surroundings to repair itself. It also granted him 50,000 mana, along with 20,000 mental power and mental capacity. He also cultivated and absorbed about 20,000 mana and 6,000 mental power in his free time.
In total, he had gained about 250,000 mana and an extra 125,000 mana capacity, 26,000 mental power and an extra 20,000 mental power capacity.
So right now, his status was like this:
[Mana Capacity: 800,860 / 880,000]
[Mental Power Capacity: 187,740 / 200,000]

’...If I go into four more third circle Gates, I will be able to reach the peak of 4th circle easily.’ He narrowed his eyes. ’As for a location to break through, I should discuss it with the Vice Principal Ramona. If she is willing to let me stay and break through in the academy, it will be much safer than doing it in a hotel room.’

Furthermore, he might be able to invest in her using valuable mental power-related elixirs in his possession. Although they probably wouldn’t affect her much considering how high her cultivation was, they would still serve as a gesture of goodwill. And if it helped her even a little, that would be worth it.
He nodded to himself and shifted his thoughts to the plan to rescue Nura and cure her illness.
’...I should still break through first and then put my focus on it.’

Once he was 5th Circle and learned how to fly after mastering Frost Wings to some extent, only then would he be able to fight against his former family. He would also unlock Winter’s Rebirth effect of his constitution, which would serve as a valuable trump card.

However, that didn’t mean he planned to sit back and do nothing while waiting. In fact, over the past three nights, he had spent his free time practicing new recipes, steadily improving his proficiency in Exquisite Magic Meals with each attempt. And today, he planned to practice the recipe he prepared for Nura. Zura would help him with the process since it was a fire-element-oriented dish. She had also agreed to serve as his test subject.

’I should invite Ryan too. He will learn flame manipulation by watching and become the second test subject.’ Soren smiled, already imagining the scene in his mind. ’The more feedback I get, the faster I can refine the dish before giving it to Nura.’
However, even if the dish turned out perfect, there was still one major hurdle standing in his way: getting it to Nura without any interference and ensuring its effects took root properly.
’...I’ll have to discuss it with Lady Zura later.’

As for her missing memories, they could only deal with it after improving her physical condition. And part of the delay stemmed from their inability to locate Grandma Kanie, despite Maalkor scouring the entire city over the past few days. Her absence suggested she was far more powerful, and far more skilled at hiding and erasing her tracks, than they had initially assumed.
’...In the worst case, we might have to ask help from the princess.’
With a sigh, he stood up from the bench and made his way toward the administration building.

Later that afternoon, they all gathered in the kitchen. Soren, Zura, and Ryan had each put on special cooking gloves and matching aprons, standing around the counter like a team of chefs. Meanwhile, Ethea watched them from nearby, a soft plushie resembling Soren sitting on her lap with a cute expression.

"Whoa," Zura exclaimed, looking down at her apron before glancing over at the rest of them. She let out a short laugh and shook her head. "We look like we’re preparing to set a record-breaking meal or something, right?"
The others laughed softly, and the tension in the room eased a little.
Soren smiled at the sight, exhaled softly, and rubbed his hands together. "Well, should we start then?"
"Ready when you are!" Zura declared, raising a gloved hand. "Though I reserve the right to sue you if your experimental cuisine sets my hair on fire."
"I’m ready too!" Ryan added from the side. "I’ll pay close attention to your flame control and do my best to learn, Lady Zura."
"Good, that’s the spirit!" Zura encouraged him with a grin.

"Then let’s start by preparing the ingredients," Soren explained. "First, we’ll cut the Ember Carrots, Ashgold Onions, and Scarlet Sunfruit. We’ll prepare the Inferno Cabbage afterward, then deal with the meat and rice."

He gently took out the magic vegetables one by one and placed them on the counter. The temperature in the kitchen rose almost immediately, the solar mana radiating from the ingredients warming the air around them.
"Chef Zura, can you help me control their flame mana? And tell me if I make a mistake."
"Got it, Chef Soren!" Zura giggled while raising her hands, her palms glowing faintly as she began to regulate the heat.

Soren nodded and picked up his knife. His hands moved with practiced precision, slicing through the ember carrots first. Each cut was clean and even, the pieces falling onto the cutting board in perfect uniformity. Next came the ashgold onions, their golden layers parting easily beneath his blade. Then the scarlet sunfruits, their red flesh gleaming as he diced them into neat cubes.
Zura watched closely, occasionally calling out his mistakes and offering suggestions.
"I think you are putting too much power on the carrots. You might wanna tone it down a little, or you’ll bruise the veins and leak the mana before they hit the pan..."
"Urgh, if you don’t slow down while cutting onions, we’re all going to cry ourselves to death! Urgh, my eyes!"
"A little slower on the sunfruit too. The skin’s tougher than it looks, and if you rush it, the juices might spill out and burn."
From the other side of the counter, Ryan watched every movement without blinking, taking in how Soren guided the blade and how Zura subtly controlled the volatile fire mana.
Swing... Swing... Swing...
Soren adjusted his pace each time, and the vegetables piled up neatly on the cutting board, their colors vibrant and their aromas filling the kitchen.
"Good! This is how it’s done!"
"Yeah! You’re doing great, Chef Soren!"
And the chatterbox Zura didn’t forget to throw in a constant stream of playful praise. Soren didn’t mind it at first and even found it strangely funny.

Noticeable as it was, Ryan and Ethea caught sight of the smile tugging at his lips. They exchanged a brief glance, a spark of mischief passing between them, before joining in the cheering. Soon enough, their voices overlapped with Zura’s, filling the kitchen with a noisy chorus of encouragement.
"Nice cut, Brother Soren!"
"That’s perfect, dear."
Fortunately, despite the distraction, Soren managed to finish without any major mistakes.
Zura wiped an imaginary sweat from her forehead and leaned against the counter, flashing a bright grin. "Alright, chef! What’s next on the menu?"
"Let me see if the water is ready," Soren said, stepping toward the large copper pot resting on the stove.

He lifted the lid slightly, feeling a pleasant burst of warm steam hit his face. The liquid inside was bubbling steadily at a full boil. Satisfied, he picked up a wooden bowl filled with shimmering grains of Aureole Rice and carefully tipped them into the pot.
Zura tilted her head, sniffing the crisp scent rising with the steam. "Wait, is this water special too? It smells different from regular water."

Soren nodded as he stirred the grains once with a long spoon before putting the heavy lid back on. "It’s called Dawnwater. It holds a faint trace of morning light, which helps soften the tough outer shell of Aureole Rice without stripping away its natural energy."
Stepping away from the boiling pot, he shifted his focus to the empty cooking pot nearby.
"Now," he said, glancing at Zura and Ryan, "we can start the stove."

chapters.title: Chapter 383: Cooking Together [2]
paragraphs: "Ooh, what is this oil?!"
"Oh, this?" Soren held up the small glass jar filled with a thick, amber-red liquid. "It’s Flamehorn Essence."
"Wait, Flamehorn?" Zura’s eyes lit up instantly. "You mean that rare magic beast living near active volcanoes?"
"The very same." Soren nodded, carefully uncorking the jar and pouring a small splash into the warm pan. "While it heats up, let’s prepare the meat and the rest of the ingredients."
He reached into his inventory and pulled out a thick slab of meat, its deep crimson surface threaded with thin black lines like veins of cooling magma.
"Wait, let me guess!" Zura leaned closer, her eyes narrowing as she studied the meat. "This is fire dragon meat, right?"
Soren raised a brow, a bit surprised by her reaction. "You know it?"

"Of course," Zura said, puffing out her chest slightly and nodding proudly. "I’ve had dishes made with it a few times before. But..." Her expression hardened as if she recalled a terrible memory. "Every time, it was bland and hard to chew. The texture was like rubber, and the flavor was practically nonexistent. I only forced myself to eat it because the benefits were good for my cultivation."
"Is that so?"
"Mm. And..." She pinched her nose and stepped back a few paces. "I don’t remember it smelling like this either. Are you sure this is the real deal? You didn’t get scammed, right?"
Soren chuckled softly, shaking his head at her reaction. "Don’t worry, I’m confident in my eye for quality. It’s definitely the real deal."
"Then why does it stink so much?" Zura asked, still holding her nose with one hand while gesturing toward the cutting board.

"The smell comes from those black lines," Soren explained, pointing his blade at the dark veins running through the crimson flesh. "They’re called magma veins. They store the dragon’s residual fire mana, along with the impurities and toxins its body couldn’t expel while it was alive. That’s where the odor comes from. We have to remove them carefully without damaging the rest of the meat or spilling too much blood."
"I see, but," she stared at him, narrowing her eyes, "why are you fine? Can’t you smell it?"
"What do you mean I can’t?" Soren gave her a wry smile. "Honestly, with my senses, I’m probably smelling it ten times worse than you are. But I’m the chef, so I don’t have much of a choice."
"Ah, right, forget I asked," Zura muttered, shaking her head. "I keep forgetting you’re built different from the rest of us. So... we’ll leave all of that to you!"

She quickly distanced herself again, retreating to the far side of the kitchen and even putting up a small barrier around herself. Ryan chuckled softly from around the corner, having already positioned himself as far away as possible. Ethea giggled at their antics and hugged the plushie tightly, saying, ’Fighting, dear!’
Soren’s lips twitched. They had already left the barrier surrounding the working space, so there was no need to go that far away, right?
"...Let’s just finish this as soon as possible.
With a sigh, he adjusted his grip on the knife, focused his attention on the dark streaks running through the meat, and got straight to work.
’...Endure it, Soren.’
’This is nothing...’
’...Think about your sister...’

The suffocating odor clung relentlessly to the back of his throat, making his nose twitch nonstop, yet his fingers remained dead steady as the blade traced the dark veins. Five grueling minutes passed before the final streak lifted free, prompting him to instantly freeze the discarded impurities into solid ice and stow them away with a flick of his wrist.
’Malakor, can you get rid of these and the smell, please?’
’Leave it to me, Master.’
’Thank you.’

Soren smiled faintly as Malakor whisked the frozen waste away, dissolving the trapped reek until the surrounding air became clean and odorless. Reaching into his storage, he then pulled out a small diffuser jar filled with crushed Star-Anise Blossom, uncorked it over the counter, and released a sweet aroma that swept away the stale emptiness and lifted his spirits.

With the air restored, he gently washed the good parts of the meat and then sliced it into a few smaller parts. He then stepped out of the barrier, picked up the bowl of prepped Ashgold Onions, and slid them straight into the shimmering Flamehorn Oil.
Whoosh-!
Hisss-!

The oil reacted instantly, flaring up in a burst of orange flame. Soren then picked up the skimmer and stirred the onions, moving them around so they cooked evenly. He waited until they turned crimson, and without breaking his rhythm, he fetched the prepped Ember Carrots and Scarlet Sunfruits and slid them directly on top of the onions.

He kept stirring, mixing them with the onions, and watched as the sunfruit’s red flesh deepened to a darker crimson and the carrots softened at the edges. Once they reached the exact texture he wanted, he laid the clean slices of Fire Dragon meat right over the sizzling base. The crimson flesh seared against the intense heat, releasing a rich and strangely mouthwatering aroma.
’Good, but let’s do our best not to repeat yesterday’s mistake...’

He recalled how he half-burned the fire dragon meat during yesterday’s practice and heightened his senses to control the mana and essence. After a minute, he smiled in satisfaction, then picked up a pinch of crushed Crimson Salt and dusted it evenly over the surface to lock in the juices and bring out the meat’s savory depth.
Drawn back to the station by the intoxicating scent, Zura, having long since dispelled her barrier, cautiously stepped up beside him.
"Okay, nowthatsmells incredible," she said, craning her neck to peek inside the pot. "Need any help?"
Soren gave a brief nod, his eyes still fixed on the sizzle inside the pot. "Hold on a second." He glanced toward the far side of the kitchen. "Ryan, could you prepare another jar of Dawnwater?"
"Ah, yes!" Ryan called back, snapping out of his spell and hurrying over to fetch the water.
Soren turned toward Zura, giving the sizzle inside the pot a careful glance. "Could you strain the water from the rice pot over there? It should be just about ready."
"On it!" Zura nodded eagerly and turned on her heel to tend to the boiling Aureole Rice.

With his hands free, Soren reached into his spice pouch and selected a pinch of crushed Sunspice and ground Groundnut Bark. He dusted them lightly over the searing top layer before sliding the skimmer underneath each slab, turning the meat over so the seasoned side locked into the direct heat of the pot’s bottom.

A few minutes passed as the rich fragrance deepened into a savory, roasted aroma. Once the meat was fully cooked, Soren signaled Zura, took the Aureole Rice from her, and spread it evenly over the sizzled base without packing it down.

Ryan stepped forward right on cue, handing over the fresh pitcher. Soren took it with a word of thanks and slowly poured the Dawnwater along the rim until the liquid rose to meet the exact level of the rice line.

Leaving the pot to simmer on low heat, he moved back to the main prep counter and reached into his inventory for the next ingredient: a round, glowing head of Inferno Cabbage. He laid it flat on the counter. Taking his paring knife, he carefully sliced around the core, loosening the leaves one by one without tearing their crimson veins. Each leaf held a faint, naturally warm sheen that flexed smoothly beneath his fingers.

Once he had a clean stack ready, he brought them over to the pot. Reaching for the Crimson Salt again, he seasoned the rice and water mixture before lightly dusting the broad leaves on both sides to soften their outer toughness.
Working quickly before the steam could escape, Soren arranged the leaves across the surface, meticulously overlapping each one to form a seamless thermal dome directly over the layer of rice.
With the pot sealed beneath the cabbage leaves, he grabbed the lid and fitted it tightly to lock in the steam. He then wiped his hands on his apron, turned to face the group, and let out a breath.
"That’s the prep done," he said. "Now we just wait."
"Huh? It’s already over?" Zura blinked, looking almost disappointed. "I thought there’d be more fire and excitement."

"The main part is done," Soren said while wondering why she was so disappointed. "We’ll have to wait about half an hour or so for it to cook properly. But in the meantime, we can prepare some salad to eat together."
"Oh!" Zura’s eyes lit up. "I can help with that!"
"I can do it myself." Soren shook his head and paused before adding, "If you’d like to help, you and Ryan can set the table."
"Then... Ethea and I will prepare the table," Zura said, already moving toward the cupboard. "You two stay here and call us when the time comes."
"Alright, we’ll call you when it’s ready."

"What do you mean I can’t?" Soren gave her a wry smile.
"Honestly, with my senses, I’m probably smelling it ten times worse than you are.
But I’m the chef, so I don’t have much of a choice."
"Ah, right, forget I asked," Zura muttered, shaking her head.
"I keep forgetting you’re built different from the rest of us.
So... we’ll leave all of that to you!"
She quickly distanced herself again, retreating to the far side of the kitchen and even putting up a small barrier around herself.
Ryan chuckled softly from around the corner, having already positioned himself as far away as possible.
Ethea giggled at their antics and hugged the plushie tightly, saying, ’Fighting, dear!’
Soren’s lips twitched.
They had already left the barrier surrounding the working space, so there was no need to go that far away, right?
"...Let’s just finish this as soon as possible.
With a sigh, he adjusted his grip on the knife, focused his attention on the dark streaks running through the meat, and got straight to work.
’...Endure it, Soren.’
’This is nothing...’
’...Think about your sister...’
The suffocating odor clung relentlessly to the back of his throat, making his nose twitch nonstop, yet his fingers remained dead steady as the blade traced the dark veins.
Five grueling minutes passed before the final streak lifted free, prompting him to instantly freeze the discarded impurities into solid ice and stow them away with a flick of his wrist.
’Malakor, can you get rid of these and the smell, please?’
’Leave it to me, Master.’
’Thank you.’
Soren smiled faintly as Malakor whisked the frozen waste away, dissolving the trapped reek until the surrounding air became clean and odorless.

Reaching into his storage, he then pulled out a small diffuser jar filled with crushed Star-Anise Blossom, uncorked it over the counter, and released a sweet aroma that swept away the stale emptiness and lifted his spirits.
With the air restored, he gently washed the good parts of the meat and then sliced it into a few smaller parts.
He then stepped out of the barrier, picked up the bowl of prepped Ashgold Onions, and slid them straight into the shimmering Flamehorn Oil.
Whoosh-!
Hisss-!
The oil reacted instantly, flaring up in a burst of orange flame.
Soren then picked up the skimmer and stirred the onions, moving them around so they cooked evenly.
He waited until they turned crimson, and without breaking his rhythm, he fetched the prepped Ember Carrots and Scarlet Sunfruits and slid them directly on top of the onions.
He kept stirring, mixing them with the onions, and watched as the sunfruit’s red flesh deepened to a darker crimson and the carrots softened at the edges.
Once they reached the exact texture he wanted, he laid the clean slices of Fire Dragon meat right over the sizzling base.
The crimson flesh seared against the intense heat, releasing a rich and strangely mouthwatering aroma.
’Good, but let’s do our best not to repeat yesterday’s mistake...’
He recalled how he half-burned the fire dragon meat during yesterday’s practice and heightened his senses to control the mana and essence.
After a minute, he smiled in satisfaction, then picked up a pinch of crushed Crimson Salt and dusted it evenly over the surface to lock in the juices and bring out the meat’s savory depth.
Drawn back to the station by the intoxicating scent, Zura, having long since dispelled her barrier, cautiously stepped up beside him.
"Okay, nowthatsmells incredible," she said, craning her neck to peek inside the pot.
"Need any help?"
Soren gave a brief nod, his eyes still fixed on the sizzle inside the pot.
"Hold on a second." He glanced toward the far side of the kitchen.
"Ryan, could you prepare another jar of Dawnwater?"
"Ah, yes!" Ryan called back, snapping out of his spell and hurrying over to fetch the water.
Soren turned toward Zura, giving the sizzle inside the pot a careful glance.
"Could you strain the water from the rice pot over there?
It should be just about ready."
"On it!" Zura nodded eagerly and turned on her heel to tend to the boiling Aureole Rice.
With his hands free, Soren reached into his spice pouch and selected a pinch of crushed Sunspice and ground Groundnut Bark.
He dusted them lightly over the searing top layer before sliding the skimmer underneath each slab, turning the meat over so the seasoned side locked into the direct heat of the pot’s bottom.
A few minutes passed as the rich fragrance deepened into a savory, roasted aroma.
Once the meat was fully cooked, Soren signaled Zura, took the Aureole Rice from her, and spread it evenly over the sizzled base without packing it down.
Ryan stepped forward right on cue, handing over the fresh pitcher.
Soren took it with a word of thanks and slowly poured the Dawnwater along the rim until the liquid rose to meet the exact level of the rice line.
Leaving the pot to simmer on low heat, he moved back to the main prep counter and reached into his inventory for the next ingredient: a round, glowing head of Inferno Cabbage.
He laid it flat on the counter.
Taking his paring knife, he carefully sliced around the core, loosening the leaves one by one without tearing their crimson veins.
Each leaf held a faint, naturally warm sheen that flexed smoothly beneath his fingers.
Once he had a clean stack ready, he brought them over to the pot.
Reaching for the Crimson Salt again, he seasoned the rice and water mixture before lightly dusting the broad leaves on both sides to soften their outer toughness.
Working quickly before the steam could escape, Soren arranged the leaves across the surface, meticulously overlapping each one to form a seamless thermal dome directly over the layer of rice.
With the pot sealed beneath the cabbage leaves, he grabbed the lid and fitted it tightly to lock in the steam.
He then wiped his hands on his apron, turned to face the group, and let out a breath.
"That’s the prep done," he said.
"Now we just wait."
"Huh?
It’s already over?" Zura blinked, looking almost disappointed.
"I thought there’d be more fire and excitement."
"The main part is done," Soren said while wondering why she was so disappointed.
"We’ll have to wait about half an hour or so for it to cook properly.
But in the meantime, we can prepare some salad to eat together."
"Oh!" Zura’s eyes lit up.
"I can help with that!"
"I can do it myself." Soren shook his head and paused before adding, "If you’d like to help, you and Ryan can set the table."
"Then...
Ethea and I will prepare the table," Zura said, already moving toward the cupboard.
"You two stay here and call us when the time comes."
"Alright, we’ll call you when it’s ready."

chapters.title: Chapter 384: Eating Together
paragraphs: “What are you doing, Brother Soren?” Ryan asked as he saw Soren preparing another pot and taking out a new set of ingredients. “Are these for a salad? Isn’t it too much?”

“Ah,” Soren replied, setting down a smaller copper pot and selecting a batch of mild roots. “This is for Ethea. She can’t eat the dish we are preparing. Since her main affinity is ice and her body is already weak, the volatile fire mana in that pot would only conflict with her condition and worsen it.”
“I see,” Ryan said, nodding in understanding as he looked between the two pots. “Then let me know if you need any help with this one.”
Soren gave a brief nod. “Good. Then you’ll be my new assistant this time.”
“Hehe, understood, Master Chef!”
With assistant Ryan helping Chef Soren, the time passed quickly.

Thirty minutes later, it was time to check on the first dish. While Ryan went out to call Ethea and Zura, Soren approached the big pot and lifted the lid. A thick cloud of savory steam billowed out, carrying the intense aroma of seared dragon meat, sweet sunfruit, and toasted spices across the entire kitchen.
“Whoa! What is this smell?!” Zura exclaimed as she entered the kitchen. “It’s so... so different than I imagined! Anyway, is it finally ready?”
‘What did you even imagine?’ Soren wanted to ask but decided it would be better not to. “Yes, now, all that’s left is the final step.”
“Oh, do you need help again?” Zura asked enthusiastically.
“Yes, while I do my part, can you make sure no mana leaks from the pot until I say you can stop?”
“Understood, leave it to me.”

“Alright. I’m starting then.” Soren reached into the pot with his skimmer and started tossing and fluffing the glistening rice from the bottom up while folding the caramelized onions, tender carrots, and rich meat into a steaming mountain. He only stopped once every grain was evenly coated in the spiced oil and the ingredients were thoroughly mixed.
“You can stop now.”
“Oh, ok.”
“Ryan, can you bring me the platter?”
“On it!”

Ryan hurried over with two platters, one large and one small. Soren took the smaller one first, carefully lifted the meat pieces from the pot and setting them aside to rest. He then scooped the rice mixture onto the large platter, forming a mound in the center.

Once the rice was plated, he picked up a knife and cut the meat into bite-sized cubes. Each piece was still steaming, with dark seared edges and a tender center. He arranged them on top of the rice, scattering them across the surface so every serving would get a piece.
Then he stepped back to take a broader look.

And honestly, the dish looked every bit as good as he’d imagined. Steam rose from the platter, highlighting the Aureole Rice’s deep golden hue, the meat’s seared edges, and the carrots’ bright orange streaks.
“It looks... incredible,” Zura murmured, leaning in to admire the sight.
Ryan set the remaining utensils down and nodded in agreement. “The colors turned out amazing.”
“You did well, dear,” Ethea added with an affectionate smile, her eyes warm as she took in the vibrant spread.
“Thanks, but this is the result of everyone’s hard work,” Soren said, wiping his hands on a clean towel. “Let’s not hurry to judge just yet. We still have to taste it and test its effects after all.”
“Ah, right,” Zura muttered, snapping out of her trance. She picked up the salad platters and turned to the door. “Come on, Ethea, let’s head out to the table.”
Ryan stepped up to the counter and carefully lifted the heavy main dish. As he walked past, he leaned toward Soren and whispered, “You should bring Sister-in-Law’s food yourself.”

Soren gave him a brief nod and turned back to the secondary burner. He uncovered the smaller pot, picked up a ladle, and carefully poured the broth into a bowl. He then closed the lid and headed into the living room.
“Hurry up, Head Chef! Everything is going to get cold at this rate!” Zura called out from the table, practically bouncing in her seat as she tapped her spoon against her plate.
“Zura. Don’t rush my husband.” Ethea nagged her from the side.
“Urgh!” Zura dramatically clutched her heart. “You traitor!”
Soren set the bowl of broth in front of Ethea, then sat in his own chair. He chuckled and shook his head. “Alright, let’s dig in.”

Taking his spoon, Soren served himself a portion of the golden rice, topped with a piece of seared dragon meat. He took a bite and chewed slowly. It tasted rich, savory, and well-spiced, with a pleasant warmth that settled gently in his stomach. It was good, but without a fire affinity, he couldn’t feel the true depth of its magical properties.
He leaned back, shifting his eyes to Ryan and Zura to gauge their reactions.

“...Gulp.” Zura had already shoved a heavy spoonful of rice into her mouth. As soon as she swallowed, her eyes widened in shock. A sudden flush swept over her cheeks, and a flickering red ember sparked at the tip of her fingers.

“Whoa,” Ryan breathed out moments later, dropping his spoon on the table. His breath came out unusually warm, almost visible in the air. And then, he suddenly closed his eyes, his posture straightening as his breath settled into a rhythmic pace.
Is he cultivating? Soren raised a brow at the sudden change in Ryan’s demeanor.

“The fire mana inside is pure,” Zura said as she immediately scooped up another spoonful. “The meat is easy to chew and so tasty!” She threw him a thumbs up with her free hand. “As expected of the Golden Ladle Championship winner!”
“You flatter me too much.” Soren smiled, then helped Ethea eat her meal. “And I hope you can be more honest and critical of the food. About its effects and whether they work, as I told you before.”

“Oh, right. But I meant what I said.” Zura insisted before devouring another spoonful of the meal. “Besides, I have to eat more and wait for some time to actually be able to tell its effects. So, it’s better to enjoy the food while it’s hot.”
Soren nodded, accepting her reasoning. “Fair enough.”
He turned back to Ethea and offered her a spoonful of the broth.
A moment later, Ryan slowly opened his eyes, exhaling a faint trail of heat as he settled back into his chair and picked up his spoon again.
“By the way, how are you feeling about tomorrow’s exam, Ryan?” Soren asked, watching him take another bite.
“I feel like I can easily pass it if I can absorb the effects of this food properly,” Ryan replied, a confident smile touching his lips. “My mana feels far more stable than it did this morning.”

Zura leaned across the table, her eyes lighting up as she saw her chance. “Speaking of which, what kind of questions did you get on the written portion today? I took the third-year exam last year, so I might actually know the answers. Just tell me the ones you weren’t sure of or gambled on.”

Ryan paused with his spoon halfway to his mouth, thinking it over before listing a few complex problems from the test. Zura chimed in between bites, debating the trickier concepts while Ethea and Soren occasionally joined the discussion to offer their own opinions.
The dinner passed smoothly, filled with laughter, shared stories, lively debates over the exam’s trickiest questions, and small talk.

After finishing the main dish, Soren brought out light snacks, and they stayed at the table talking and eating together. Eventually, Ryan checked the time and stood up, saying his parents would worry and it would be better if he rested more before the exam.

“Alright, I should get going too,” Zura said, standing up from her seat. She turned to Soren and Ethea with a bright grin. “But you have to promise we’ll all eat together again soon and spend the rest of the night having fun!”
“We will,” Soren smiled. “...I promise to spend a whole day having fun together someday soon.”
“Good! You promised!” Zura’s grin widened. “Let’s go, boy. I will drop you off at your house myself.”
Ryan gave a quick nod, thanking Soren and Ethea once more for the meal before following her out into the hallway.
Soren stood by the doorway with Ethea at his side, watching the pair walk down the corridor until their figures disappeared as they entered the lift.
“...They’re gone.”
“...Right, let’s go back inside.”
Soren smiled, wheeled her back, and locked the door.
“Let me clean up first, ok?” He told Ethea. “You can watch TV in the meantime.”

Soren smiled and turned on the TV, putting on a show she used to watch. He then cleared the table, quickly washed the dishes, wiped down the counters, and put everything back in its place. Once the kitchen was tidy, he opened the microwave and pulled out a plate he had prepared earlier. It held a thick cut of dragon meat, seasoned with spices and herbs.
‘...Malakor.’

chapters.title: Chapter 385: Training Together
paragraphs: Darkness coiled around Soren, pooling on the kitchen floor before rising into the shadowy form of a panther. Soren knelt and set the plate of herb-crusted dragon meat on the ground in front of him. ‘Here, this is for you.’
The panther shifted his violet eyes toward Soren, then down to the steaming meat. ‘Thank you, Master.’ Malakar replied softly before opening his jaws and swallowing half the portion in a single bite.

Soren smiled and reached for a new large platter, and served the remaining main dish on it. Setting it down right next to the plate, he said, ‘Eat this too and tell me what you think. After all, you’re at the emperor level, so your insights are much better.’
Malakar nodded in agreement and stepped closer to the platter.
“Take your time,” Soren added, then headed back into the living room, where Ethea sat watching TV.
“Are you ready, dear?”
“Mm, are you finished already?”

“Yes,” Soren chuckled, then bent down, slipping one arm behind her back and the other beneath her knees to lift her effortlessly into his arms. She rested her head on his shoulder as he carried her straight into the bedroom.

Half an hour later, after helping her change into her sleeping clothes, Soren carefully laid Ethea on the bed and pulled the blanket up over her shoulders. He leaned over and brushed a strand of hair from her face.
“I’ll be back soon.”

He went to the kitchen and washed the platters Malakor had left in the sink after eating. He then quickly prepared a moonleaf tea for Ethea and returned to the bedroom. He sat on the edge of the bed and helped her sit up, holding the cup steady while she drank. When she finished, he helped her lie back down, set the cup aside, and climbed in beside her, wrapping his arms around her and pulling her close.
“Goodnight, my love.” He pressed a gentle kiss to her lips.
“...Goodnight, my love.” She whispered as they parted their lips.
They closed their eyes.
A moment later, they appeared in their shared mental realm. The grassy field stretched out around them, and Ethea was still nestled in his embrace as they lay on the ground.
“...Should we start the training?”
“Okay.” She closed her eyes briefly, and the surroundings shifted. The grassy field melted away, replaced by a large training ground with wooden dummies, weapon racks, and a wide-open floor.
They stood up. Ethea picked up a wooden sword from the rack and tossed it to him.
“Dear,” she called, her face solemn. “Do you really want to learn and practice swordsmanship instead of your new spear technique? You’re not doing it because I told you about it, right?”

“I’m already practicing the spear in reality,” Soren replied as he familiarized himself with the sword by swinging and switching it between his hands. “And even if I lack a natural talent for swordsmanship, I still want to try. And maybe with a teacher as skilled and beautiful as you, I’ll actually be able to pull it off.”
“Flattery won’t make the training any lighter, dear. And...” Ethea smiled at his words. “I will be teaching you strictly from the absolute basics. Are you prepared for that too?”
“I’m ready.” Soren nodded solemnly. “In fact, it’s better if you don’t show mercy and work me to the bone. I need to build proper muscle memory from scratch.”
“...Alright.” Ethea nodded and walked toward him. “Then let’s start with the foundation of everything: your stance and weight distribution.”

She circled him slowly, her eyes tracking every line of his posture. “...You’re standing like a spearman, dear. Your center of gravity is pulled back, preparing for range and forward momentum. A sword demands balance from the center: receptive, yet ready to drive forward at a moment’s notice.”
Soren adjusted his feet, widening his stance slightly, but Ethea shook her head.
“Lower,” she said, stepping in and pressing her fingers against the side of his hip to shift his alignment. “...Drop your weight into your thighs, not your knees.”
Soren did as he was told, and then her hands moved up to his shoulders, pressing down until his upper body relaxed. “Unclench your neck too. Your upper body should be fluid, dear.”

Ethea then moved directly behind him, closing the remaining space until her front brushed against his back. Her arms wrapped around his waist, her hands tracing the sides of his ribs before sliding down to cup his hands over the sword’s hilt.
Her breath warmed the side of his neck as she aligned her elbows with his.

“Feel the difference?” she whispered, her chin resting lightly near his shoulder as her fingers tightened over his knuckles, adjusting his grip until the blade aligned perfectly with his wrist. “Your index finger relaxes. The power doesn’t come from a white-knuckled squeeze; it flows from the pinky and ring fingers, rooted straight down through your spine into your heels.”

‘...’ Soren gulped dryly as he did his best not to get distracted by her proximity. Although he was used to holding her close and caring for her every day, this kind of almost deliberate, body-to-body contact under the guise of “strict martial instruction” was a completely different test of endurance.

His eyes darted slightly to the side, catching the faint curve of her jaw just inches from his own. Every slight shift of her body against his back sent a sharp pulse through his mind, rendering the sword in his hands almost entirely forgotten.
“Are you listening, dear?” Ethea murmured right against his ear, and though her voice carried that same innocent lightness, the tiny tug at the corner of her lips betrayed her amusement.

“I-I am listening,” Soren said quickly, oblivious to her playful intent as he cleared his throat and stared rigidly straight ahead, simply assuming her close proximity was part of the rigorous training process. “Pinky and ring fingers. Spine. Heels.”

“Then why did you just tense up?” she asked softly, her hands smoothing over his chest down to his waist, pretending to adjust his posture while clearly enjoying his reaction. “Focus. Or do I need to hold you like this until you learn to keep your head cool?”
“N-No,” Soren muttered, locking his gaze onto a distant pillar and forcing his pulse to settle. “I’m focused.”
“Good, now hold this stance. We will move on to basic vertical cuts once you can keep your balance for thirty minutes without breaking form.”
“Thirty minutes?”
“Hmm? You can’t do it?”
“No, I can do it,” Soren replied seriously. “...You can cultivate in the meantime if you want.”
“No, dear.” Ethea shook her head, finally distancing herself from him. “I will be watching you so you don’t slack off or slip back into your spear habits the moment my eyes leave you.”
“Come on, dear,” Soren said, keeping his arms steady and his eyes still fixed on the distant pillar. “You can trust me to take this seriously.”
“I do trust you,” Ethea replied smoothly, then sat on the floor not far from him. “There is actually another reason I am staying... I want to talk about your past again.”
Soren blinked, maintaining his stance despite the sudden shift in topic. “My past?”

“Yes,” Ethea said, resting her chin on her hand as she watched his form. “...Dear, why didn’t you learn to fight or train with a weapon back then? And... why didn’t you ask me to teach you swordsmanship sooner instead of choosing a spear?”
“You don’t have to answer if it brings up bitter memories, dear.”
Soren kept his posture intact, his arms steady and the wooden blade level, though his eyes shifted toward her. A faint smile touched his lips, devoid of any genuine bitterness.

“I think you’ve already guessed most of it, dear. And the truth really isn’t that dramatic or interesting,” Soren said, his voice measured as he maintained his breathing. “I never trained with a weapon back then because my family never intended for me to actually learn. Whenever they arranged ‘lessons’ for me, it was just an excuse to use me as a punching bag. Between the knights, the instructors, and my own family, I heard the exact same thing every day. They kept telling me I was weak, devoid of talent, and completely useless with a sword...”

He shrugged slightly without letting his shoulders rise, keeping his core locked. “But I knew they only said those things to break my spirit, so I just ignored their words as usual and stopped ‘learning’ altogether after some time. There was no point in giving them the satisfaction of watching me fail.”
“...” Ethea remained in her place, barely stopping herself from jumping and taking him to her embrace.

“...As for choosing the spear when I came here,” Soren continued with a thoughtful expression, “it was simply the most practical option. You should also know that it’s widely considered easier for beginners to grasp. It also offers good reach from a distance. And... you could barely speak back then, and our relationship wasn’t exactly close enough for me to ask you to teach me swordsmanship. And...”

sentences.text: Darkness coiled around Soren, pooling on the kitchen floor before rising into the shadowy form of a panther.
Soren knelt and set the plate of herb-crusted dragon meat on the ground in front of him.
‘Here, this is for you.’
The panther shifted his violet eyes toward Soren, then down to the steaming meat.
‘Thank you, Master.’ Malakar replied softly before opening his jaws and swallowing half the portion in a single bite.
Soren smiled and reached for a new large platter, and served the remaining main dish on it.
Setting it down right next to the plate, he said, ‘Eat this too and tell me what you think.
After all, you’re at the emperor level, so your insights are much better.’
Malakar nodded in agreement and stepped closer to the platter.
“Take your time,” Soren added, then headed back into the living room, where Ethea sat watching TV.
“Are you ready, dear?”
“Mm, are you finished already?”
“Yes,” Soren chuckled, then bent down, slipping one arm behind her back and the other beneath her knees to lift her effortlessly into his arms.
She rested her head on his shoulder as he carried her straight into the bedroom.
Half an hour later, after helping her change into her sleeping clothes, Soren carefully laid Ethea on the bed and pulled the blanket up over her shoulders.
He leaned over and brushed a strand of hair from her face.
“I’ll be back soon.”
He went to the kitchen and washed the platters Malakor had left in the sink after eating.
He then quickly prepared a moonleaf tea for Ethea and returned to the bedroom.
He sat on the edge of the bed and helped her sit up, holding the cup steady while she drank.
When she finished, he helped her lie back down, set the cup aside, and climbed in beside her, wrapping his arms around her and pulling her close.
“Goodnight, my love.” He pressed a gentle kiss to her lips.
“...Goodnight, my love.” She whispered as they parted their lips.
They closed their eyes.
A moment later, they appeared in their shared mental realm.
The grassy field stretched out around them, and Ethea was still nestled in his embrace as they lay on the ground.
“...Should we start the training?”
“Okay.” She closed her eyes briefly, and the surroundings shifted.
The grassy field melted away, replaced by a large training ground with wooden dummies, weapon racks, and a wide-open floor.
They stood up.
Ethea picked up a wooden sword from the rack and tossed it to him.
“Dear,” she called, her face solemn.
“Do you really want to learn and practice swordsmanship instead of your new spear technique?
You’re not doing it because I told you about it, right?”
“I’m already practicing the spear in reality,” Soren replied as he familiarized himself with the sword by swinging and switching it between his hands.
“And even if I lack a natural talent for swordsmanship, I still want to try.
And maybe with a teacher as skilled and beautiful as you, I’ll actually be able to pull it off.”
“Flattery won’t make the training any lighter, dear.
And...” Ethea smiled at his words.
“I will be teaching you strictly from the absolute basics.
Are you prepared for that too?”
“I’m ready.” Soren nodded solemnly.
“In fact, it’s better if you don’t show mercy and work me to the bone.
I need to build proper muscle memory from scratch.”
“...Alright.” Ethea nodded and walked toward him.
“Then let’s start with the foundation of everything: your stance and weight distribution.”
She circled him slowly, her eyes tracking every line of his posture.
“...You’re standing like a spearman, dear.
Your center of gravity is pulled back, preparing for range and forward momentum.
A sword demands balance from the center: receptive, yet ready to drive forward at a moment’s notice.”
Soren adjusted his feet, widening his stance slightly, but Ethea shook her head.
“Lower,” she said, stepping in and pressing her fingers against the side of his hip to shift his alignment.
“...Drop your weight into your thighs, not your knees.”
Soren did as he was told, and then her hands moved up to his shoulders, pressing down until his upper body relaxed.
“Unclench your neck too.
Your upper body should be fluid, dear.”
Ethea then moved directly behind him, closing the remaining space until her front brushed against his back.
Her arms wrapped around his waist, her hands tracing the sides of his ribs before sliding down to cup his hands over the sword’s hilt.
Her breath warmed the side of his neck as she aligned her elbows with his.
“Feel the difference?” she whispered, her chin resting lightly near his shoulder as her fingers tightened over his knuckles, adjusting his grip until the blade aligned perfectly with his wrist.
“Your index finger relaxes.
The power doesn’t come from a white-knuckled squeeze; it flows from the pinky and ring fingers, rooted straight down through your spine into your heels.”
‘...’ Soren gulped dryly as he did his best not to get distracted by her proximity.

Although he was used to holding her close and caring for her every day, this kind of almost deliberate, body-to-body contact under the guise of “strict martial instruction” was a completely different test of endurance.
His eyes darted slightly to the side, catching the faint curve of her jaw just inches from his own.
Every slight shift of her body against his back sent a sharp pulse through his mind, rendering the sword in his hands almost entirely forgotten.
“Are you listening, dear?” Ethea murmured right against his ear, and though her voice carried that same innocent lightness, the tiny tug at the corner of her lips betrayed her amusement.

“I-I am listening,” Soren said quickly, oblivious to her playful intent as he cleared his throat and stared rigidly straight ahead, simply assuming her close proximity was part of the rigorous training process.
“Pinky and ring fingers.
Spine.
Heels.”
“Then why did you just tense up?” she asked softly, her hands smoothing over his chest down to his waist, pretending to adjust his posture while clearly enjoying his reaction.
“Focus.
Or do I need to hold you like this until you learn to keep your head cool?”
“N-No,” Soren muttered, locking his gaze onto a distant pillar and forcing his pulse to settle.
“I’m focused.”
“Good, now hold this stance.
We will move on to basic vertical cuts once you can keep your balance for thirty minutes without breaking form.”
“Thirty minutes?”
“Hmm?
You can’t do it?”
“No, I can do it,” Soren replied seriously.
“...You can cultivate in the meantime if you want.”
“No, dear.” Ethea shook her head, finally distancing herself from him.
“I will be watching you so you don’t slack off or slip back into your spear habits the moment my eyes leave you.”
“Come on, dear,” Soren said, keeping his arms steady and his eyes still fixed on the distant pillar.
“You can trust me to take this seriously.”
“I do trust you,” Ethea replied smoothly, then sat on the floor not far from him.
“There is actually another reason I am staying...
I want to talk about your past again.”
Soren blinked, maintaining his stance despite the sudden shift in topic.
“My past?”
“Yes,” Ethea said, resting her chin on her hand as she watched his form.
“...Dear, why didn’t you learn to fight or train with a weapon back then?
And... why didn’t you ask me to teach you swordsmanship sooner instead of choosing a spear?”
“You don’t have to answer if it brings up bitter memories, dear.”
Soren kept his posture intact, his arms steady and the wooden blade level, though his eyes shifted toward her.
A faint smile touched his lips, devoid of any genuine bitterness.
“I think you’ve already guessed most of it, dear.
And the truth really isn’t that dramatic or interesting,” Soren said, his voice measured as he maintained his breathing.
“I never trained with a weapon back then because my family never intended for me to actually learn.
Whenever they arranged ‘lessons’ for me, it was just an excuse to use me as a punching bag.
Between the knights, the instructors, and my own family, I heard the exact same thing every day.
They kept telling me I was weak, devoid of talent, and completely useless with a sword...”
He shrugged slightly without letting his shoulders rise, keeping his core locked.
“But I knew they only said those things to break my spirit, so I just ignored their words as usual and stopped ‘learning’ altogether after some time.
There was no point in giving them the satisfaction of watching me fail.”
“...” Ethea remained in her place, barely stopping herself from jumping and taking him to her embrace.
“...As for choosing the spear when I came here,” Soren continued with a thoughtful expression, “it was simply the most practical option.
You should also know that it’s widely considered easier for beginners to grasp.
It also offers good reach from a distance.
And... you could barely speak back then, and our relationship wasn’t exactly close enough for me to ask you to teach me swordsmanship.
And...”

chapters.title: Chapter 386: Training Together [2]
paragraphs: "And when I asked you to guide me during spear training, I saw how much strain it put you under, so I didn’t want to burden you with swordsmanship on top of everything else." He took a deep breath and smiled. "Besides, I actually ended up enjoying the spear once I started practicing it. It suited my needs at the time and helped me build confidence when I needed it most... That’s really all there is to it."
"...I see," Ethea whispered. "Thank you for telling me all of this, dear."

"Haha, there’s no need to thank me. We’re loving husband and wife, aren’t we? It’s only natural for us to talk about these things." Soren grinned, keeping his eyes locked straight ahead while trying his best not to let his arms shake. "Besides, if I can’t be honest with you, then who else can I turn to?"
"Right..." Ethea’s features softened into a tender smile as she looked at him. "It’s natural... we are a loving couple after all..."

Then her soft expression faded. Her lips curled into a mischievous arch, and her eyes gleamed with intent. "By the way, dear, you broke your posture just now. That’s why the countdown starts from the beginning."
She leaped into the air and helped him ’correct’ his posture, as before.
’...’ Soren noticed she changed almost nothing but said nothing other than, "Understood."
They spent the next fifteen minutes in silence, with Ethea staring at Soren without missing a second.
"...You’re doing remarkably well, dear," she finally broke the silence, standing up and walking back toward him slowly and deliberately. "Your posture hasn’t wavered once since you reset."
She stopped just a step away.

"Now we move to the real test," she continued, beginning to circle him. "Holding your form like this must be easy now. However, keeping it under pressure or distraction is what keeps you alive in battle. That’s why, for the rest of the time, I’m going to actively test your focus. If you break your stance, drop your arm, or let your mind wander, even for a second, another half hour will be added to your time."
"...Go ahead," Soren replied while steeling his resolve.

"..." Ethea merely smiled before suddenly snapping her hand forward. A sharp rush of wind whistled in his ears as a wooden blade materialized in her grip, stopping barely a hair’s breadth from his throat. Soren didn’t move, let alone flinch. His eyes remained focused on the task.

Ethea didn’t give up with that surprise feint attack either. She continued to test him, sometimes with another surprise attack, while other times with subtle mental attacks. She even told him he could relax since he passed the test, but Soren, counting the time in his head, didn’t let his guard down.
Eventually, the full thirty minutes passed and the test ended.
"...Good job, dear. You did well."
"Thank you for not going easy," Soren replied while stretching his somewhat stiff body.
"..." Ethea smiled, not mentioning that she could have used the previous method to make it harder but chose not to. "...Now let’s move on to the next step."
"Yes."
"First, let me tell you the basics of swordsmanship..."

Ethea started explaining, and Soren listened, taking in every detail. She broke down the core mechanics, showing him how to hold the blade in different scenarios and positions, move his feet, perform basic moves, and so on.

But understanding the theory was only the first step. To lock each movement into muscle memory, she had him repeat every stance, footwork pattern, and swing for at least half an hour, or a hundred times, under her watchful eye, correcting his form whenever his technique drifted even slightly.
By the time they finished going through the entire sequence, it was already time for Ethea to sleep. So, he told her to rest and promised he would get some sleep himself soon.

But the moment she left the mental realm, he picked up the sword again and resumed his drills. He repeated every movement she had taught him until his body moved without thinking, until the sword felt less like a foreign object and more like an extension of his arm.

He only stopped when the first rays of morning light began to filter through the curtains in the real world. However, he was certain he had learned more in this one session than in years of ’learning’ during his childhood. He resolved to work harder and train this way every day, then left the mental realm to wash up and make breakfast.
’Malakor.’ Soren called out mentally as he began cooking. ’Can you give your feedback now?’

’Of course, Master.’ Malakor’s voice echoed in his mind. ’The rice meal and the roasted meat were both delicious. Honestly, they’re one of the most flavorful things I’ve ever eaten. The effects were amazing too. Despite being at the Emperor level, I could feel the fire mana settling into my core and affecting my pathways.’
Soren nodded, waiting for the rest.

’However,’ Malakor continued, ’they didn’t exactly match the effects you were aiming for. According to my calculations, the meal would indeed help strengthen and heal the pathways and the core, but it contains too much pure fire mana. That makes it volatile if consumed in large quantities. And the core-healing effect is probably lower than what you intended as well.’
Soren paused, considering this. ’Thank you for your help. That’s exactly what I needed to hear.’
He set the knife down and thought it through.

’If the fire mana is too concentrated, I’ll need to adjust the preparation to tone down the volatile heat while preserving the restorative traits.’ He wiped his hands on a towel and decided to hear Ryan and Nura’s opinions first before attempting again.
Later morning, Etenia Academy.
Three figures waved at the blue-haired boy as he walked toward the building. He turned once, waved back with a confident smile, then disappeared through the doors.
The three of them stared at the building for a moment. Then the woman holding the wheelchair turned to the man beside her.
"Then, we’ll get going too. Call us when he comes out, Sir Ren."

The man called Ren, who was Soren in disguise, gave a nod and watched the two of them until they disappeared around the bend of the walkway. He then turned, strolled to a nearby bench nestled in the shade of a large tree, and sat down.

’...Let’s see. Lady Zura said similar things as Malakor, but Ryan’s thoughts were a bit different from theirs.’ He paused as he recalled Ryan’s words about how beneficial it had been for him. He said it not only strengthened his pathways and core, but also improved the quality of his existing mana by a small margin. Although it might have sounded small, mana quality meant a lot for an awakened. Higher quality meant stronger spells, more efficient techniques, and a higher ceiling for growth.

’...I think I forgot something important.’ He narrowed his eyes as an idea formed in his mind. ’While Malakor is an Emperor, he doesn’t have affinity with fire. In fact, his being at the Emperor level might have been the issue. And the same goes for Lady Zura. Although she has high fire affinity, she’s already at the sixth circle, and her core and pathways are already strengthened, perhaps to the point where the meal’s effects felt weaker than they actually were.’
He was preparing the meal for Nura, who had high fire affinity, a weaker constitution, and a damaged core and pathways, so the recipe might actually be closer to the target than he had thought.

’...No, I still have to research more and make sure first. Nura’s life depends on this, so I can’t afford any mistakes.’ He leaned back against the bench, letting out a breath as he stared up at the rustling leaves above. ’...Perhaps if I could give her a small sample first to gauge her reaction, it would make balancing the recipe so much easier.’
He closed his eyes, thinking about how to pull off this not-so-simple task.
’...It seems I have to rely on Lady Zura again.’

He sighed inwardly. The best and easiest solution he could think of was to have Zura offer the sample to Nura while teaching her personally. She could also tell her it would be beneficial for her and help her absorb its effects much better.

Then again, this had been his initial plan for the actual magic meal all along. Since Zura was already guiding Nura through her training, having her introduce the dish under the guise of an instructional aid was the most natural way to deliver it without raising suspicion or causing unnecessary worry.

’...I was overthinking it again.’ Soren opened his eyes, a small smile softening his serious expression. The more he considered it, the more he liked the idea: it was safe and controlled, and it gave him the data he needed without putting Nura at too much risk. ’...I’ll discuss it with Lady Zura later.’
