chapters.title: Chapter 387: Deep Thoughts
paragraphs: Soren spent the rest of his time cultivating while waiting for Ryan to come out. Hours passed by, the high sun signaling that lunchtime had already arrived.
He opened his eyes and stretched, contemplating whether to call Zura and Ethea so they could grab lunch together, or just tell them to eat something while he waited for Ryan to finish.
Before he could decide, Malakar’s deep voice resonated in his head. ’...Master, she has left the academy grounds again.’
Soren narrowed his eyes. ’Good. Follow her and make sure to record everything.’
’Understood.’

’...’ Soren relaxed his expression and thought about what he had just said. Actually, the person he asked Malakor to watch and record their actions was none other than Nura’s personal maid. However, she was also the biggest obstacle in their way to reach her and the spy planted by the family by Nura’s side. That’s why he had set up this secret surveillance, using Malakar to shadow her every move.
Fortunately, the effort had already paid off with a few crucial findings.

Whenever the maid left the academy grounds alone, her first job was always to contact the family and deliver a detailed report on Nura’s status. Once her task was done, she would stop by local shops to buy meals or whatever specific items Nura had requested before heading straight back inside.
Even within the academy walls, she never truly let her guard down, consistently keeping a specific distance from Nura to observe her every action and word.

To a third party, that level of constant surveillance might have seemed downright creepy too. But in truth, it wasn’t an uncommon sight among noble families like the Valmeres. The difference was that most houses monitored their young masters and ladies to protect them, not to feed reports back to a shadow network for their own self-serving interests. And this only proved just how rotten the Valmere family truly was from the inside out.
Not that it bothered Soren. In fact, their hands were so dirty that he’d have plenty to use against them if a confrontation ever arose.
’...No, I shouldn’t wait for one.’ He squinted again. ’It’s best to strike them when they least expect it.’

Catching them off guard would not only drastically increase the chances of rescuing Nura, but also give him the perfect opportunity to exact revenge and tear down the family once and for all. Furthermore, knowing that innocent people were likely suffering under the Valmeres’ cruel, self-serving rule didn’t sit well with him. That’s why taking the initiative to bring them down was the only logical path forward.
’...I’ll have to plan it seriously, but I should still break through first.’
Furthermore, he couldn’t be half-hearted about it. He had to ensure that the truly evil ones suffered the punishment they deserved, while any innocent lives caught in the web remained unharmed.

Still, pulling that off wouldn’t be easy. The Valmere family mainly operated in the Oros Kingdom, far from their current position. If he sent Malakar off to handle things on his own, they would be left without their strongest guard.

On top of that, he needed a clearer picture of their network and allies. He had to stay vigilant about who might be backing them, most notably his father-in-law, their strongest potential ally, or perhaps the true master behind the scenes. From a man like him, you could expect almost anything.
’...Come to think of it, we haven’t seen him or heard from him once since leaving Kalmira City.’

Soren frowned as the realization settled in. It was genuinely strange. Back in Kalmira City, Darius had turned up like clockwork whenever they faced life-threatening danger and survived. Yet after that incident during their travel, and even throughout the ordeal in Bagdad City, he hadn’t visited even once, not even secretly.

’Could he have given up entirely? Or is he plotting something else?’ Soren pondered, letting out a faint exhale through his nose. ’Or since he knows we have Malakar, he doesn’t want to risk being detected, or is he certain she will be safe now?’
Whatever the case, Soren needed to factor him into his plans too. Darius was unpredictable, and unpredictable elements were dangerous. He would have to be ready for anything.

’I should read that book to the end,’ he reminded himself. The one Nuelia had gifted him before. He hadn’t read it until now for various reasons, but the biggest was his incomplete elven language skills. He knew a few phrases, could manage basic conversation, and knew the alphabet and how to read and write a few words, but that was the extent of it. Reading and understanding it properly would require a far better grasp of grammar and vocabulary.

’...Perhaps I should look for an elven tutor here at the academy,’ Soren mused, tapping his fingers thoughtfully against his knee. ’There are plenty of elven teachers and students around. Finding someone to help shouldn’t be too difficult.’
’Hmm?’
Just then, he sensed a familiar presence approaching. He looked toward the building and saw Ryan come out, wearing a new set of clothes and a bandage on his forehead.
"Brother Ren!"
Ryan also spotted him quickly and waved with a smile.
Soren waved back, pushed himself off the bench, and stood up. As the younger boy trotted closer, Soren ’noticed’ the fresh bandage and raised an eyebrow.
"What happened? Are you alright?"

Ryan rubbed the back of his neck and let out an awkward laugh. "I’m fine, Brother Ren. Just a little accident during the practical evaluation." His sheepish grin quickly gave way to a bright smile. "But I passed it! I finally made it into the academy!"
Soren smiled and clapped him on the shoulder. "Congratulations. But it was all because of your hard work. So be proud of yourself."
Ryan rubbed the back of his neck, clearly pleased. "Still, I couldn’t have done it without you."
"A push in the right direction only works if you’re ready to run," Soren said with a meaningful smile. "And you were more than ready."
"...Right."
"Come on, let’s go now." Soren smiled. "We should tell the others the good news."

sentences.text: Soren spent the rest of his time cultivating while waiting for Ryan to come out.
Hours passed by, the high sun signaling that lunchtime had already arrived.
He opened his eyes and stretched, contemplating whether to call Zura and Ethea so they could grab lunch together, or just tell them to eat something while he waited for Ryan to finish.
Before he could decide, Malakar’s deep voice resonated in his head. ’...Master, she has left the academy grounds again.’
Soren narrowed his eyes. ’Good.
Follow her and make sure to record everything.’
’Understood.’
’...’ Soren relaxed his expression and thought about what he had just said.
Actually, the person he asked Malakor to watch and record their actions was none other than Nura’s personal maid.
However, she was also the biggest obstacle in their way to reach her and the spy planted by the family by Nura’s side.
That’s why he had set up this secret surveillance, using Malakar to shadow her every move.
Fortunately, the effort had already paid off with a few crucial findings.
Whenever the maid left the academy grounds alone, her first job was always to contact the family and deliver a detailed report on Nura’s status.
Once her task was done, she would stop by local shops to buy meals or whatever specific items Nura had requested before heading straight back inside.
Even within the academy walls, she never truly let her guard down, consistently keeping a specific distance from Nura to observe her every action and word.
To a third party, that level of constant surveillance might have seemed downright creepy too.
But in truth, it wasn’t an uncommon sight among noble families like the Valmeres.
The difference was that most houses monitored their young masters and ladies to protect them, not to feed reports back to a shadow network for their own self-serving interests.
And this only proved just how rotten the Valmere family truly was from the inside out.
Not that it bothered Soren.
In fact, their hands were so dirty that he’d have plenty to use against them if a confrontation ever arose.
’...No, I shouldn’t wait for one.’ He squinted again. ’It’s best to strike them when they least expect it.’
Catching them off guard would not only drastically increase the chances of rescuing Nura, but also give him the perfect opportunity to exact revenge and tear down the family once and for all.
Furthermore, knowing that innocent people were likely suffering under the Valmeres’ cruel, self-serving rule didn’t sit well with him.
That’s why taking the initiative to bring them down was the only logical path forward.
’...I’ll have to plan it seriously, but I should still break through first.’
Furthermore, he couldn’t be half-hearted about it.
He had to ensure that the truly evil ones suffered the punishment they deserved, while any innocent lives caught in the web remained unharmed.
Still, pulling that off wouldn’t be easy.
The Valmere family mainly operated in the Oros Kingdom, far from their current position.
If he sent Malakar off to handle things on his own, they would be left without their strongest guard.
On top of that, he needed a clearer picture of their network and allies.
He had to stay vigilant about who might be backing them, most notably his father-in-law, their strongest potential ally, or perhaps the true master behind the scenes.
From a man like him, you could expect almost anything.
’...Come to think of it, we haven’t seen him or heard from him once since leaving Kalmira City.’
Soren frowned as the realization settled in.
It was genuinely strange.
Back in Kalmira City, Darius had turned up like clockwork whenever they faced life-threatening danger and survived.
Yet after that incident during their travel, and even throughout the ordeal in Bagdad City, he hadn’t visited even once, not even secretly.
’Could he have given up entirely?

Or is he plotting something else?’ Soren pondered, letting out a faint exhale through his nose. ’Or since he knows we have Malakar, he doesn’t want to risk being detected, or is he certain she will be safe now?’
Whatever the case, Soren needed to factor him into his plans too.
Darius was unpredictable, and unpredictable elements were dangerous.
He would have to be ready for anything.
’I should read that book to the end,’ he reminded himself.
The one Nuelia had gifted him before.
He hadn’t read it until now for various reasons, but the biggest was his incomplete elven language skills.
He knew a few phrases, could manage basic conversation, and knew the alphabet and how to read and write a few words, but that was the extent of it.
Reading and understanding it properly would require a far better grasp of grammar and vocabulary.
’...Perhaps I should look for an elven tutor here at the academy,’ Soren mused, tapping his fingers thoughtfully against his knee. ’There are plenty of elven teachers and students around.
Finding someone to help shouldn’t be too difficult.’
’Hmm?’
Just then, he sensed a familiar presence approaching.
He looked toward the building and saw Ryan come out, wearing a new set of clothes and a bandage on his forehead.
"Brother Ren!"
Ryan also spotted him quickly and waved with a smile.
Soren waved back, pushed himself off the bench, and stood up.

"What happened?
Are you alright?"
Ryan rubbed the back of his neck and let out an awkward laugh.

Just a little accident during the practical evaluation." His sheepish grin quickly gave way to a bright smile.

I finally made it into the academy!"

"Congratulations.
But it was all because of your hard work.
So be proud of yourself."
Ryan rubbed the back of his neck, clearly pleased.
"Still, I couldn’t have done it without you."

"And you were more than ready."
"...Right."
"Come on, let’s go now." Soren smiled.
"We should tell the others the good news."

chapters.title: Chapter 388: Celebration
paragraphs: Ryan nodded and followed, his steps considerably lighter despite his weariness. His posture radiated satisfaction, making it clear how much passing the evaluation meant to him, though every few paces he instinctively touched the bandage wrapped around his brow.
"...Should I give you a potion?" Soren couldn’t help but ask as they walked. "Or did the academy healers already patch you up?"
"Ah, thank you, but there’s no need." Ryan hurriedly replied. "...Actually, I received a blow to this spot after the official exam ended. One of the instructors offered to spar with me."

He paused, a faint flush rising on his cheeks as he admitted the rest. "It wasn’t much of a duel, honestly. He defeated me pretty brutally before I could even land a hit on him, and that was how I ended up with this."

He touched the fabric over his temple, yet as he spoke, his voice carried an unmistakable edge of enthusiasm. Soren caught the contrast immediately. For someone who had taken a rough beating, the boy sounded remarkably eager.

Noticing Soren’s expression, Ryan grinned sheepishly and continued. "Even though it was over in less than a minute, I learned so much from just those few exchanges. In fact, I even ended up getting an enlightenment because of that final attack!"

"I see," Soren said, nodding slowly as the pieces clicked into place. This explained why Ryan’s mental state had been in a trance state for some time earlier. "That instructor must be quite skilled to be able to make you enlightened."

"Mm. I think I heard they called him the Chief Sword Instructor," Ryan said, his eyes shining with clear admiration. "He probably leads the Weaponry Department too. And... He even asked if I wanted to become his personal disciple on the spot."
Soren smiled slightly and glanced over at him. "Did you accept, then?"
Ryan shook his head without hesitation. "No, I thanked him politely first, but I rejected the offer."
"Did he... get angry?" Soren asked, raising an eyebrow.
"No, actually," Ryan chuckled, rubbing the back of his neck again. "He just laughed out loud and said I was interesting, then told me he’d be looking forward to seeing what I do in the future."
"...What a strange man," Soren muttered, though he guessed the instructor was simply pleased to find someone with genuine talent and the resolve to forge his own path.

"He really is," Ryan agreed, nodding before his tone turned deeply respectful. "But he was unbelievably strong too. Even though I had to decline his offer, I’d still love to learn whatever I can from him while I’m here.

Soren chuckled softly, looking ahead as they walked. "If I had to guess, you’ll be seeing plenty of him from now on. The academy isn’t so big that you can avoid the Chief Sword Instructor, and there will be more than enough opportunities to pick up a few things along the way."
"Right." Ryan agreed. "And I am glad I chose to transfer here."

Soren felt happy for Ryan too, and given the Vice Principal’s keen eye for talent, the academy’s upper management would undoubtedly invest heavily in Ryan’s growth, ensuring he had every resource he needed to reach his full potential.
The two kept walking and talking until they reunited with Ethea and Zura. Like Soren, they both reacted the moment they saw the bandage on Ryan’s forehead.
"What happened to you, Ryan?"
"Are you ok?"
"I am ok. But more importantly, I passed!" Ryan announced before they could worry further.
"Really? That’s amazing news!" Zura gasped, her eyes lighting up instantly as she rushed forward to slap Ryan on the shoulder. "Congratulations, Ryan!"
"Congratulations, Ryan," Ethea added with a sincere smile. "You did well."
Ryan thanked each of them in return.
"We should celebrate it." Zura turned toward Soren with a grin. "Sir Ren will be treating us, right?"
Before Soren could reply, Ryan spoke up, waving his hands modestly. "Actually... I’d like to treat everyone. My parents said they would prepare a lunch for us today, so please come over to my house."
Zura raised an eyebrow, a teasing grin spreading across her face. "Oh? Were you that confident you would pass?"
Ryan rubbed the back of his neck, a soft yet determined smile on his face. "I had no choice but to pass, so..."

Zura chuckled, crossing her arms as her grin softened into an approving look. "There’s no need to be so serious about it. Having confidence is a good thing, as long as you don’t let it turn into overconfidence.
"I will keep that in mind," Ryan replied, nodding earnestly.
"Though I certainly won’t reject a party," Zura added with a wink before turning toward Soren and Ethea. "And I doubt these two will either."
"Not at all," Soren said with a light nod. "And let’s continue the celebration at our place in the evening."
"Cool, it’s decided then!" Zura exclaimed. "Let’s go!"
The other three laughed and followed after her.
After having lunch at Ryan’s house, they all parted ways, and Zura and Ryan had agreed to gather at the hotel for dinner.
Soren and Ethea returned to their room and went through their daily routine. Once Ethea was settled and had drifted off to ’sleep,’ Soren sat on the floor, closed his eyes, and began to cultivate.
But soon after he entered a meditative state, a familiardingchimed gently in his mind, and translucent message windows materialized, floating in his vision.
He didn’t react outwardly, keeping his breath steady as he read through the incoming notifications and allowed the rewards to seamlessly integrate into his body and mind.

It was another round of investment returns, this time modest gains yielded from cooking for Malakar and Zura. In total, the Authority granted him Cooking Mastery +1 and a substantial influx of 50,000 mana.
’...Status Open.’
Soren scrolled down and stopped at the one line that caught his attention.
[Mana Capacity: 869,704 / 880,000]
’...I think there’s no need to go into Gates anymore.’

chapters.title: Chapter 389: Lonely...
paragraphs: Since there was about ten thousand mana left to reach the mana capacity limit, Soren decided to cultivate till evening and even activated the Synchronicity effect. As his cultivation speed increased dramatically, he took out more than enough mana crystals and began cultivating.
Time passed, and evening eventually came.
[Mana Capacity: 877,704 / 880,000]
’...Not bad,’ Soren thought as he stretched his muscles. ’I can easily fill the rest up at night.’
There was also an ongoing investment for Ryan, which would likely finish soon. The upcoming returns might include enough mana and spare him from cultivating the remainder himself.
’...Hah,’ Soren sighed softly, shaking his head slightly. ’I shouldn’t rely on returns for every minor step.’
He then picked up his phone from the nightstand and noticed a few calls and unread messages waiting for him. He opened the app and began reading them one by one.

The first message was from Ryan, explaining that he wouldn’t be able to make it for dinner this evening. His parents were taking him and his younger sister on a city tour to celebrate his admission, and he apologized for canceling on short notice.
Soren smiled as he typed back a reply.
’No need to apologize or worry about it,’ he sent. ’Just make sure to enjoy the time with your family. I’ll save some food for you so you can eat tomorrow...’
The next message was from Zura, telling him she might arrive half an hour or so late. He also replied to her appropriately and read the next message.
Surprisingly, it was from a recent acquaintance, Mr. Doran, the head of the Bagdad Magic Chefs Association.
’...Let’s see...’

Soren narrowed his eyes and started reading the rather long message. It began with a polite greeting and added that he was writing a message since he couldn’t reach him by phone. He expressed that he didn’t want to disturb him if he was doing something important or still resting.
Then he stated why he was reaching out.

He first explained that Soren’s original recipes had all been formally submitted, reviewed, and accepted into the association’s database, meaning they would now be available for other magic chefs to learn and share. He offered his warmest congratulations and praised Soren for such a noble deed, expressing his belief that Soren’s name would eventually echo across not only the Temur Empire, but the entire continent or even the world.

Furthermore, Doran mentioned that after extensive discussion with the other branch heads, they had unanimously decided to promote Soren’s official rank directly from Expert Chef to Senior Chef, waiving the need for another practical evaluation. He closed the message with another set of hearty congratulations and well wishes for Soren’s continued well-being.
’...So it’s finally wrapped up.’ Soren thought, relaxing his shoulders as he finished skimming the text.

A small smile touched his lips at the thought that Doran still believed he was resting and recovering from severe injuries. Misunderstandings aside, the branch head had proven himself to be a man worthy of respect once again. He had faithfully executed every detail of their arrangement, honoring his word without hesitation and personally reaching out to keep him informed.
’I even got to increase my rank easily thanks to him.’
He didn’t doubt it was Doran who must have pushed the idea and made others agree.
’I should respond properly too.’

Tapping on the screen, he typed out a polite reply thanking Doran for his immense help, for handling the submission so smoothly, and for his thoughtful well wishes. He added a brief reassurance that his recovery was progressing smoothly so the old master wouldn’t worry.
After sending the text, his thoughts naturally drifted back to the broader impact of the release.

He wondered how his authority would process this development. With his recipes now circulating among magic chefs across the region, the prospective returns could prove substantial. It was still uncertain exactly how those yields would take shape, but there was no reason to rush.
’I will find out when the time comes,’ he reasoned. ’Most likely, the messages will start flowing in once I step out of seclusion.’

As for his name making waves, Soren didn’t care much about it, nor did he expect things to go quite as far as Doran had hoped. Still, having a higher rank and a recognized reputation would certainly open a few doors, making it easier to acquire rare ingredients or handle matters in the culinary world down the line. That alone was enough for him.
’...Then again, I wonder if Lady Nuelia has arrived safely at her home.’

Soren narrowed his eyes thoughtfully, pulled up her contact, and tapped out a polite message asking about her journey back and a few other things. Once the text went through, he nodded to himself in satisfaction, slipped the phone back into his pocket, and stepped out of the bedroom.

Since Zura had mentioned that she would be running a bit late, he decided to get a head start. He made his way to the kitchen and set to work, organizing the ingredients, prepping the cookware, and setting the dining table so they could dive straight into cooking the moment she arrived.

Not long after he finished prepping, Zura arrived with her usual lively energy. They gently ’woke’ Ethea from her rest, and soon the kitchen filled with familiar warmth as the three of them set to work cooking dinner together, seamlessly repeating the pleasant routine of the previous evening.
However, once they sat down to eat, Soren decided to bring up the matter.
"I think I’m going to break through soon."
Zura paused mid-bite, her spoon hovering inches from her mouth as she blinked in surprise. "Huh? Already? Didn’t you say just yesterday that you’d need a few more days?"

Soren nodded and set his cutlery down. "It’s largely thanks to the meal. I managed to absorb a solid amount of mana from it, which sped things up considerably. If I cultivate seriously, by tomorrow morning, I should reach my capacity limit."
He turned his gaze toward Ethea, a fleeting trace of reluctance softening his expression. "My only concern is leaving her alone..."

"...Dear," Ethea’s expression softened with affection at his words. Then she offered him a reassuring smile. "Please don’t worry about me. Focus on yourself, and I’m sure you’ll get through this successfully.
"She’s right," Zura piped up, tapping her chest confidently with her spoon. "I’ll look after her myself, so you can focus on breaking through."
Soren looked back at Zura. "...Will it really be alright?"

"Of course! It’s not as if we haven’t stayed under the same roof before," Zura replied with a playful smirk, then her expression grew curious. "More importantly, where are you planning to do it? Did the Vice Principal approve your request?"
"Yes," Soren replied with a small nod. "I’ll be holding the breakthrough within the academy’s grounds."

"Oh, then that works out perfectly," Zura grinned. "Ethea and I can just stay at my academy villa while you’re in seclusion. We will be right nearby if you need anything, and we can easily meet up the moment you finish."
"That’s good." Soren smiled and paused. "You have a villa in the academy?"
Zura tilted her head, blinking in slight confusion. "Huh? I didn’t tell you before?"
Soren shook his head. "No. And if you have a villa there, why aren’t you staying in it instead?"

"Well, it’s pretty big, and I really don’t feel like taking care of a whole house by myself," Zura explained with a casual shrug. "So I just stay at a small apartment nearby instead. It’s much easier."
"I see," Soren nodded understandingly.

"Hey, don’t misunderstand it!" Zura hurriedly added, waving her hands defensively. "It’s not that I’m lazy or anything — it’s just practical! Managing a large place all alone takes way too much effort, so saving that energy for cultivating makes far more sense."
Soren let out a quiet chuckle, a faint smirk tugging at his lips as he decided to tease her back.
"Mm, I understand. It must be quite a chore, managing all that extra space when you could just stay in a cozy apartment..."
"Hey, it really is!" Zura puffed out her cheeks, crossing her arms. "You’ll see when we get there. It’s way too big for just one person!"
"It must be lonely too..."

"That’s right!" Zura nodded enthusiastically, as if he had finally caught on to her logic. "It’s way too boring on your own. But now I have Ethea staying with me! So it won’t feel empty at all while you’re tucked away in seclusion."
"...Am I just entertainment to you, Zura?" Ethea asked coldly, raising a brow.
"Huh? No, why are you-!" Zura cut herself off mid-sentence, catching the amusement in their eyes. She let out an incredulous laugh. "Haha, look at you two! Joining hands to gang up on me now, huh?"
Soren and Ethea exchanged a glance and shook their heads in perfect unison, innocence written all over their faces.
"Well, laugh while you can!" Zura puffed out her chest and smirked evilly. "Once he leaves for seclusion, let’s see how it feels to be lonely~."

They gently ’woke’ Ethea from her rest, and soon the kitchen filled with familiar warmth as the three of them set to work cooking dinner together, seamlessly repeating the pleasant routine of the previous evening.
However, once they sat down to eat, Soren decided to bring up the matter.
"I think I’m going to break through soon."
Zura paused mid-bite, her spoon hovering inches from her mouth as she blinked in surprise.
"Huh?
Already?
Didn’t you say just yesterday that you’d need a few more days?"
Soren nodded and set his cutlery down.
"It’s largely thanks to the meal.
I managed to absorb a solid amount of mana from it, which sped things up considerably.
If I cultivate seriously, by tomorrow morning, I should reach my capacity limit."
He turned his gaze toward Ethea, a fleeting trace of reluctance softening his expression.
"My only concern is leaving her alone..."
"...Dear," Ethea’s expression softened with affection at his words.
Then she offered him a reassuring smile.
"Please don’t worry about me.
Focus on yourself, and I’m sure you’ll get through this successfully.
"She’s right," Zura piped up, tapping her chest confidently with her spoon.
"I’ll look after her myself, so you can focus on breaking through."
Soren looked back at Zura.
"...Will it really be alright?"
"Of course!
It’s not as if we haven’t stayed under the same roof before," Zura replied with a playful smirk, then her expression grew curious.
"More importantly, where are you planning to do it?
Did the Vice Principal approve your request?"
"Yes," Soren replied with a small nod.
"I’ll be holding the breakthrough within the academy’s grounds."
"Oh, then that works out perfectly," Zura grinned.
"Ethea and I can just stay at my academy villa while you’re in seclusion.
We will be right nearby if you need anything, and we can easily meet up the moment you finish."
"That’s good." Soren smiled and paused.
"You have a villa in the academy?"
Zura tilted her head, blinking in slight confusion.
"Huh?
I didn’t tell you before?"
Soren shook his head.
"No.
And if you have a villa there, why aren’t you staying in it instead?"
"Well, it’s pretty big, and I really don’t feel like taking care of a whole house by myself," Zura explained with a casual shrug.
"So I just stay at a small apartment nearby instead.
It’s much easier."
"I see," Soren nodded understandingly.
"Hey, don’t misunderstand it!" Zura hurriedly added, waving her hands defensively.
"It’s not that I’m lazy or anything — it’s just practical!
Managing a large place all alone takes way too much effort, so saving that energy for cultivating makes far more sense."
Soren let out a quiet chuckle, a faint smirk tugging at his lips as he decided to tease her back.
"Mm, I understand.
It must be quite a chore, managing all that extra space when you could just stay in a cozy apartment..."
"Hey, it really is!" Zura puffed out her cheeks, crossing her arms.
"You’ll see when we get there.
It’s way too big for just one person!"
"It must be lonely too..."
"That’s right!" Zura nodded enthusiastically, as if he had finally caught on to her logic.
"It’s way too boring on your own.
But now I have Ethea staying with me!
So it won’t feel empty at all while you’re tucked away in seclusion."
"...Am I just entertainment to you, Zura?" Ethea asked coldly, raising a brow.
"Huh?
No, why are you-!" Zura cut herself off mid-sentence, catching the amusement in their eyes.
She let out an incredulous laugh.
"Haha, look at you two!
Joining hands to gang up on me now, huh?"
Soren and Ethea exchanged a glance and shook their heads in perfect unison, innocence written all over their faces.
"Well, laugh while you can!" Zura puffed out her chest and smirked evilly.
"Once he leaves for seclusion, let’s see how it feels to be lonely~."

chapters.title: Chapter 390: Zura’s Villa
paragraphs: Zura’s words evaporated the playful atmosphere in an instant, leaving both Soren and Ethea with visibly fallen expressions.
Without meaning to, she had blurted out the exact thing they were trying to ignore.

For all their cheerful talk over dinner, the thought of being apart had been sitting in the back of their minds the whole time. With no way to tell how long his seclusion would actually drag on, saying goodbye so soon after finally reaching this point in their relationship was a tough pill to swallow.
’Huh? Did I say something wrong?’

Seeing the mood plunge so fast, Zura blinked in confusion. As she activated her insight talent, her eyes subtly shimmered as she took in their emotional flow. The moment she registered the raw reluctance stirring between them, she realized it, and a wave of awkward guilt washed over her.

"Ah... wait! Forget I said that!" she stammered, frantically waving her hands to patch up the mood. "Look, if you’re worried about missing each other, just make the most of tonight! Fill up on each other’s faces, talk until you’re sick of listening, and get your fill before tomorrow. Problem solved!"
Soren and Ethea looked at her, then turned to each other with faint smiles.

While the reluctance was real, neither of them was foolish enough to let it hold them back. Breakthroughs were a necessity, and short separations were simply part of life. Like mature adults, they understood that brooding over the inevitable wouldn’t change a thing.
Still, taking Zura’s advice sounded like a really good plan.
"...Dear."
They turned back to each other, their faces giving away exactly how much they cared about one another without a word spoken. In fact, they were too obvious about it.
"..." Zura deadpanned, looking back and forth between the two. "Can you two at least hold off until I leave?"
"...Hehe." Ethea let out a sheepish chuckle, while Soren simply smiled, the earlier awkward mood completely swept away.
"Hmph," Zura snorted, though a faint smile tugged at the corner of her lips.

They finished the rest of the meal in good spirits, chatting easily and sorting out the plans involving Nura and the villa. When the meal finally wound down, Zura bade them goodnight and headed out to her own place. Soren and Ethea cleaned up, showered, and changed into sleep clothes.

Soren pulled Ethea close, wrapping his arms around her as they lay side by side, looking into each other’s eyes. They wanted to carve every single detail of this moment into their minds, a feeling that shone clearly in the depth of their gaze. No words were needed between them tonight.
"I love you, Ethea."
Soren whispered and leaned in, kissing her deeply, pouring all his affection into the touch. Ethea kissed him back, resting her hands against his chest until the kiss slowly drew to an end.
"Goodnight... And..."
She kissed him back.
"...I love you too."
She then rested her head against his arm, and they closed their eyes, sinking into sleep together.
"So this is the big villa you talked about," Soren said, taking in the sight before them.

The structure featured clean architectural lines, sweeping stone arches, and tall windows that let in plenty of daylight. It was sprawling, yet the design avoided unnecessary ostentation, balancing elegance with actual functionality.
Zura nodded smugly, arms crossed over her chest as she stepped up to the front doors and pushed them open. "Come on in!"

Inside, the layout was practical as well as refined. High ceilings gave the main hall an open feel, with polished floors running throughout and tastefully arranged furniture lining the main living space. Broad hallways ensured easy movement, making transitions between rooms seamless.
"Not bad at all," Soren praised, glancing around the main floor. "It’s well-designed."
"Told you!" Zura beamed, practically puffing up with pride. "Come on, I’ll give you a tour."

They nodded and followed after Zura. The ground floor housed a spacious dining area, a fully equipped kitchen, and study nooks, while the upper level contained several private guest rooms, a cultivation room, and a large balcony. Every space was tastefully furnished and well kept, designed for comfort and daily convenience.
"Should we head to the bedroom now?" Soren asked as they stepped down the stairs back toward the main hallway.
"Ah, right," Zura nodded. "You said you wanted to teach something."
She stepped ahead to lead the way down a wide corridor toward the primary bedroom suite on the ground floor.
"I want to walk you through Ethea’s caretaking routine," Soren explained as they walked. "I’ll show you how it’s done now, so please pay attention and try to get the hang of it."
"Got it," Zura replied, nodding seriously. "Show me the ropes."
Once they stepped inside, Soren started the lesson. "...Watch closely. The most important part is making sure she stays comfortable and safe during transfers."

He moved beside Ethea’s wheelchair, explaining each step clearly as he demonstrated. He showed Zura the proper grip and posture needed to lift Ethea without straining either of them, how to pivot cleanly to move her to and from the bed, and how to adjust her position once she was settled. He covered every detail, from supporting her back to positioning her legs correctly.
After finishing the lesson, Soren pulled a folded piece of paper from his pocket and handed it over.
"I wrote down her dietary restrictions and the foods she likes," Soren said, then added after a pause. "Ethea can guide you through the rest later."
Zura took the paper, read the detailed list, then looked up at him with a bemused expression.

"I think you’re way too protective of her," Zura muttered, though a genuine smile broke across her face a moment later. "But I approve! Honestly, if two people were ever meant to end up together, it’s definitely you two."
"Mm, I can’t argue with that," Soren admitted, a hint of warmth in his eyes as he glanced back at Ethea. "After all, we’re bound together for life, and there’s truly no one else for me."
"...Urgh, if you keep being like this, I will kick you out right now!"

chapters.title: Chapter 391: Into the Seclusion
paragraphs: With that slightly cheesy episode, they stayed in the room for a while, talking through the last few small details and making sure everything was settled. When the time came, Soren took a deep breath, knowing he couldn’t delay his seclusion any longer.
He stepped up to Ethea and leaned down to pull her into a close hug. Holding her against him for a brief moment, he pressed a gentle kiss to her forehead before pulling back.
"I’ll be back as soon as I can," Soren said softly, offering her one last look before turning toward the door. "Take care of yourself."
"Good luck!" Zura called out, waving encouragingly.
Ethea raised her hand as well, her eyes fixed on him with encouragement and confidence. "Do your best, dear. We’ll be waiting."
Soren gave them both a final nod and took his leave.
’...Malakor.’ He called out in his mind after walking a fair amount of distance.
’...Master.’ Malakor replied almost instantly.
’You know what to do, right?’ Soren asked.
’Yes.’

’Good. However, if you’re discovered and your life is in danger, don’t hesitate to abandon the mission and run away.’ Soren instructed firmly. ’And if I complete my breakthrough and come out before you return, I’ll contact you myself.’
’I understand, Master,’ Malakor answered without hesitation. ’May your breakthrough go smoothly.’
’Thank you,’ Soren replied. ’And good luck to you too.’
With their final exchange complete, the mental connection went quiet, leaving Soren alone as he continued his way toward his destination.
About ten minutes later, he arrived at Vice Principal Ramona’s office. He knocked once, stepped inside, and exchanged brief greetings with her.
"Are you ready?" Ramona asked, setting aside her paperwork and looking up at him.
Soren gave a firm nod. "I am.
"In that case, let’s go," she said.

Ramona raised her hand and channeled a surge of mana. Space distorted around them in an instant, and the office melted away. When the sudden flash of light settled, a familiar chilling sensation struck Soren’s face.

He looked around, taking in the vast expanse of ice and snow blanketing the ground and jagged mountain peaks stretching out into the pale horizon. Frost hung thick in the air, creating a dense environment saturated with frigid mana.
"Since your affinity is ice, I chose this secluded chamber for you," Ramona explained, adjusting her coat slightly against the frosty wind. "It will aid your concentration and mana gathering."
"Thank you for being so thoughtful," Soren said, genuinely appreciating the preparation.
"Do well," Ramona said, offering him a brief nod of encouragement. "Good luck."
With a flick of her wrist, space warped again, and she disappeared from sight, leaving him alone.

Soren took a deep breath and walked to the center of the snowy clearing, sat down cross-legged, and closed his eyes. Closing off all external distractions, he began initiating the breakthrough process and soon lost himself to the rhythm of his meditation.
Later afternoon, Nura headed for her private lesson with Instructor Zura.

As she walked toward the classroom, her thoughts drifted to the gift the Instructor had mentioned yesterday. She wondered what kind of surprise her tutor had prepared. She had said it would be something Nura actually needed, which left her curious. Could it be a unique cultivation technique, or maybe a new spell tailored to her affinities?

Entering the room, she took her usual seat and pulled out her books and notebooks, laying them flat on the desk. She shook her head slightly and refocused on the task at hand. She would find out soon enough anyway, so she decided to make good use of the time and start reviewing yesterday’s material.
And just like that, half an hour passed in the blink of an eye.
Nura finally lifted her head from the open pages, stretched her arms above her head, and let out a small yawn. Mid-stretch, she froze.
Sitting quietly in the teacher’s seat at the front of the room was a familiar figure, watching her with an amused expression.
"Ah!" Nura blurted out, dropping her arms quickly. "Teacher! When did you—I mean, good afternoon!"
"Good afternoon, Nura," Zura replied, waving a hand playfully. Her wavy bob shook lightly as her lips curled up mischievously. "Did you lose yourself in your studying again?"
Nura blushed, ducking her head with a sheepish nod.
Zura let out a soft laugh, resting her chin on her hand. "Alright, gather your things."
"Huh? What do you mean?" Nura blinked in confusion, her hand pausing over her desk.
"We won’t be studying theory today," Zura explained, leaning back in her chair.
"So it’s a practical lesson?" Nura asked, her curiosity piqued. She hurriedly gathered her books and notebooks, stuffing them back into her bag.
"Something like that," Zura answered, watching her zip the bag shut. Once Nura swung it over her shoulder, Zura stood up and gestured toward the door. "Follow me."
Nura silently followed after her down the corridor. After walking a short distance, Zura glanced back over her shoulder.
"By the way, did you eat lunch? Are you hungry at all?"
Nura raised an eyebrow at the sudden question, but replied truthfully. "I ate lunch, so I’m not that hungry right now."
"I see," Zura muttered, turning her head back forward as she lapsed into silence.
Nura narrowed her eyes slightly, watching the back of her instructor and thought, ’Could she be taking me out to treat me to a meal or something?’

However, that guess quickly faded as Zura led her away from the central facilities and toward the quieter edge of the campus. Before long, they arrived at a spacious villa tucked into a corner of the outer academy grounds.
While Nura looked around the property, taking in the peaceful surroundings, Zura pushed open the front entrance.
"Take a seat in the living room," Zura instructed, gesturing toward the main hall. "I’ll go grab something to drink."
Nura nodded and stepped inside. As she entered the living area, her attention settled on the center of the room, where a beautiful, silver-haired woman sat in a wheelchair with a plushie on her lap.
’...Is she someone close to Instructor Zura?’ Nura briefly wondered, then composed herself. Not wanting to seem rude by staring, she straightened her posture and offered a polite bow.
"Good afternoon. I’m Nura, one of Instructor Zura’s students."

chapters.title: Chapter 392: A Gift
paragraphs: The woman turned toward Nura and gave a subtle nod, accompanied by an amiable smile. "Hello, Nura. I’m Lea, a close friend of your instructor."
"Y-yes..." Nura muttered, momentarily captivated by the woman’s graceful appearance and gentle smile.
"She’s my best friend, to be more exact," a voice echoed from behind as a hand rested on Nura’s shoulder, making her jump in surprise.
Zura giggled as she walked past, carrying a tray of tea. "Skittish as ever, aren’t you?"
Nura felt heat rush to her cheeks, blushing in embarrassment once again as she tried to regain her composure. She quickly bowed her head to hide her red face.
"I brought some tea," Zura said, setting the tray down on the table between the couches. She gestured toward the seat opposite Lea. "Sit down, Nura. There’s no need to stand on ceremony here."
Nura nodded and carefully sat down, trying to keep her posture straight as her mind raced with questions. She glanced between Zura and Lea, wondering what kind of lesson this was supposed to be.
Zura poured tea for everyone, handed the first cup to Lea, then slid another across the table to Nura.
"I know you’re probably confused right now," Zura began, taking a seat beside her friend. "Truth is, I brought you here to give you that gift I mentioned yesterday."
Nura accepted her cup with both hands, taking a tiny sip before looking up with a puzzled look. "The gift... is it meeting your friend?"
"Haha, no, of course not~" Zura laughed again, then paused. "Well, in fact, getting to know Lea is a privilege on its own. But the gift I brought you here to receive is this."
Zura reached into her storage ring and retrieved a heat-insulated magic container. She set it down in the center of the table and popped open the lid.

A rich, savory steam rose into the air as the meal came into view: a vibrant, perfectly balanced dish of tender cuts of meat nestled over fluffy, fragrant rice, with aromatic vegetables glistening throughout.
Nura’s eyes widened slightly as the rich aroma reached her.
"Is this..." Nura started, her gaze shifting from the steaming meal back to Zura. "The gift?
"Mm. It’s a magic meal specifically made for you." Zura replied. "It will help you heal your damaged pathways and core, and will also strengthen your body."

A spark of genuine excitement lit up Nura’s face as she processed what that meant. Yet a second later, a wave of hesitation crossed her face. "Is it really alright for me to accept something this valuable?"
"Of course. Or..." Zura paused, tilting her head. "Do you not want to improve?"
Nura shook her head immediately. "No! I definitely want to get better!"
"Good," Zura smiled warmly. "If you like it and the effects work well, I’ll bring you more. But... you have to promise me you won’t tell anyone about this... Not even your family."
Nura’s expressive eyes flickered with doubt. She leaned forward slightly and asked cautiously, "Why?"
Zura’s playful tone vanished, her expression turning dead serious. "Because...
Nura swallowed hard, her heart pounding as wild theories raced through her mind. Was this some forbidden food? Illegal? Or did it have some hidden side effect?

"What... what is actually going on?" Nura asked, looking back and forth between the two of them.

"Don’t listen to her nonsense. She’s just playing with you," Lea said with a soft chuckle, shaking her head. She turned her eyes to Nura, her tone taking on a gentler tone. "However, she really did go through a lot of effort to get this meal for you. And the chef who made this food doesn’t want anyone to know about it or that they were the one who prepared it. "I see..." Nura muttered and nodded earnestly. "I swear I won’t say a word to anyone. My lips are sealed."
"Good girl," Lea said, her expression softening as she gestured toward the steaming container on the table. "Now, go on and eat before it gets cold."

Nura’s eyes widened in surprise. Her face instantly flushed as she realized her oversight. "Ah... I’m so sorry! I didn’t mean to-"
"Don’t worry about it," Lea interrupted gently, waving off the apology.

"Alright, enough fussing," Zura chimed in, resting an arm over the back of the couch. "Don’t eat too much all at once. Take a few bites, then pause to absorb the mana and let it settle through your pathways first."

The moment the flavor hit her tongue, her eyes went wide. It tasted incredible, far beyond anything she had tasted in the academy’s kitchen or anywhere else she had visited until then. But even more surprising than the flavor was the sudden sensation that followed.

As soon as she swallowed, a wave of soothing warmth bloomed deep in her chest. The heat spread outward in soft ripples, sinking directly into her damaged mana pathways. The dull ache around her core eased, and the flow of mana became a bit smoother.

"A-Amazing..." She muttered in awe, then, recalling Zura’s advice, quickly closed her eyes and focused inward. She carefully guided the current through her mana pathways, allowing the magic food to take effect.

"It really works just like you said, Teacher!"
"I told you." Zura chuckled with satisfaction. "Keep going at that pace. I’ll keep an eye on you while you eat."

Nura nodded enthusiastically and picked up her spoon again. Taking small portions at a time, she repeated the process: eating a few bites, closing her eyes, and carefully circulating warm energy through her pathways.
An hour passed, and the container gradually emptied until Nura finally set down her spoon, having finished every last drop.
"How do you feel?" Lea asked while lowering her cup.
"I feel great!" Nura smiled brightly. "Thank you"
She turned to Zura, her excitement bubbling over. "Teacher, look!"
Nura raised her open palm between them. "...Ignite."
A small fireball appeared above her hand and hovered steadily. Then the floating flame stretched and narrowed, molding itself into an arrow’s outline.

"Hmm..." Narrowing her eyes, she flicked her wrist, and the floating flame stretched into a small blade, melted into a swirling ring, then reshaped into an arrow. With another subtle shift of her mana, the fiery arrow dissolved into a cluster of swirling sparks and quickly split into roughly twenty thin needles suspended in midair.
As she continued to manipulate the flame, her control became smoother, without the usual strain or trembling that used to ruin her spells.
Zura’s eyes lit up as she clapped her hands together. "Amazing! Your control has already improved so much!"
"Hehe, it’s all thanks to the gift you gave me, Teacher!" Nura laughed, a bright spark of pure happiness lighting up her face.

For the first time in months, she felt genuine hope. Her damaged pathways were finally healing, and her strength was actually returning, all from just a single meal. Overwhelmed with relief, she stood up and bowed deeply to Zura.
"I will never forget this kindness, and I promise to work hard to repay you," Nura said earnestly.
Zura smiled and shook her head slightly. "The one you should be thanking isn’t me, but the person who cooked this for you."
"R-Rght," Nura straightened up, her curiosity piqued. "Then... Is it possible to meet that person? I really want to thank them in person."
Zura shook her head. "Unfortunately, no. Because he’s currently in seclusion. But once he comes out, I’ll try to arrange a meeting for the two of you."
"Thank you!"
"Haha, don’t get your hopes up too high just yet. I honestly have no idea when he’ll actually finish his seclusion."
"That’s alright. I can wait as long as it takes."

chapters.title: Chapter 393: ...Incredible
paragraphs: Nura stayed with them for another hour. Once Zura was sure nothing was wrong and that Nura had absorbed the magic food, she gave her permission to head back.
"Get some rest, and remember to keep practicing your control," Zura instructed, her expression relaxed as she saw Nura off at the door. "Don’t forget to visit tomorrow too."
"I won’t! Thank you so much, Teacher. Thank you, Sister Lea," Nura said, bowing politely to both of them before leaving the villa.

Zura and Lea watched as Nura left the villa grounds, her stride full of fresh energy. When she was out of sight, Zura leaned back against the doorway and smirked. "You really are good at this. Already got her calling you Sister on day one."

’Well, she is my husband’s little sister, after all.’ Ethea thought to herself with genuine affection. Out loud, she gave a modest chuckle. "I just treated her the way I would want someone to treat my own little sister."
"Haha, that’s so like you," Zura laughed, wheeling her back inside.
Once the front door closed and they sat down, her playful demeanor gave way to a more focused one. "Still, she didn’t react at all when we mentioned his name earlier."

Ethea nodded thoughtfully, hugging the plushie tightly. "...Either she genuinely remembers nothing about him, and Valmeres kept her completely in the dark, or she is remarkably skilled at hiding her emotions."
"Right... Speaking of emotions," Zura said, narrowing her eyes as she leaned against the sofa, "I picked up a distinct trace of doubt from her when I brought up her memory recovery."

"Couldn’t that have been natural?" Ethea tilted her head slightly. "She has been struggling with this condition for so long. She might have just been unsure about whether she will ever get those memories back."
"Well, you are right about that, but do you remember what he said?"
Ethea fell silent and recalled Soren’s words. ’Hmm... Right, he told us Nura might already suspect her parents and perhaps the whole situation. However, he didn’t know why or how.’
"Should we investigate?"

"...I think we should wait till he comes out of seclusion," Zura answered, resting her chin on her hand. "However, if there is a chance, we can gently probe around without pushing too hard. We definitely shouldn’t do anything to make her suspect us."
"Right." Ethea nodded in agreement. "I also want to build a genuine bond with her, not drive a wedge between us or make her put her guard up."

"I guess you are lucky then," Zura’s lips curled up. "You have enough time to get close to her at a natural pace before everything comes out in the open. And once she finally recovers her memories, you won’t have to start from scratch to build that trust."
"...Let’s hope so."

"Come on, you should be more positive about it!" Zura said, clapping Ethea gently on the shoulder with a light grin. "You saw how quickly she warmed to you today. At this rate, she’ll be looking up to you in no time."
Ethea let out a small breath, her expression softening as she looked toward the door. "...I just want things to go smoothly for her sake. She has already carried enough burden on her own."
"She has," Zura agreed, stepping back toward the kitchen to clean up the remaining dishes. "Which is why today was a solid start. And... you should get some rest now. We will continue it tomorrow."
"...Alright." Ethea nodded and let Zura bring her into the bedroom and put her on the bed.
Zura put a light blanket on top of her and muttered with a smile. "Sleep well."
Ethea closed her eyes and entered her soul space.

Inside, the vast dark void stretched endlessly, illuminated by the radiant glow of countless shimmering stars. The brilliant points of starlight drifted around her, pulsing gently to the rhythm of her breathing. As she gazed at the boundless cosmic display around her, calm determination settled deep in her chest.

’...I should work hard too,’ she thought, watching the starlight weave through the void. She didn’t want to always sit back and watch helplessly while others carried the burden. ’Before he comes out of seclusion, I should try to break through to the next stage.’
With that single-minded thought, she closed her eyes within the stellar expanse and began to cultivate, drawing the ambient energy of the stars directly into her core.
Ten days passed in the blink of an eye.

The special glacial breakthrough spatial chamber was usually freezing; however, it was especially frigid today. The temperature inside had dropped to levels that would kill an ordinary person within seconds. A blizzard raged within the enclosed space, snow and ice swirling in violent currents.

At the center of the storm stood a massive block of translucent ice, towering like a solitary monolith. The raging snowstorm revolved around it, feeding its pristine surface with layer after layer of pure glacial essence.
As time passed, the howling wind gradually died down, leaving behind a stark, motionless silence.
"...Crackle."

A crisp snap broke the silence, and on the surface of the frozen monolith, a tiny hairline fracture appeared. Within seconds, spiderweb cracks branched out in every direction, spreading rapidly across the whole surface.
Crackle-!
Crackle-!
Crackle-!
The cracking sounds intensified until the monolith’s structural integrity failed completely, and the ice gave way in a blinding burst of motion.
BOOM!
The ice shattered, bursting outward in a shower of countless shimmering fragments that dissolved into fine mist before they even touched the floor.
At the epicenter of the burst sat a solitary human figure. He opened his eyes, and a brilliant flash of pure white light burst from his gaze as the surging glacial aura settled around him.
"Huff..."

He let out a long breath that instantly crystallized into a plume of white mist before dispersing into the air. He drew in a deep intake of the freezing atmosphere, letting his lungs adapt to the newly heightened baseline of his core.
Straightening his posture, he slowly looked down at himself.

His upper body was completely bare, exposing his chiseled chest and tightly defined abs, both glistening faintly under the remaining glacial shimmer. A satisfied smile touched his lips as he stretched his shoulders, feeling the raw power flowing through his veins.
He paused, looking around the vast space as the storm around him began to calm.
’...How long has it been?’

He narrowed his eyes, and with a light flick of his fingers, a translucent barrier expanded around him, instantly walling off the extreme cold and absolute zero environment of the chamber. Inside the small perimeter, the temperature stabilized.
He then reached into his inventory space, pulled out his phone, and lit up the screen.
’...Eleven days, huh.’ He checked the clock and noted the time.
’...Looks like it’s early morning.’
He slipped the phone back into his mental inventory, closed his eyes, and mentally called out to bring up his status.

’Hmm...’ His eyes scrolled through the translucent window and stopped at the particular line that drew his immediate attention.
All he could utter was a single word.
’...Incredible.’

chapters.title: Chapter 394: Breaking Through!
paragraphs: To think his capacity would increase to two and a half million, and at the 5th stage no less.
’It’s not different from an Emperor’s mana capacity!’
In fact, that figure was comparable to emperors known for their unusually large energy reserves.
’Just what kind of monster am I becoming?’
At the staggering thought, his heart thudded wildly against his ribs as adrenaline surged through his limbs. He closed his eyes and took a deep breath, forcing himself to regain his composure.

It was an astounding leap, but he needed to remain rational. While his sheer mana volume might match an emperor’s, a vast gap still separated them. After all, mana was just energy, a fuel for the Awakened. Without the domain control, refined intent, and authority that came with the higher realms, raw capacity alone did not make one invincible.
’Still... I will be far stronger when I actually reach that stage.’
He pondered his growth trajectory. If his foundation was already this broad at the 5th stage, what would happen when he reached the 7th circle? Would his pool expand past ten million?
Somehow, with his investment authority driving every milestone, that unthinkable number felt less like a distant dream and more like a guaranteed milestone.
’Speaking of which, should I check if there are any finished or ongoing investments?’
The idea was tempting, but he quickly put it on hold. He decided to finish reviewing his status window before turning his attention elsewhere.
As his eyes continued down the panel, he paused at the line directly below his mana pool.
[Mental Power Capacity: 197,740 / 200,000]
His gaze lingered on the numbers. His mental capacity had grown by another twenty thousand, bringing him within striking distance of the upper limit.
Did the breakthrough cause this jump, or was it a return on investment?

Regardless of the source, the opportunity was clear. Reaching the threshold would allow him to trigger a breakthrough in his mental cultivation as well. Completing both advancements in quick succession would solidify his foundation before he stepped out of seclusion.
He clenched his fists and quickly skimmed the rest of his status window. Finding no other significant changes to his core stats or other tabs, he opened the notifications.

Four completed investment notifications were waiting for him. The first two came from Zura and Malakor. He opened them and initiated the integration, receiving a total of 60,000 mana and a new recipe specifically designed for magic beast bonds. They were satisfactory for moderate-grade investments.

The third one came from Ryan and was high-grade. It gave him 20,000 mana and an artifact called the Flameheart Stone. According to its description, it can start fires or enhance fire-based cooking. It would never cool down, so it could be used indefinitely and would be useful for cooking in the future.
And finally...
’It’s from Nura...’
Soren’s lips curled up because it meant that his food worked and she got better, no matter how small the improvement might have been.
He then tapped yes, and messages appeared in his vision.
[Investment detected.]
[Target: Nura Valmere]
[Analyzing Investment...]
[Investment: You provided the target with a specially prepared magic meal tailored to her fire-attribute constitution...]
[Analyzing target response...]

[As a result of your actions, the target’s condition has improved considerably. Her damaged pathways and core have begun to heal, and her fire mana is no longer as volatile. She doesn’t know your name or your face, but she is profoundly thankful to the person who offered her hope and a chance to get better.]
[Evaluating investment significance...]
[Evaluation complete.]
[Investment Grade: SUPREME]
[Calculating returns...]
[Calculation complete.]
[Applying Authority Modifier: Amplification (Passive) — Baseline bonus applied. Reward tier scaling upgraded.]
[Returns granted:]
[2. Cooking Mastery +1]
[3. Recipe Unlocked: Flameheart Risotto]
[4. Fire Resistance (B-Rank → A-Rank)]
[5. Solar Flare Extract]
[6. Sun’s Blessing (B-Rank)]
[Integration initiated...]
[Integration Complete!]
"Huff..."

Soren opened his eyes and let out a long breath. This time, his breath was warm, rising gently into the air without freezing as it had earlier. His whole body felt warm too, as if a gentle fire had been kindled inside him.
’This must be the passive effect of Sun’s Blessing.’
He thought, but decided to inspect the ability’s specifics and other returns later. With a mental command, he dismissed the glowing interface windows.

It was finally time to focus on his mental cultivation. He reached into his inventory, withdrew a Clear-Mind Serenity Pill, and swallowed it. The pill dissolved immediately, sending a cooling sensation straight to his mind. He then closed his eyes and sank his consciousness deep into his soul space.
Hours passed in complete silence within the subterranean chamber. With his concentration at its peak, he steadily gathered and refined his mental power, pushing it toward the final threshold.
After roughly four hours of continuous cultivation, a subtle tremor echoed through his mind space.
Soren recognized it at once. His spiritual core had reached its limit, and pressure was beginning to build within it.

He furrowed his brows and recalled the Scripture’s teachings about the third stage. The breakthrough wouldn’t happen on its own, and waiting for it would only waste time and opportunity. He had to force it himself and, no matter how difficult and painful it is, endure it.
’Huff... Alright, let’s start.’

Soren drew his mental power, gathering it from every corner of his soul space until it pooled around the core in a dense ring of golden light. Then he pressed the ring inward, compressing the core even further until the pressure inside became unbearable.

The core resisted, vibrating violently as Soren steadily tightened the ring of mental energy. However, soon enough, hairline fractures began to spread across its surface, groaning under the immense internal load.
’Urgh...’
A searing pain flared between his eyes, striking his forehead like a burning needle. But he kept his focus steady, refusing to let the sensation break his concentration.
Crackle...
Crackle...
The fractures deepened until the core gave way, cracking open like a seed splitting under immense strain.
Swoosh-!
From the heart of the split, a dense, thin tendril of golden mental power forced its way out.

Soren guided it upward, aiming for the invisible boundary that separated his soul space from his physical body. The moment the tip pressed against the wall, a wave of agony shot through his entire nervous system. It felt as though a thick pin was boring through his brainstem, trying to puncture his flesh from the inside out.

His jaw clamped tight. Sweat broke out across his forehead, mixing with the thin stream of blood that began to trickle from his left nostril. He ignored the burning sensation behind his eyes and pushed harder, driving the tendril forward millimeter by millimeter.
Swoosh-!
Swoosh-!

More tendrils began to emerge from the split core, each one thin and golden and writhing like a living thing. They spread out in different directions, some pressing against the boundary of his soul space, others curling around the walls and searching for weak points. Soren directed them with his will, spreading the pressure across multiple points. The agony dulled from a single searing spike to a broad, throbbing ache that he could push through.

He pinpointed the cracks along the boundary where the spiritual wall felt thinnest. Bending his intent toward those coordinates, he forced the golden tendrils to align, their sharp tips pointing straight up like needles.
With a single, unified push, he drove them against the weakened points at once.

The boundary groaned under the combined pressure, and Soren felt the resistance buckle. A network of fine cracks spread across the wall, connecting the points he had struck. Despite the immense pain tearing through his mind, he pushed harder, channeling more power into the tendrils until the cracks joined and the wall began to give way.
’A-Again!’

He pulled the tendrils back and drove them forward again, striking the same weakened points. The cracks widened, and a thin line of golden light split the boundary from one end to the other. Soren pushed one more time, pouring everything he had into the strike.
’...BOOM!’
The golden tendrils burst through into his physical body, and a wave of spiritual force exploded outward from his soul space.

In the real world, the surrounding ice and snow were blown away from him in a wide circle, clearing the floor around his seated form and sending the frozen debris skittering into the far corners. The air rippled visibly as the wave passed through it, distorting the space around him like heat rising from a summer road.

Soren’s eyes snapped open, radiant golden light flickering in his gaze, and the pressure radiating from his body settled over the chamber like an invisible hand pressing down on everything within reach.

The pressure held for a moment before beginning to recede. The golden light in his eyes dimmed and faded, and his gaze returned to its usual brown. He exhaled sharply, then quickly closed his eyes again.
It wasn’t over yet!

chapters.title: Chapter 395: Breaking Through! [2]
paragraphs: The breakthrough to the Spiritual Manifestation stage had opened the channel between his mind and his body, but the spiritual core itself was still fractured, and he had to retract and gather his scattered mental power to finish the process.

Soren directed the stray strands of energy floating through his soul space, pulling them back toward the center. Like rivers flowing back to their source, the golden light streamed inward, pooling in the fractured core, filling its cracks, and coating its surface.
’Now, I have to hammer it...’
He narrowed his eyes and shaped a portion of his mental force into a golden hammer. He gripped the weapon and raised it high above the core.

Unfortunately, the scripture hadn’t described this part in detail. It mentioned reforging the core after the breakthrough, but the exact method was left to the cultivator’s intuition. One wrong move might completely shatter the core, but yeah, he had to figure it out himself. To make it worse, he didn’t have the luxury of time. The longer the core remained cracked, the more energy leaked into the surrounding space, threatening to destabilize the newly formed connection.
’...Soren, you can do it. Just focus.’
He took a deep breath and floated around the core, studying it from every angle. Then he raised the hammer and brought it down slowly.
Clang.

The tool struck the core with a dull thud, sending a tremor through his soul space. Soren flinched at the brief stab of pain, but the cracked surface held. Golden light pooled inside the seam, compacting slightly as it welded the edges a fraction closer.
Encouraged by the result, he struck again, applying slightly more force. The impact rang out more clearly this time, driving the energy deeper into the crevice.
’Oh!’

His eyes lit up, and he struck again; however, he misjudged the force, hitting a delicate split at an awkward angle. A sharp spike of agony tore through his consciousness, and the crack he had been trying to seal split wider, golden light spilling out of the new fracture. Soren pulled the hammer back and gritted his teeth, waiting for the pain to fade before he tried again.
’I need to be more careful.’

He continued at a medium pace, adjusting the force with each strike. Some blows landed well and sealed the fractures, while the others were too strong or too weak, and he had to correct them each time while enduring the pain.
Clang! Clang! Clang!

Gradually, his control improved, and his movements gained a ceaseless rhythm. The trial and error faded as he learned the exact amount of power required for every angle and seam. Time slipped away, and he became fully immersed in the process, moving around the sphere and striking with precision.
Clang! Clang! Clang!

Blow after blow rained down upon the core, compressing the material and driving out every remaining flaw. The jagged fracture lines shrank, filled with golden light, and fused until the seams vanished entirely.
He raised the golden hammer one last time and brought it down with everything he had.
CLANG!

The impact resounded through his entire mind space, sending one last tremor across his soul before settling into silence. The hammer broke down into light as the ringing died away. Soren lowered his hands and took a moment to catch his breath, letting the tension drain from his arms as the pain in his head began to fade.
He then looked up to inspect his work.
’Whoa... Is this really my core?’
In place of the fractured seed sat a massive golden ball, its surface smoothed out and gleaming as if someone had trapped a miniature sun inside his soul space.
’It’s... a lot bigger than before. And it feels a lot stronger and sturdier too.’
He stared at it for a moment longer, then, thinking of something, summoned his status.
[PERSONAL INFORMATION]
Name: Soren Everly
Age: 23
Circle Rank: Fifth Circle (Early Stage)
Mental Cultivation: Sovereign Soul-Refining Scripture — Stage 3: Spiritual Manifestation Stage
Potential: ???
Hunter Rank: C
[CORE STATUS]
[Mental Power Capacity: 247740 / 500000]
His eyes briefly paused at the mental cultivation line, then scrolled down to the mental power capacity.
’Five hundred thousand...’ He couldn’t help but stare at the figure, a soft whistle escaping his lips.

That was more than double his previous limit, or, more precisely, two and a half times. The immense expansion explained why the forging process had taken such a brutal toll on his mind, but seeing the actual number made every second of that agony worth it. Not to mention the fact that he had already accumulated about fifty thousand mental power in the process.
He dismissed the status window and leaned back, letting his thoughts drift.
’It would have been amazing if the Authority rewarded me for investing in myself. Perhaps I would have become an Emperor by now...’

He gave a brief laugh at the absurd thought, then settled into a meditative pose and closed his eyes to steady his condition and calm himself. Time passed as he sat there, his mind gradually settling after the strain of the breakthrough. But when he finally opened his eyes, his breath caught in his throat.

Because across from him sat a beautiful woman with long silver hair and lively green eyes, full of curiosity and amusement. She leaned forward slightly, her chin resting on her knuckles as she studied him without a word.
Soren blinked and muttered in confusion.
"Vice Principal Ramona...?"
"...Good evening, Mr. Everly." She greeted him with a smile that radiated a motherly warmth. "And... congratulations on your successful breakthroughs."
Soren caught the meaning immediately and hurried to his feet, bowing deeply. "Thank you, Vice Principal. I wouldn’t have been able to do this without your permission and your hospitality."
Ramona chuckled. "There’s no need for such formality. Though I would suggest you get dressed first. It’s... a little distracting talking to you like this."
"Hmm?" Soren raised a brow, looked down, and saw his bare upper body. His eyes widened, and he scrambled for a shirt from his inventory, pulling it on as quickly as he could.

It’s... a little distracting talking to you like this."
"Hmm?" Soren raised a brow, looked down, and saw his bare upper body.
His eyes widened, and he scrambled for a shirt from his inventory, pulling it on as quickly as he could.

paragraphs: Fortunately, his trousers were still in one piece, or the situation would have turned into a complete disaster. With that in mind, he smoothed his clothes, straightened his collar, and cleared his throat, trying to regain his composure.
"My apologies, Vice Principal," he said, rubbing the back of his neck as the heat left his face. "I was a bit preoccupied."

"It’s fine. Breakthroughs are rarely graceful affairs. I’m just glad to see you made it through in one piece. Besides," she offered an apologetic smile, "it was my fault for dropping in unannounced. I shouldn’t have intruded on your post-breakthrough recovery like that."
Soren nodded, inwardly surprised that someone of her standing would apologize so easily. Still, he didn’t let the gesture distract him, because he could guess why she had appeared without warning.
’It is related to my mental breakthrough.’
He was sure of it.
"Then, what brings you here, Vice Principal?" Soren asked, fixing his gaze on her. "I assume... this isn’t just a casual visit to check on my health."

"It’s partly to check on your well-being, of course. And..." She paused, her eyes narrowing. "I am sure you already guessed it, but it’s about your mental cultivation. You manifested your will into reality, right?"
’...Right, Spiritual Manifestation is also called Will Manifestation,’
Soren thought, recalling the terminology.

He gave a slow nod, leaning into a look of mild surprise. "I did. But... how did you know? Could it be...?" He trailed off, leaving the question hanging as if he were only now putting the pieces together.

"Mmm, what you think is correct," She replied with a knowing smile. "I cultivate mentally too, and currently, I’m at the Inner Sanctum stage. That’s why I’m particularly sensitive to mental power and its fluctuations. I also know how powerful and dangerous it can be."

She paused as if choosing her words. "...Actually, I’ve been keeping an eye on this place since you entered seclusion, just in case something went wrong. So when I felt that sudden wave of mental energy, I thought you were in trouble and came running. And the rest, well, you already know."
"I see," Soren muttered, bowing politely again. "Thank you for your concern, Vice Principal."
"Mm.
"But," Soren continued, "if you’ve already reached the Inner Sanctum stage, then you’re truly extraordinary. Reaching such a level requires incredible talent and mastery."

Ramona smiled at his words, a soft chuckle escaping her lips. "You flatter me, Mr. Everly. Compared to what you’ve just accomplished at your age, I’m hardly anything exceptional. But I appreciate the compliment." She paused, then tilted her head slightly. "Speaking of which, would you like to talk about mental cultivation sometime? We could exchange insights and learn from each other."

Soren’s eyes lit up. Learning directly from an Inner Sanctum practitioner was a rare opportunity he wouldn’t dream of passing up. Besides, he was searching for a way to get close to her, so he nodded without hesitation. "I’d be honored, Vice Principal Ramona."
She nodded again. "Then it’s settled. Now, are you going to stay here, or should I take you out?"

"Ah, please-," Soren almost blurted out, "take me out," eager to leave and reunite with Ethea, but he caught himself and reconsidered before finishing his sentence. "...Let me stay for a while longer."
"Are you sure?" Ramona asked, raising a gentle eyebrow as she observed his sudden hesitation.
Soren gave a firm nod. "Yes. And... is it ok if I train here too?"
"Of course," She replied, producing a small white crystal and holding it out to him. "If you inject a trace of your mental power into this, I will know immediately and come pick you up."
Soren took the crystal and nodded. "Thank you, Vice Principal."
She smiled and disappeared.

Soren looked down at the delicate crystal in his palm before stowing it safely away. Actually, he wanted to familiarize himself with his new realm and strength and practice a few techniques before heading out. That’s why he chose to remain behind.
’Alright, let’s start.’

He took a deep breath and started with the basics. He tested his ice manipulation, then moved on to his spearmanship and swordsmanship. Hours slipped away unnoticed as he poured himself into every movement. By the time he finished, it was already around lunchtime in the real world.
He was more than satisfied with his progress, so he pulled out the crystal and injected a trace of his mental power into it.
Within moments, the air before him rippled, and Vice Principal Ramona reappeared.
"Ready to head back?"
Soren nodded, and the world around him blurred. When it came back into focus, they were standing in her office.
Soren steadied his footing and looked toward her. "When should we meet for our discussion on mental cultivation?"

Ramona crossed the room and rested a hand against the edge of her mahogany desk, pondering his question for a moment. "Let’s make it three days from now, in the morning. That should give you enough time to rest and consolidate your foundation. I will also finish my work and clear up my schedule so we won’t be interrupted."
"Understood," Soren replied. He reached into his inventory, retrieved a small glass bottle, and held it out to her. "This should be helpful for your mental cultivation. Please accept it."
Ramona stared at the vial curiously and accepted it. "Thank you, Mr. Everly. I will make good use of it."
"Then I will take my leave, Vice Principal," he said, bowing politely before straightening up.

"Go on and get some rest," Ramona replied, watching him turn and walk out of the office as the door closed softly behind him. Once he was gone, she sank back into her desk chair. She held the small bottle up to the light, watching the luminous liquid swirl inside.
’Lady Herald... he seems even more monstrous than you predicted. I didn’t even need to guide him...’
She let out a soft breath, a faint smile touching her lips as she carefully stowed the bottle in her drawer.
’...Perhaps it’s for the best.’
