chapters.title: Chapter 397: Welcome Back
paragraphs: "...Good." Zura licked her lips, clearly pleased with how the dish had turned out. She turned off the stove, served the food into bowls, carried them back to the living room, set one down for Ethea, and placed her own beside it. She sat down, picked up her utensils with an eager smile. "Let’s dig in now, shall we?"
"Zura," Ethea called out, "let’s wait a bit more."
Zura raised a brow in confusion. "Huh? Wait for what?"

"...My husband," Ethea answered, the joy in her voice impossible to miss. Her whole face brightened, the way a person’s does when something they have been waiting for is finally about to happen. "He’s coming back!"
"He is?" Zura asked dumbfounded.
"Mm!" Ethea nodded enthusiastically. "Can you bring another bowl for him?"
"..." Zura was stunned at first, but a faint smirk quickly tugged at her lips as she prepared to tease her. "You really..."

Yet, when she saw the look on Ethea’s face, the words died in her throat. Recalling how deeply Ethea had missed him throughout his long seclusion, Zura let her playful poke slide and shook her head with a fond chuckle.
"Alright, alright," Zura said, pushing her chair back and rising to her feet. "I’ll fetch another bowl."

"Thank you." Ethea smiled and turned her attention back to the door. Thanks to Eternal Bond, she could sense it when he moved away from where he had been for the past few days. And now, he was approaching rapidly in their direction.
’He must have succeeded,’ she thought, and her heart swelled with even more happiness. ’Hehe.’

Then, she began planning everything she would tell him the moment he stepped inside. First, she would greet him like a loving wife, ask if he was unharmed, and make sure everything had gone smoothly. Next, she would congratulate him properly on his breakthrough.
Most of all, she wanted to hold him close and tell him just how deeply she had missed him. But...
’Doing all that in front of Zura might be a bit too embarrassing...’
A gentle blush flushed across her cheeks at the thought. She peeked over her shoulder toward the kitchen, her fingers lightly fidgeting with the hem of her sleeve.
’No... She will understand it.’

Zura had always been perceptive and supportive, and she knew full well how much Ethea cherished every moment with Soren. Besides, feeling embarrassed over showing affection to her own husband made no sense at all.
Even if Zura teased her mercilessly later, she could easily endure it. As long as her reunion with the love of her life was sweet and sincere, nothing else mattered.

’Mm.’ Ethea nodded satisfiedly and continued to wait. Zura also returned from the kitchen carrying an extra set of tableware. She stepped over to the table and neatly arranged the bowl and utensils right beside Ethea’s right side.
"There," Zura said, straightening up with a smirk. "Satisfied now?"
"Very satisfied!" Ethea gave an eager nod.
"Good. Then let’s wait for your husband now.
They spent a few minutes exchanging small talk.
Knock... Knock...
Zura exchanged a quick glance with Ethea, and before Ethea could react, she grabbed the handles of her wheelchair, spun her around, and wheeled her straight toward the entryway.
Then, she gestured to her with her eyes, gave a thumbs-up meaning ’you can do it’, and quickly scampered back toward the dining space to leave them be.

Ethea’s lips twitched at the sudden exit, a light chuckle escaping her throat. Yet a deep wave of gratitude washed over her heart for her friend’s thoughtfulness. Drawing a soft breath, she turned her full attention toward the entryway and called out, "Come in."
The latch clicked open, and the door swung inward. A familiar face appeared in the doorway, and his eyes found hers immediately. It was none other than her dear husband, Soren.
"...I’m back, dear."
He said, his voice soft, as a tender smile crossed his lips.
"Mm..." A sweet smile bloomed across Ethea’s face, her eyes filled with endless affection. "Welcome back... darling."

They continued staring at each other before Soren stepped forward, closing the distance between them. He leaned down and wrapped his arms around her, pulling her close into a warm embrace. Ethea buried her face into his shoulder, her arms wrapping close around his neck as she whispered, "I really missed you, dear."
"...I missed you too," Soren replied softly, his breath brushing against her hair.
"...Are you ok?" Ethea asked a moment later. "Nothing bad happened, right?"
"Mm, don’t worry," Soren answered. "I succeeded too."
"Mm, I believed in you," Ethea whispered, pressing her face deeper into the crook of his neck. "But... I still wanted to hear it from you."
"And now you have. Are you satisfied, dear?" Soren asked with a laugh while gently rubbing her head.
"Extremely," Ethea replied, her voice muffled against his shoulder. A content sigh escaped her lips as she leaned into his solid warmth.
They stayed like that for a moment, hugging.

Then Soren leaned back just enough to frame her cheeks with his hands, his eyes lingering on hers for a brief second before he leaned in and pressed his lips to hers. The kiss started gently, but as their longing took over, it deepened into a tender, passionate embrace that made the rest of the world fade away.
When they finally parted, they rested their foreheads together, catching their breath. An amused giggle escaped Ethea’s lips, and Soren couldn’t help but chuckle along with her.
"Shall we go in?" Soren suggested.
"..." Ethea stared at him, then braced herself with her hands and leaned up to give him a quick peck on the lips. "...Mmm."

Soren took hold of the handles and wheeled her into the living room, where Zura stood waiting for them with a light flush dusting her cheeks. Soren realized with a sudden pang of amusement that he had completely forgotten to set up a sound barrier in the entryway. She had almost certainly heard their sweet exchanges and the sounds of their intimate acts.
However, since she seemed to be doing her best to pretend nothing out of the ordinary had happened, he decided to play along and act blissfully ignorant.
"Long time no see, Lady Zura," he greeted her with a polite bow.
"Welcome back, Mr. Soren." Zura smiled, though her cheeks were still a little pink. "And congratulations on your breakthrough."
"Thank you." Soren expressed his gratitude. "I’m also deeply grateful that you kept Ethea company for so long while I was away."
"Oh, please, it was nothing at all," Zura said, waving her hand dismissively with a quick smile. "Come on now, let’s eat lunch before the food gets cold."
"Right." Soren nodded with a chuckle, guiding Ethea’s wheelchair toward her spot at the dining table.
Zura pulled out her own chair and sat down, a proud grin returning to her face. "I cooked everything myself today! While it might not be as good as your cooking, please eat as much as you like."
"Then, I will gladly accept," Soren said, taking his seat. He picked up his utensils and took a thoughtful bite of the stew Zura had prepared.
Zura leaned forward slightly, watching him with anticipation. "Well? Be honest with your feedback! Don’t hold back just to be polite."
Soren swallowed the bite, pondering the flavor for a moment as he let the lingering taste settle on his palate.

"It is really delicious," Soren replied with a sincere nod. "Honestly, I think it’s not that different from a Fine Magic Meal. Though I think you went slightly light on the herbs toward the end of the simmer, which kept the mana circulation a bit mild. But purely in terms of home-cooked comfort, it is wonderful."
Zura let out a breath and beamed. "I’ll take that as a win, especially coming from you!"

"You flatter me," Soren chuckled, setting his bowl down for a second. "Furthermore, with your strong fire affinity and precise heat control, I think you have a natural talent for culinary. If you wanted, you could easily become a certified Magic Chef."

Zura’s eyes lit up for a brief second, bright with genuine surprise. Yet after a moment, she let out a quiet sigh and waved her hands in front of her face. "Ah, no, no. That sounds like way too much trouble! I am more than content with my current job at the academy. I think I will stick to cooking as a hobby for now."
She paused, took a bite, then flicked her eyes back to him with a sudden thought. "Speaking of which, I actually gave some ofthatfood you made earlier to one of my students, and she really liked it."

Soren didn’t answer immediately. Instead, he picked up his spoon, carefully scooped up a bite, and fed it to Ethea, gently wiping away a stray trace from her lower lip. Once she swallowed with a contented hum, he turned his attention back to Zura, raising an eyebrow.
"So it worked?"

chapters.title: Chapter 398: Sharing News
paragraphs: "It worked well." Zura nodded with a smile. "Her condition improved considerably just from eating three portions."
"I see," Soren muttered, thinking, ’Then I should cook for her again. And add some healing elixir to improve its healing effects.’
"...Do you want to meet her?" Ethea asked as she swallowed another scoop of stew. "I can arrange a meeting if you like. In fact... she actually mentioned wanting to meet you."

Zura chimed in, setting her spoon down as a playful smirk spread across her face. "You have no idea, Mr. Soren. Our Lea is a total cunning fox. She charmed my poor student completely and got her to start calling her ’Big Sister’ on their very first meeting! Now the two of them are practically as close as real sisters."
Ethea flushed slightly, giving Zura a look of mild protest, though a fond smile remained on her lips. "I didn’t force her or anything. She was just very sweet and easy to get along with."
"Is that so?" Soren chuckled softly at the exchange and offered Ethea another spoon of stew. "Then I suppose I will definitely have to meet this new little sister of yours soon."
"Mm." Ethea smiled brightly and added mentally. ’Let’s meet our sweet little sister together.’
’...Yes, our little sister,’ Soren chuckled and took a few spoons himself.
"By the way, did anything worth mentioning happen when I was in seclusion?" Soren inquired. Although eleven days wasn’t that long, anything could have happened in the outside world in that time.
"Nothing that directly affects us or is worth getting concerned about," Zura answered, taking a sip of water. "Though if you just want some interesting news, there are a few things going on."
Soren nodded, gesturing for her to continue.

"For starters, the freshman entrance exams will be starting soon," Zura explained, leaning back a little. "The entire campus is going to be incredibly busy and lively over the next few weeks with all the new applicants rushing in from all over the continent."
Soren nodded quietly in agreement. ’A new class of freshmen means a new batch of prodigies and geniuses. Perhaps I can find a few talented individuals worth investing in when the time comes.’
As the thought crossed his mind, a familiar face unexpectedly surfaced in his memories, prompting a quick smile. ’I should probably drop by and meet him again, too.’

"...I heard there are quite a few remarkable prodigies among this year’s batch. Several prominent noble houses and renowned Awakened have sent their youngest talents here. The competition is going to be far fiercer than usual. Besides, the summer vacation will end by the end of the entrance exam. So the upper-year students should start returning soon as well."
She took a few bites of her food, letting the news settle for a second before continuing. "Speaking of news... are you interested in Hunter-related matters as well?
Soren raised his eyes to meet hers and nodded. "Go on."

"First, it’s related to the Obsidian Abyss," Zura said, her expression turning solemn. "One of the strongest Guilds in Khorvath Continent, Black Moon, is assembling a massive expedition party to head into the depths. Publicly, their stated motive is to explore the deadly gate, recover the fallen explorers’ remains and belongings, and bring peace to the unsettled spirits trapped inside."

Soren raised a brow, his interest piqued instantly. Since Ryan had told him the Tower of Apocalypse might be the key to uncovering the truth behind everything, he had suspected other 9th Circle Gates might be related in some way, too. So any information about them was useful for him.

"However, rumors circulating through the upper circles suggest otherwise. Word is that they uncovered the location of a powerful artifact, said to guarantee a cultivator’s progression straight into the 9th Circle without bottlenecks or failure."

"...Allure of becoming a Paragon must be quite high," Soren said with a thoughtful hum. "Though seeking it inside the Obsidian Abyss is nothing short of reckless. I heard that gate is far more deadly than even the upper floors of the Tower of Apocalypse."
"I agree with you," Zura nodded grimly, resting her chin on her palm. "Navigating those abyssal depths is outright suicidal. But I think I know why they are doing it."
"Oh?"

"The Guild Master of the Black Moon is the one who needs that treasure. He has been stranded at the peak of the 8th Circle for over two decades now, and his bottleneck refuses to budge. To make matters worse, he also has a serious injury from an old battle, and his remaining lifespan shrinks noticeably with each passing year, leaving him with no other choice but to make one last desperate gamble."

"...Desperation makes even the wisest leaders act recklessly," Ethea remarked gently, her eyes reflecting a faint sadness for the man’s plight. "He is putting not only himself but numerous lives in danger as well. And even if he manages to reach the treasure, he might get backstabbed by his own ambitious subordinates, or find rival factions and evil forces lying in wait outside to butcher him and steal the treasure the moment he steps out. And... if it ends up falling into the hands of evil, it will bring nothing short of a catastrophe to the entire continent or even the whole world."
"Indeed." Zura narrowed her eyes. "The bloodbath waiting outside the gate will likely be far worse than the monsters inside."

"...I think the powerhouses in the region must know this too and will probably make their own preparations," Soren said calmly, setting his teacup down. "And that Guild Master isn’t probably a fool either; he undoubtedly foresees the ambush and has contingencies in place. Let’s hope nothing bad happens, and it resolves without spilling over to others, including us."
"Agreed." Zura nodded. "In fact, it’s better if they get scared and cancel it altogether or at least postpone it until they are better prepared."
"We should definitely keep an eye on the news about it, then," Ethea chimed in softly, her eyes turning toward Soren.
Soren made a mental note to monitor the developments surrounding the Black Moon Guild’s expedition before looking back at Zura. "And what about the other news you mentioned?

"This one is actually related in a way," Zura replied, leaning in slightly. "The Emperor himself made a rare public appearance and delivered a grand speech about eradicating the Outcasts and all evil organizations lurking in the shadows. He publicly rewarded several high-ranking individuals and groups who actively participated in the recent extermination, and at the end, he announced that the Empire will soon launch a widespread purge against any remaining evil factions within its borders."
"I see," Soren muttered, slightly surprised. "But... won’t making such a grand public announcement just alert those evil factions in advance?"

Zura nodded in agreement. "I thought so too. It seems foolish to announce a strike before carrying it out. Now, those groups will either go into hiding, flee to neighboring nations, or worse, get desperate and commit atrocities out of spite. But since it is the Emperor behind the decision, there must be more to it than meets the eye. Well, I hope so."
Soren nodded thoughtfully, resting his chin on his hand. "Perhaps there is a deeper strategy behind it... Like the public threat could be a ploy to force hidden factions into making a careless move."

"...You might be close to the mark, dear," Ethea said thoughtfully, a soft gleam of intelligence in her eyes. "The Empire took over a week to make this public announcement after the initial extermination of the Outcasts. That delay suggests they were actively using that time to seal off borders and lay traps across the border and key regions. By announcing it now, they leave the villains with nowhere to run except directly into those prepared nets."
She paused, taking a gentle sip of the tea Soren held for her before continuing.

"This must have been a direct warning to local lords and leaders to heighten their security and stay vigilant against desperate retaliation too. And beyond that, the Emperor undoubtedly wanted to boost the public’s morale and reassure the citizens that the Empire stands firm."
"..." Zura stared at Ethea for a moment, her eyes wide with admiration, before her face suddenly broke into a brilliant, cheeky grin. "Hehe, so smart~ As expected of my bookworm bestie!"
Without missing a beat, she leaned across her seat and threw her arms around Ethea, pulling her into a tight hug and affectionately rubbing her cheek against Ethea’s.
Soren couldn’t help but smile at the lively sight, taking another sip of his tea as the dining room filled with their familiar banter.

Ethea flushed softly under the sudden physical affection, though her lips curled up into a fond, teasing smile. "Perhaps you should have spent more time reading books instead of sleeping during classes back then, Zura."
Zura pulled back just enough to puff out her cheeks, replying without batting an eye, "Hey! I read books too! Just... not as much as you..."

chapters.title: Chapter 399: Plans
paragraphs: They shared a few more lighthearted laughs before continuing their conversation over the meal. Soren learned more about the shifting political tides, local rumors, and minor events in the outside world, gradually catching up on everything he had missed while in seclusion. Eventually, as the dishes were cleared, the long lunch came to a natural end. Zura stood up with a satisfied stretch, bidding them both farewell before taking her leave to attend to her duties, leaving Soren and Ethea alone in the villa.

After taking a relaxing bath and changing into comfortable clothes, the two shared some intimate quality time, enjoying the gentle affection and sweet closeness they had both missed when they were apart.

Mentally and physically relieved and content, Ethea gradually yielded to a sweet fatigue and fell asleep by evening, resting peacefully in his arms. Soren looked down at her serene face, his expression softening. He carefully shifted her onto the pillows, pulled the blanket over her shoulders, and planted a gentle kiss on her forehead before quietly slipping out of the bedroom.

He had sent a message to Ryan revealing his emergence and success. And now, as he looked at his phone, he saw a notification with a congratulatory message from him. While he was pleased to receive his little friend’s enthusiastic words, his attention quickly shifted down the screen.
His focus landed on the next unread message, sent from a contact simply named Panther.
[Congratulations on your successful breakthrough, boss. I knew you could do it...

...I’ve already secured most of the materials you requested, with just a few remaining things to settle on my end. You don’t need to worry about anything here because everything is under my control...
...Take care and see you soon.]
’...For a panther, he certainly knows how to stay in character.’

Being called ’boss’ still sounded a bit strange to his ears, making him feel like some sort of underworld gang leader. But since this was the exact disguise and cover identity they had agreed upon, he let the thought slide.

More importantly, a wave of relief washed over him as he read through the details. Everything on that end was progressing smoothly, and Malakor had already managed to track down and secure most of the ’materials’ they needed. With those groundwork preparations moving forward according to plan, Soren could direct his full attention to the upcoming matters involving his little sister and lovely wife.
’Of course, I can’t forget about the sponsorship plan too.’

He was currently sponsoring Ryan, and the other candidate was Darian, the lucky yet unlucky boy they met at Morning Dew during their date. Although he hadn’t awakened yet, he had been keeping an eye on him. He had 8th-circle potential and Supreme investment value, after all.
’I should meet with his family and discuss it with them soon.’

The freshman exam was going to start soon, and if Darian wanted to enter the academy, they had to hurry with his awakening. Soren could easily handle all the necessary resources and arrangements as long as he received the family’s agreement.
However, one troubling detail lingered in his mind: from what he’d learned, Darian had already failed his awakening during the official public ceremony.
Soren frowned slightly, puzzling over it. With a talent capable of reaching the 8th Circle, an ordinary awakening ritual should have been a breeze. Why had it failed back then?

Could it be for a reason similar to his own? Perhaps Darian possessed an authority of his own that required specific conditions to awaken. Or was there some hidden physical/mental ailment, a blockage in his mana pathways, or another underlying issue altogether?
’Ha... Whatever the reason, we can only hope he can awaken this time...’

With that in mind, Soren shifted his thoughts to his own progress. Now that he had achieved his breakthrough, his control over mana and delicate elemental nuances had improved immensely, meaning he could prepare even more effective magical meals than before too.

And after meeting his little sister, he decided to cook the last batch of ingredients he had set aside for her meal. Next, he would dive into studying new recipes and experimenting with complex culinary techniques, aiming to create something perfectly tailored to aid Ethea’s current condition and speed up her recovery.
’I shouldn’t forget training and Gate clearing with Ryan too.’
After all, it was the fastest way to increase his mana and battle experience.
’However, I should increase my hunter rank first.’

Although he could technically enter 4th Circle Gates with a C-rank license, attempting them with just a two-man team would be difficult since the Bureau banned it. The Bureau strictly mandated a minimum party of five C-rank Hunters for 4th-Circle Gates or at least one B-rank or higher, given the immense danger involved.

So, upgrading to a B-rank license would not only streamline access for him and Ryan, but it would also open up the flexibility to join higher-tier raid parties for 5th- or even 6th-Circle Gates whenever Ryan was unavailable.
’Ryan told me he would increase his rank to C rank too. I wonder if he already did it...’

With Ryan’s rapid growth and power rivaling higher circles, passing the promotion evaluation shouldn’t have been a problem for him. If both of them secured their rank upgrades, their options for Gate raiding would expand dramatically, giving them more freedom in choosing their next targets.

’Hmm... Should I invite him to our meeting with Nura too?’ He pondered the idea for a moment before deciding it was a good plan. Since Ryan intended to stay at the academy for at least the entire upcoming year, introducing him to Nura early on made sense. If the two formed a genuine bond, keeping an eye on her and ensuring her safety when they weren’t around would become much easier for both of them. ’...Alright, tomorrow, let’s take care of all of these. Meet with Darian’s parents, increase my rank, invite Ryan to the meeting, and prepare to meet Nura.’

chapters.title: Chapter 400: Master Soren!
paragraphs: "Good morning, Brother Soren!"
"Good morning, Ryan."
Soren waved through the car window and gestured for him to get in.

Ryan opened the door and climbed into the passenger seat, but as he settled in, he noticed another presence in the back. He looked over his shoulder and saw a red-haired boy who looked a year or two younger than him, with slightly chubby cheeks and bright, curious eyes.
Before he could even speak, the boy offered him a wide smile and greeted him enthusiastically. "Good morning! You must be Senior Ryan Master talked about! It’s a pleasure to meet you!"

’Master? Is he talking about Brother Soren?’ Ryan thought, momentarily caught off guard by the title. Recovering quickly, he gave a polite nod and smiled back. "Good morning. Yes, I’m Ryan. And who might you be?"

The boy’s eyes widened in realization, and he hurriedly bowed his head, looking a bit flustered. "Ah, forgive me! I forgot to introduce myself! My name is Darian, Darian Dervish! I’m Master Soren’s disciple!"
’I really guessed right?’ Ryan raised a brow in surprise and immediately turned his gaze toward the driver’s seat.
Soren offered a wry smile, catching Ryan’s baffled expression in the rearview mirror. "I’ll explain everything on the way," he said while smoothly pulling the car into traffic.

After a moment of silence, Soren glanced at Ryan and broke the quiet. "...Darian is the boy I talked to you about before, the one I wanted to sponsor. Before coming to pick you up, I went to his house with him to talk with his parents and got their consent."

He kept his eyes on the road as he continued. "Fortunately, his family was supportive of the idea, especially given the benefits of being an Awakened and the opportunities he could get at the academy. Since he’ll be training under my direction, he decided to call me ’Master,’ even though I told him a simple ’Brother’ or ’Mister’ would suffice."

In the back seat, Darian puffed his chest out slightly, grinning with pride. "Master Soren paid for another awakening test and promised to help me get into Etenia Academy! He even said he would help with tuition once I pass! He’s helping me achieve my lifelong dream. How could I not call him Master? And he’s a 5th Circle Awakened too!

"I see..." Ryan listened carefully, the pieces clicking into place. He looked back at Darian and nodded with genuine appreciation. "It’s a huge opportunity to learn from Brother Soren, Darian. Work hard, and make sure you listen to everything he teaches you."
"I will!" Darian replied eagerly, leaning back against his seat with eyes sparkling at the prospect of the journey ahead.

"You should be taking notes from Ryan, too," Soren said with a slight smirk through the rearview mirror. "He is a 4th-Circle Awakened and exceptionally talented. Plus, he’s a swordsman, just like you want to be. So you can ask him for guidance whenever you get stuck with your swordsmanship in the future."
Darian’s eyes lit up instantly. "Really?!"
Ryan rubbed the back of his neck, offering a modest wave of his hand. "I only broke through to the 4th Circle not long ago. I’m really not that amazing."
"He’s still sixteen," Soren added seamlessly.
Darian’s gaze brightened even more, practically burning with starry-eyed reverence.
Slightly embarrassed by the boy’s intense awe, Ryan shifted in his seat and cleared his throat to change the subject. "Have you not taken the awakening test before?"
As soon as the words left his mouth, a sudden silence fell over the car.
Darian’s excited expression deflated, his shoulder dropping as his eyes cast downward. Ryan froze, immediately realizing he might have touched upon a sensitive subject.

"Actually..." Just as Soren was about to step in and break the heavy silence, Darian raised his head. The momentary shadow on his face had completely vanished, replaced by a spark of pure determination.
"I failed to awaken at the official ceremony," Darian explained, his voice steadying before firing up again. "But I didn’t give up, and I never will!"
He leaned forward slightly, his eyes surprisingly calm despite his usual scattered energy.

"Grandma always says that flowers don’t all bloom in the same month, and fruit doesn’t ripen on the same day. Everything in this world has its own right time. I think... my time just hadn’t arrived yet, but it’s definitely near. This time, I probably will—no, I must awaken!"
Ryan blinked, caught off guard by the unexpected depth in the young boy’s words. The sheer conviction in Darian’s tone hung in the air, carrying an uncanny weight that seemed far beyond his years.

Soren caught Ryan’s eye in the mirror and offered a subtle nod. Thanks to Eyes of Truth, Soren knew that Darian might be a bit scatterbrained most of the time, but every so often, he dropped truths that held a strange, almost prophetic weight. Perhaps this was one of those moments.

"That’s the spirit," he said softly, a subtle smile touching his lips as he steered the car toward the Bureau. "Hold onto that belief. Keep pushing forward, and don’t stop no matter what anyone says."

Ryan turned in his seat, the remaining awkwardness melting away into an encouraging smile. "That’s right, as long as you don’t give up, anything is possible. And... once you awaken, I’ll help you practice your swordsmanship."

Darian’s smile widened until it practically reached his ears, his eyes shining with newfound determination. "Thank you so much, Master! Thank you, Senior Ryan! I promise I won’t let either of you down!"

Soren and Ryan shared an amused smile at the boy’s boundless enthusiasm. Soren kept his eyes on the road, though his thoughts drifted for a moment as he wondered how to handle the situation if Darian failed to awaken again.
’No... Let’s not think about failure for now. Today is about giving him a chance. Let’s believe in him.’

They continued with small talk as the car moved through the city streets, with Darian mostly asking questions while Ryan and Soren answered. Eventually, they arrived at their destination: the Ademary Awakened Bureau.

He looked over his shoulder and saw a red-haired boy who looked a year or two younger than him, with slightly chubby cheeks and bright, curious eyes.
Before he could even speak, the boy offered him a wide smile and greeted him enthusiastically.
"Good morning!
You must be Senior Ryan Master talked about!
It’s a pleasure to meet you!"
’Master?
Is he talking about Brother Soren?’ Ryan thought, momentarily caught off guard by the title.
Recovering quickly, he gave a polite nod and smiled back.
"Good morning.
Yes, I’m Ryan.
And who might you be?"
The boy’s eyes widened in realization, and he hurriedly bowed his head, looking a bit flustered.
"Ah, forgive me!
I forgot to introduce myself!
My name is Darian, Darian Dervish!
I’m Master Soren’s disciple!"
’I really guessed right?’ Ryan raised a brow in surprise and immediately turned his gaze toward the driver’s seat.
Soren offered a wry smile, catching Ryan’s baffled expression in the rearview mirror.
"I’ll explain everything on the way," he said while smoothly pulling the car into traffic.
After a moment of silence, Soren glanced at Ryan and broke the quiet.
"...Darian is the boy I talked to you about before, the one I wanted to sponsor.
Before coming to pick you up, I went to his house with him to talk with his parents and got their consent."
He kept his eyes on the road as he continued.
"Fortunately, his family was supportive of the idea, especially given the benefits of being an Awakened and the opportunities he could get at the academy.
Since he’ll be training under my direction, he decided to call me ’Master,’ even though I told him a simple ’Brother’ or ’Mister’ would suffice."
In the back seat, Darian puffed his chest out slightly, grinning with pride.
"Master Soren paid for another awakening test and promised to help me get into Etenia Academy!
He even said he would help with tuition once I pass!
He’s helping me achieve my lifelong dream.
How could I not call him Master?
And he’s a 5th Circle Awakened too!
"I see..." Ryan listened carefully, the pieces clicking into place.
He looked back at Darian and nodded with genuine appreciation.
"It’s a huge opportunity to learn from Brother Soren, Darian.
Work hard, and make sure you listen to everything he teaches you."
"I will!" Darian replied eagerly, leaning back against his seat with eyes sparkling at the prospect of the journey ahead.
"You should be taking notes from Ryan, too," Soren said with a slight smirk through the rearview mirror.
"He is a 4th-Circle Awakened and exceptionally talented.
Plus, he’s a swordsman, just like you want to be.
So you can ask him for guidance whenever you get stuck with your swordsmanship in the future."
Darian’s eyes lit up instantly.
"Really?!"
Ryan rubbed the back of his neck, offering a modest wave of his hand.
"I only broke through to the 4th Circle not long ago.
I’m really not that amazing."
"He’s still sixteen," Soren added seamlessly.
Darian’s gaze brightened even more, practically burning with starry-eyed reverence.
Slightly embarrassed by the boy’s intense awe, Ryan shifted in his seat and cleared his throat to change the subject.
"Have you not taken the awakening test before?"
As soon as the words left his mouth, a sudden silence fell over the car.
Darian’s excited expression deflated, his shoulder dropping as his eyes cast downward.
Ryan froze, immediately realizing he might have touched upon a sensitive subject.
"Actually..." Just as Soren was about to step in and break the heavy silence, Darian raised his head.
The momentary shadow on his face had completely vanished, replaced by a spark of pure determination.
"I failed to awaken at the official ceremony," Darian explained, his voice steadying before firing up again.
"But I didn’t give up, and I never will!"
He leaned forward slightly, his eyes surprisingly calm despite his usual scattered energy.
"Grandma always says that flowers don’t all bloom in the same month, and fruit doesn’t ripen on the same day.
Everything in this world has its own right time.
I think... my time just hadn’t arrived yet, but it’s definitely near.
This time, I probably will—no, I must awaken!"
Ryan blinked, caught off guard by the unexpected depth in the young boy’s words.
The sheer conviction in Darian’s tone hung in the air, carrying an uncanny weight that seemed far beyond his years.
Soren caught Ryan’s eye in the mirror and offered a subtle nod.
Thanks to Eyes of Truth, Soren knew that Darian might be a bit scatterbrained most of the time, but every so often, he dropped truths that held a strange, almost prophetic weight.
Perhaps this was one of those moments.
"That’s the spirit," he said softly, a subtle smile touching his lips as he steered the car toward the Bureau.
"Hold onto that belief.
Keep pushing forward, and don’t stop no matter what anyone says."
Ryan turned in his seat, the remaining awkwardness melting away into an encouraging smile.
"That’s right, as long as you don’t give up, anything is possible.
And... once you awaken, I’ll help you practice your swordsmanship."
Darian’s smile widened until it practically reached his ears, his eyes shining with newfound determination.
"Thank you so much, Master!
Thank you, Senior Ryan!
I promise I won’t let either of you down!"
Soren and Ryan shared an amused smile at the boy’s boundless enthusiasm.
Soren kept his eyes on the road, though his thoughts drifted for a moment as he wondered how to handle the situation if Darian failed to awaken again.
Let’s not think about failure for now.
Today is about giving him a chance.
Let’s believe in him.’
They continued with small talk as the car moved through the city streets, with Darian mostly asking questions while Ryan and Soren answered.
Eventually, they arrived at their destination: the Ademary Awakened Bureau.
